sections.heading: Dominance Kills and Gets Killed
paras: Arabs call a disobedient horse as Satan and not the one grazing in the meadow, as the latter is engaged to meet its physical needs. The former is well fed and strong and therefore, disobedient. Devilishness means arrogance and disobedience in the dictionary, deserving curses and condemnation for it. A hundred persons sit around a dining sheet to eat, but two claimants of domination cannot occupy the world. No such claimant likes to see another one on the face of the earth. With a fear of any claim or participation, a king kills his own father. Kingship is called sterile and will not have an offspring. Like fire it has no relationship with anybody. Whatever it sees or meets is torne down and burnt to ashes by it. When it does not find anything to burn, it swallows itself and gets lost. Therefore, become worthless and protect yourself from its teeth and do not seek any mercy from it as it is like a soft bed kept to absorb the shocks of the hammers on gold or silver to flatten. How can one constantly receiving beatings protect you from beatings? However, when you get rid of the desire of domination and become humble, you need not fear beatings. It is only the hard things that are beaten and not the soft ones.

Godliness is the mantle of that Authority with Grandeur and it becomes troublesome to anyone who tries to wear it. Crown is His property and ours is only a waistband of humility. One who attempts to go beyond his limits faces destruction. Your pride upon your possession of greatness is like the feathers of the peacock. It is a trial for you as though, you search this for domination and godhood, uniqueness and holiness.

chapters.title: Peacock Plucking Its Own Feathers
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a wiseman who saw a peacock picking out its feathers with its beak making its body bald and ugly. In surprise, he asked it whether it does not feel sorry for it. It said: “I do feel, but my life is dearer to me than my Feathers, as they are enemies of my life. That is why I am plucking them out

sections.heading: Beauty and Coquettishness
paras: A wise man while strolling in a forest came across a peacock which was plucking its own feathers. He said: “O peacock! Why do you pluck such precious feathers from their roots one after another? How does your heart permit you to pluck such precious apparel and throw it in slush? With great value, regard and affection, reciters of the Quran, keep your feathers in its folds. In order to move beneficent air, fans are made out of your feathers. What kind of thanklessness and carelessness is this that you do not know as to who is the artist and painter of your feathers? Or is it that you are deliberately showing coquettishness to keep these paintings and beauties away from you? Many a times may coquettish behaviours are considered wrong rendering the servants into lower levels in the king’s view. Dallying appears nice if done in a sweet manner, but too much of it becomes crushing, putting one into great difficulties. Path of humbleness is a place of comfort and satisfaction. Therefore, stop dallying, and develop intimacy with this comfortable place. Many a times exhibition of stylish behaviours have resulted in further styles, ultimately resulting in troubles and difficulties.

The path of submission is full of peace; therefore, give up the path of making an exhibition of yourself. Many people have exhibited their feathers and hairs of beauty which became the cause of their calamity. The beauty of your styles raises you up instantly, but your hidden fear of these very things melts you down.

sections.heading: While Stylishness Puts You in All These Fears and Risks, Submission and Humility Make You Very Frail, but It Makes Your Breast Bright Like the Moon. as God Creates the Living Out of the Dead, Everyone Who Behaves Like Dead Receives Great Godly Guidance of Life
paras: Reciprocally, God also makes a living one, dead. The soul of the living goes towards death and receives a different kind of lasting life. In the former case life had to end in death, but in the latter case, where life has come after death, it has no death. It is lasting. Therefore, make yourself as dead, so that, God the Eternal, Absolute, and Causer of life, may bring out the living one out of the dead. Become one like autumn, so that you may see the spring; become a night so that you may see the entrance of night into day.

sections.heading: Do Not Spoil Beauty
paras: Do not pluck your feathers as it is not possible to darn the wound caused by it. Whatever may be the intensity of your mourning, do not peel your beautiful face. It is wrong to peel the face that is bright like the morning sun. it is a high act of rejection of gift to cause injuries upon your face with your fingernails.

A beautiful face and fingernails are not given by God for this purpose. You do not appear to look at your own face to know its worth and the processes followed one after another to evolve it to this beautiful level; and out of this ignorance, you are not valuing it and engaging yourself in unwanted disputations.

chapters.title: Useless Thoughts Spoil Mind
chapters.subtitle: To Explain: The cleanliness and simplicity of the contented self gets disturbed with unwanted worries just as a writing by you on a mirror leaves its marks even after your washing and wiping it off

sections.heading: Inconclusive Thoughts Lead Nowhere
paras: Face of the contented self in the body gets injured with unwanted worries. Consider the vicious thoughts of yours as poisonful fingernails which seriously injure the face of the soul. They cause various knots and pollutions in the clean pleasures of the soul. Your efforts to reach the ultimate of everything will not be met with success, as these knots are made on an empty bag. You open one knot and yet there is one to be opened and again there are knots one after another, putting you in an endless job. You become old in your efforts to open some of them, but you cannot open all. What will you achieve by opening some of them? There are many left to be opened.

The knots that are put around your neck are very hard to open. You do not know as to what those knots are. You do not know whether this job leads you to fortune or misfortune. It will be very good for you, if you just know only this much, as it would settle the matter, whether it is good or bad, or useful or useless. The tension of your mind will go enabling you to think of other matters depending on this understanding. Therefore, try to solve this difficulty. Spend all your abilities and put all your efforts that can be put by a man to solve this problem of unnecessary confusing thoughts.

sections.heading: Limits of Logical Knowledge
paras: Know the limits of knowledge of substances and accidents. (Bases and the constructions upon them). Suppose that you know about all the substances and the accidents, then you may consider the limitations of your mind. You will come to know that all these are impossibles and impossible approaches. Upon knowing this you will know of your own worth or worthlessness and limitations. You may pass on from them, you may proceed toward that Entity whose reality of is unknown. The whole life is lost in syllogistic deductions of minor and major premiss and the conclusions thereof, and in assessments heard from others without observing any realities. Every argument is without any impact and satisfaction. It is only verbal. Think over! You have seen only the creatures but not the Creator. Every thought rests on speculations, such as, the world is not created but eternal, or has come into existence, on its own, without a creator. Philosophers believe in improving conclusions on the basis of earlier conclusions, but the elect (saint), on the contrary, believe in actual observation. The elect avoids arguments and hides his head within his lapel and avoids argumentative conclusions to observe the object by direct spiritual observation.

sections.heading: Causer and Causes
paras: The philosopher looks at the effect to know the cause. Looking at smoke he concludes its cause to be fire. But in our case, we do not lookout at smoke or fire but look at the causer of the fire. In particular, the fire which is a product of the nearness to God and devotion to Him, which strikes our sight without its connections with smoke. Love does not care about the intermediate observations. It is indecent to go away from the dishes on the dining sheet toward the thoughts of smoke and fire in the stove.

chapters.title: No Reclusion in Islam
chapters.subtitle: To explain the statement of the Prophet: There is no monasticism (reclusion) in Islam

sections.heading: Patience with Ability to Go Against
paras: O peacock! Do not pluck your feathers to root out the cause of pride. But keep your heart and inclination away from them and let them be there in their place. This Jihaad (struggle or effort) to keep yourself from ostentation and self-pride requires an enemy, the cause of ostentation, which in your case, are your feathers. There is no scope for struggle and fight when there is no enemy. When there are no carnal desires, there is no scope for self-control and patience. There is no need for an army, when you do not have an enemy. Do not castrate yourself and become a recluse, as your celibacy is connected with your sexual passions. Without there being carnal desires there is no scope of preventing yourself from them. There is no scope for fighting against the enemy that is dead; and victory cannot be exhibited upon the dead bodies.

sections.heading: Opposites Considerable to Understand Meanings
paras: When God has ordered you to expend (Anfiquu), it means that you should first earn and then expend as it is not possible to expend without earning. Though He has simply said expend (Anfiquu), but you have to read it as: earn and then expend. Similarly, it has been said: Isbiruu (have patience, perseverance, constancy, self-restraint, refusing to be cowed down — as elucidated by Abdullah Yusuf Ali). This comes about when there is need or temptation toward their opposites. You should not turn away from Isbiruu, as there will be opposition to Isbiruu for various reasons. The command “eat” (Kuluu) is for the purpose of developing strength of passions and after this the command “do not be extravagant” (wa laa tusrifuu) is for the purpose of maintaining decency and restraint from unlawful passions. There is no scope for walaa tusrifu when there is no eating (kuluu).
When there is no minor premiss in syllogism, there is no scope for major premiss. Where there are no propositions, there are no conclusions.

When you do not undergo the pain of patience to reject certain demands, which are pre-conditions for patience, you do not get any reward at all. How great is the pre-condition of patience for the great reward for patience! Both go together.

chapters.title: God, a Reward for His Lover
chapters.subtitle: To explain that God Himself is the reward from God for the lover of God

sections.heading: Meaning of La Ilaaha Illaallah
paras: God alone is the joy and sorrow of His lovers. He alone is the hand of labour and the payment of labour. If one looks at others other than Him, one is not in love, but senseless and mad. Love is such a ball of fire, which, when brightens, it sets fire to everything other than the beloved. One who moves the sword of “laa” (No) in the article of faith, La ilaaha illaallah cuts off everything other than God. You may think over on this point. Think over as to what remains when every material and non-material thing is eliminated? This Laa is followed by illaa Allah (except God), which means everything has vanished and only God remains. Thus, love is that mighty power which destroys and removes everything, leaving Allah alone for itself to be in love with. How great and grand is love! God is both the First (Awwal) and Last (Aakhir). The lover sees only Him as First and as Last, without there being anything other Him in between. Therefore, you may not see other things along with God just as a squint-eyed fellows see two things of one.

sections.heading: This Is a Strange Fact. No Beauty Anywhere Is Other Than the Reflection of God, Just as There Is No Movement of Any Part of the Body Without the Soul. That Body, Which Has a Defective Soul, That Is, with Inherent Bad Character, Cannot Be Put on the Right Side, How Many Ever Efforts May Be Put. Its Bitterness Will Not Go, Even If You Put It in Honey. This Thing Can Be Understood Only by Him Who Lives with God for a Day and Receives a Cup from His Hand. That Is; One Who Has Had a Spiritual Life Even for a Short Time, Whose Human Soul Is Alive. One Who Has Not Seen the Bright Face of God, Finds His Life as Something Burning in Smoke
paras: One who has not seen the nobility of H ‘Umar b. Abdul ‘Azeez and his justice will consider the unjust cruel, Yazeed as just and noble. When he has not seen the dominance of H. Musa’a python, he will consider the ropes of the magicians appearing as snakes as real and living. The bird that has not tasted sweet fresh water will enjoy saltish water and keep its wings and feathers washed well by it. So also, a man who has not seen the real spiritual life will consider the material life itself as real and everything.

sections.heading: This World, a Model of the Other World
paras: It is not possible to understand anything without comparing with its opposite. One, who does not see cruelties, cannot appreciate the days of peace and happiness. For the worldly man, this material world comes first so that through it, he may find out the greatness, that he had well before the creation of matter, on the occasion of Alast (the meaning of Alast has already been explained earlier). When you get separated from material world, including your material body, and go to the other spiritual world with only your soul, you will enjoy its everlasting sweetness as though you are in a sugar factory. There, you will say: I have simply roamed about in dust earlier in that world; and it is strange that, out of my ignorance, I was running away from this clean and pure world. I was going after the snake instead of the treasure and getting pleased with thorns instead of the garden. How good it would have been, had I died earlier, and my food had not been the slush of that world.

chapters.title: Death Is Pleasing to Man After Death
chapters.subtitle: To explain the meaning of hadith: Everyone after death will crave: it would have been good, had he died earlier; a good one for the reason that he would have reached the good earlier; and the bad one on the ground that he could have got his bad acts reduced

paras: It is for this reason that, that well-informed Prophet has said: “The one who died got separated from the body will not regret upon his death and departure but will regret over his misdeeds and deficiencies. Everyone after death feels: How good it would have been for him, if had died earlier, and his transfer toward his object had been earlier. A bad person would feel that had he died earlier the number of his bad deeds would have been fewer; and a good person would feel that he would have reached his destination earlier. The bad fellow would say: I was not informed and every moment I went on increasing my curtains. If my reaching to my destination had been early there would have been few curtains and obstacles to my end.”

sections.heading: Continuation of the Wise Man’s Address to Peacock
paras: The wiseman continued to tell the peacock: “Do not injure your contented face by scratching, out of your greed and pride. So also, do not injure a generous face with your miserliness, and the beautiful prostrating face with devilishness. Do not pluck the feathers that decorate the paradise and help you to go on your way.”

sections.heading: Sorrows of the Peacock
paras: When the peacock heard this advice, it looked at the face of the adviser and then started lamenting and crying which were so long, painful and full of grief that all those who were nearby also cried. The wiseman who had asked for its plucking of feathers felt ashamed and started crying without hearing for the answer to his question telling himself as to why he put that silly question. It already had some reason for its act, and I incited it to cry over it. Tears were falling down from the wet eyes and every drop had hundreds of answers in it. Tears were falling down from his eyes and with these frightening tears, the mud was getting converted into slush.

True crying causes impacts upon the souls; so much that even the heavens and empyrean start crying. Pretended and untrue crying does not create any impact, and the mean devil laughs upon it. It does not have any heat in it. It is like butter milk which has no butter. Wisdom and heart certainly have a connection with empyrean and live upon the imperial light.

chapters.title: Hidden and Subservient Desires
chapters.subtitle: To explain that wisdom and soul are imprisoned in the body of water and mud just as Haaruut and Maaruut are in the well in Babylon

paras: Wisdom and soul are imprisoned in man, who is like the frightening well in which Haaruut and Maaruut are kept imprisoned. They belonged to the upper spiritual world, but because of their indulgence in the lowly sexual crimes that they committed, they are kept imprisoned in the well at Babylon. So also, wisdom and soul belong to the upper spiritual world, but are kept imprisoned in the body of man. Both good and bad people learn magic and its counter without actual willingness from them just as some people learnt from Haaruut and Maaruut.

sections.heading: Wisdom and Soul Teach Magic to Men
paras: Men under the compulsions of their desires, without proper application of mind try to learn magic from wisdom and soul, but they warn them in advance not to learn it, not to acquire it; as it teaches them to put them to trial to see whether they use this knowledge for good or bad purpose. Your capacity to use it depends upon your control on it and there cannot be any control without power to do so. Desires are like sleeping dogs, which have both good and bad qualities in them. When they have no power, they will be in sleep like pieces of wood which lie silently. So also, a man is good so long he has no power to be bad. In such circumstances, he feels that he cannot commit wrongs. When dog is in sleep, it is powerless, but when some dead body comes in its way, and the bugle of greed plays, it gets up. When a donkey dies in their streets, hundreds of dogs get up from their sleep. Greeds that have hidden themselves behind invisible curtains raise their heads and pounce upon the dogs. Every hair of the dogs becomes a tooth and it starts wagging its tail for doing some act. Half of its body is full of tricks and the other half with wrath, just as cooling fire gets fuel. Then arrive flames from the other world and rouse it and flames upon flames arise from the cooling fire, and smoke and flames start going high up toward the sky.

sections.heading: Controlled and Uncontrolled Desires
paras: Such kinds of hundreds of dogs are sleeping in your body, and as there is no prey to catch, they are in sleep. Or like the falcon whose eyes are blindfolded, which is burning with the fire of hidden love to pounce upon other birds. And when the blindfolding cap is removed from its head, it starts flying around the hills in search of prey.

So also, the desires of a sick man are in peace and his mind is busy in thinking of the ways of health. When he sees food — apples and melons, there arises a battle between eating and the fear of diet control in his heart. Looking at these things is good for one who has patience, as desire for eating is good for a tired and sick person. And it is better not to look at, for a person, who does not have the power of self-control. A man without a coat of mail should be away from shooting arrows.

Byepass from these matters and complete the story of the peacock as to what it said in answer to the question put by the wiseman. Now, you may hear the answer of the peacock so that you may become aware of every statement that leads toward good.

chapters.title: Peacock’s Answer to the Wise Questioner

paras: When the peacock was exhausted of its crying, it said to the wiseman: “You are a slave of colour and fragrance. You do not see that from all my sides, there are hundreds of calamities for me for the sake of the feathers. There are many merciless hunters, who spread nets for me for the sake of these feathers. Many archers shoot their arrows in the air toward me for the sake of my feathers. When I do not have the strength and means of protection from these deadly fate, calamities and trials, it is preferable that I become ugly and hateable so that I remain safe in the hills and forests. I pluck my feathers one by one so that some accursed fellow may not catch me in his net. In my view, life is better than feathers and hairs. Life is permanent and body is defective. These feathers are the weapons of my self-esteem; and self-esteem puts its lovers in hundreds of difficulties.”

chapters.title: Great Qualities Have Risks
chapters.subtitle: To explain that craftmanship, intelligence and wealth are enemies of life like the feathers of peacock

sections.heading: Great Qualities Need Protection
paras: The peacock continued: “Craftmanship of an incompetent fellow puts him in difficulties, as being incompetent, he would look only at the grain spread out, but not at the net. Authority to act is good and suitable for one who is cautious and disciplined. When you do not have capacity to protect yourself and be cautious, it is better for you to throw away the tools of craftmanship and authority to act. My self-exposure and my authority to exhibit it are my feathers; and as I have no power to protect them and protect myself, I am plucking them out as they will take me to the severing of my head. One possessing patience upon on self considers one’s decorations as worthless to such an extent that they do not put one in anxieties and mischiefs. For such a person it is alright to say not to pluck out his decorative feathers. He will have the capacity to present a shield to defend himself from the shot-out arrow.

sections.heading: Weapons Need Wisdom, Discipline for Use
paras: But, for me, my beautiful feathers are my enemies, as I do not have control upon the exhibition of my beauty. If patience and means of protection were my guides, they would have increased my grandeur and beauty. I am like a humble child or an unconscious fellow in my fight against and troubles, and therefore, it is not proper for me to hold a sword in my hand. I have no capacity to use it in fight. If I had the wisdom, discipline and training to have control on the sword, a sword in my hand could have been victorious. Wisdom should be such as to give light of guidance as the sun does, to wave the sword in the proper way.

sections.heading: Do Not Keep Weapons Without Capacity to Use
paras: Why should I not throw away my weapons in the well, when I do not have a bright wisdom and good advice. I am throwing my sword and shield in the well, so that these may not be snatched from me by my enemy who would use them against me. My enemy will certainly use my weapons against me when I do not have the strength, support and help to protect my weapons. I am scratching my face to disgrace my degraded and polluted self, which never hides its face but always engages in boasting of its greatness and achievements. I do this so that my beauty and perfectness are reduced; because when beauty and perfectness are no more, I shall fall into very few troubles. It is not a sin to scratch myself and make myself ugly, if I do with such intention. This scratching becomes a protective shield. It is a good defensive measure.

That apart, this would not have been necessary for me to do, if my heart had not been greedy of self-exposure with pride having a habit of hiding itself. My beautiful face would have shown only clean, clear good feelings. When I did not find strength, wisdom and good qualities within myself, I looked at the enemy, and immediately destroyed my weapons, so that my sword may not become a cause of his perfection and my own dagger may not be troublesome to myself. So long as my nerves are well, I shall be on the run. It is quite possible to run away from the enemy but how can anybody run from himself. The man running from another finds peace of mind from the enemy, when he goes faraway beyond his reach, but I am an enemy of myself and therefore my running away from myself is permanent. Every moment I have to be on the run. My self has no peace in India nor in Khuthan, the centre of the musk trade. One has no peace at all when one’s own shadow is one’s enemy.

chapters.title: People Annihilated in God
chapters.subtitle: To explain the character of those who get lost in God with all their good and bad qualities, like the stars which get lost in the light of the sun in daytime. One who gets lost has no fear of any kind of trouble

sections.heading: Candle Has Shadow, but Not Its Flame
paras: When a man ignores all his good and bad qualities and gives up his abilities and deprives himself of the sense of all these like a destitute and gets lost in God, losing all these material burdens, he becomes shadowless like Prophet Muhammed. As the Prophet annihilated himself in God, he became shadowless like the flame of the candle. And he said: “I am proud of my poverty”. That was self-imposed destitution or annihilation in God. The candle has a flame on its head which has no shadow, but its body has a shadow. But when it becomes a flame from top to bottom, there is no shadow of anything: head or body on any side. Its wax goes away from its existence and there is no scope for shadow at all. Both wax and its shadow, get lost in the flame. The candle was made for making a flame, but it ceased to exist by becoming a part of the flame.

sections.heading: Getting Lost in God
paras: The candle maker told the candle: “I made you to get lost (which is by giving light)”. The candle also said: “I have met your object and I got lost”. This is the way of the candle’s coming into existence and getting lost. But one who gets lost in God is different. He does not cease to exist. He exists in God. His light is not mortal, nor it is lost. When the candle is totally lost in fire it is totally annihilated. You will neither see the candle nor the light. But it is different in the case of man, because the more he gets reduced in his physical quantity, greater in the light of his soul. The soul’s light is a lasting light, while the light of the candle is vanishing light because the flame of the soul’s light is not from wax but from God.

sections.heading: So Long as the Light Is Emanating from Fire, It Is in Existence. It Has No Shadow. Shadow That Causes Obstacle Does Not Exist for It. It Is Unlike the Shadow of the Cloud That Falls upon Earth, When It Is in Front of Moon. Left to Itself, Moon Has No Shadow of Its Own. the Difference Here Is Due to the Fact That the Cloud Is Dense and Thick, Whereas the Moonlight Is Absolute, Pure, Clean and Clear. Loss of Your Identity and Shedding of Your Denseness Is Like Losing the Cloud of the Body, When You Become Clean and Clear Like the Moon. but When a Passing Cloud Comes About upon You, the Clean Light of the Moon Passes Away, and What Remains Is Only a Thought or Memory of the Light. the Light Becomes Dim Due to the Overlapping of the Cloud and the Full Bright Moon Becomes Thin Crescent Like the New Moon (so Also in Partial Lunar Eclipse). Because of the Cloud and Dust, Moon Lost Its Clearness and Became Like an Image. so Also, the Cloud of Our Body Hid Realities from Us and Made Us Imaginers
Human Body Obstructs God’s Light
paras: Consider God as a giver of light to us like to the moon and see that He has called the cloud as our enemy which comes in the way of the light from the moon. However, moon is free from the impacts of dust and clouds. Its orbit of movement is high up in the sky. Cloud is an enemy of our sight as it hides the moon from us. So also, our body is like the cloud which acts as an obstacle between our soul and God. It builds a curtain, in which a young houri appears like an old woman and makes the brightful moon dimmer than the new moon. God made us sit in a place of honour by His side and said that our enemy is His enemy. By calling our enemy as His enemy, He has elevated our status. The little light that the cloud has, is from the moon. Anyone calling the cloud as moon is misguided. The fact is, when the light of the moon, fell on the cloud, its dark face became bright. Though to look at cloud may appear as rich and bright with its own light, but the light of the moon upon it is temporary. At the end of the world, on the doomsday, both sun and moon will be deprived of the light as this is given to both for a temporary period. When both of them lose their light, our eyes will naturally engage in the real light of God from Whom both received the light. This makes us know the difference between the owner of the light and His borrowers and also the difference between this temporary and mortal world and the everlasting world may appear. The wet nurse is with me for three-four days. O my mother! Come to me and lift me in your lap.

sections.heading: Light of God Through the Godly: Not Direct
paras: The peacock continued: “My feathers are like the thick and polluted cloud. They are fine and beautiful because of the reflection due to the concern and affection of God for me. I keep my feathers away from the path of His concern, so that I may look at the bright moon, God, through the light of the moon itself. I do not want the care and protection of the wet nurse. I want to be with my mother. I am like H. Musa, who, as a baby rejected the approach of so many wet nurses and went into the lap of his mother only. I do not want the direct concern and grace of the moon (God) as this has been a cause of destruction for many. It should be from a saint who has inculcated godly qualities within himself to such an extent that what all he shows would be godly, as though like a cloud that has become bright like the moon itself. That saint should show his face to me in the quality of La (no God), as though he is not different from God just as the bodies of the prophets and real saints are. That is: what all that can be known about could be known from them, and there is no need to go in search of others, others being none or nobody (La) for me. When this happens, I do not see anything other than God. I see everything in God and God in everything. That saint would be of such level as not to be like the curtain of cloud for the moon. Rather, he would be one who would tear off the curtain and be benevolent to show what is hidden behind it.

sections.heading: Clouds Losing Cloudy Appearance
paras: That perfect master is like the morning sun which chases away darkness from everything and presents in clearness. He is like the rain drops that fall without the cloud, as has been seen earlier in a miracle of the Prophet when water from a single goatskin full of water, provided water for large number of people and camels and also filled a large number of empty goatskins. This incident is already explained in the earlier chapters (pages). Because of his miracle, the cloud had assumed the colour of sky and invisible drops of rain fell from the sky. There was cloud in fact, but its cloudy qualities had vanished. Such a thing happens in the case of a patient lover, who has his body, but his bodily features disappear. His colour and smell get lost and he is entirely changed.

sections.heading: Keep Yourself Humble for Protection
paras: The peacock continued: “My feathers are for the pleasure of others, but only my head is for me, which is a house of hearing and seeing and a pillar of the body. To make yourself as a victim to be hunted by others, is rejection of the gifts of God in entirety and giving up of the hope of good things. Be careful: never to be pleasing like sugar for the birds who are these mean worldly people but become poison for them and protect yourself from losses. These fellows will tell you that you are very benevolent, appreciable and respectable to please to meet their own nefarious ends. They are doggish. Do not fall for them. Make yourself worthless and useless for them like a dead body. It is for this reason and for protection that H. Khizr damaged a good boat as such it was saved from the cruel king. The noble Prophet also said: “I am proud of my poverty”, so as to be away from the greedy worldly fellows, who go after the rich. That is the reason that treasures are kept in the ruins, so that they may remain protected from the greed of the people of populated places.

If the peacock cannot pluck its feathers, it should resort to seclusion and be away from the people so that it may not be a means of the expenses of all these and those men. This is for the reason that you are an eater of morsels of food and also the morsel of food of others. Therefore, one who is an eater of food, and the food of the other eaters must be very careful.

chapters.title: All Eat but Not God
chapters.subtitle: To explain that all things other than God are eaters and are also food of others, like the bird which is busy catching the locust while a hungry falcon from behind is after it to catch. Therefore, O Man, going after the hunt! Do not be carefree of the hunter after you. If you cannot see your hunter with your eyes, look at him with your sense and mind so that your unseeing eyes may see, upon God’s wish

paras: A tiny bird was engaged in hunting a locust, and a cat got the chance and snatched the bird away. The bird was a morsel of food of the cat, but it was not aware of it. It was hunting someone else but was not aware that someone else was at it. The thief is busy in taking away other’s materials, and the police officer along with the thief’s enemies is after the thief. The thief’s wisdom is engaged in the goods and door lock of the victim’s house but is unaware of the police and curses that his victims made before God. He is so sunk in his own affairs that he is not aware of another who is after him.

Grass drinks water and grows and it is to be digested in the animal’s stomach. Eater of grass became the food of its eater. Everything is similarly placed, except God because He is the One who feeds and does not eat as the Quran says: He is that feeds but is not fed. Wa huwa yut ‘imu wala yut ‘am: (An ‘aam: 6: 14)

God is not an eater of food, meat and skin. One who eats and itself becomes the food of another, cannot remain in peace with the other eater who is in its search. Peace of those to be eaten is a cause of mourning. They cannot be at peace with those waiting to eat them. Therefore, go to that place of One who does not eat.

sections.heading: Thoughts Eat Man
paras: One thought eats another thought. One’s thought grazes upon another’s thought. You are as well a victim of thoughts and insinuations which are always with you. You cannot get rid of them even when you sleep to avoid them. Your thoughts are like the honeybees and your sleep is like water. They will be hovering over you like honeybees hovering upon a man in water. Upon your getting up these honeybees will come over you again. Many flies of thoughts will always fly around you. They drag you this side and take you to that side. These thoughts about food are of those that eat you out. Even the routine and smallest of the thoughts which feed upon you are known to God.

sections.heading: Seek Protection of God (Treaty of Hudabiah)
paras: Therefore, be warned, to run away from the company of big eaters and go toward the One who has said: “He is your Protector”. Or run fast toward the one who has already attained this protection, if you are not capable of going directly toward the Protector. Do not hold on to the hand of anyone other than a good master, as God’s hand has held on to his hand. The master of your own wisdom has habituated you to childish conduct, as it is in the neighbourhood of your vicious self. Therefore, make yourself a friend of perfect and total wisdom so that it may cleanse you of these bad habits. When you keep your hand upon his hand, you will get out of the hands of your eaters. Your hand will be one among those who show their fealty to that great man, and in such a case, the hand of God is over their hands and yours, as stated: yadullaaha fawqa aidiihim: (Fath: 48: 10).

Your position will be like that of the companions of the Prophet, who entered into fealty with him and kept their hands upon the hand of the Prophet to be with him in all good and bad circumstances. [This transaction took place at a place, Hudaibia on the road to Makka. This fealty was called as the fealty of good pleasure: Bait-ur-Ridhwan. This transaction of the companions of the Prophet of placing hand upon hand was so pleasing that God called that the hand of God is over their hands. Yadullahi fawqa aidihim — Translator]

sections.heading: One Is with the Loved One
paras: When you give your hand into the hand of that master, you may find out that the master’s hand is nothing but wisdom, as the master is well-informed, knowledgeable and wise. He is a reflection of the Prophet of the time as the light of the Prophet emanates from him. For this reason, you enter into the treaty of Hudaibiah, which the Prophet entered into with the pagans of Makka, which gave immense benefits to Muslims. You become one among the ten companions about whose entry into paradise was foretold during their lifetime itself. [They are H-Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Usman, ‘Ali, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Awf, Abu ‘Ubaidah, Sa’ad bin Waqqas and Sayeed bin Zaid —Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. You become pure gold, which retains the same weight even after heating. You will remain in his company in this and that world as the Prophet has said: “A man is with the one he loves. Heart does not separate from its beloved object.”

sections.heading: Every Hunter, Hunted by Another
paras: Everywhere there are nets and grains. Do not be careless in this matter. Look at those weak fellows who trap the other weak fellows. The one, who traps the weak must know that there is another one with his hand above his hand. Break that rope of greed and jealousy and remember the fate of Abu Lahab’s wife who was trapped by the palm-leaf fibre around her neck: Fii jiidihaa hablun min masad: (Lahab: 111: 5). Your heart and wisdom realised that it is necessary to be away from the net; but your own net is pasted upon your own feathers. This is a strange situation to know whether you are weak or the catcher of the weak. For not finding this clearly, it is required that you should always be in fear and caution every time, about the matters of needs.

It is a strange situation that the bird is an eater of someone and the food of another. In the matter of searching, you are both a hunter and the hunted. Greed for hunting keeps a man unaware of the fact that he is also about to be hunted. He tries to steal the heart of someone and forgets that he is also liable to be stolen. Do not be unmindful like those for whom bar has been put in front and behind: wa ja ‘alnaa minbaini aidiihim saddan wa min khalfihim saddan: (Yasiin: 36: 9). In such a case, you do not see even a clearly visible enemy.

sections.heading: Look All Around Before You Act
paras: Do not be lesser than a bird in hearing the sounds of danger. See that the sparrow always looks in front and back. Do not be lesser than a sparrow and observe how it looks in front and back, when it comes near a grain to pick. It so looks by turning its face back and front, to find out whether any hunter is behind it, so that it may ignore to pick the grain in front of it. You may look at the incidents of the fate of the vicious people of the past or consider the case of the death of a neighbour and friend. God causes death without any ostensible weapon. He is very nearby to you in all circumstances. He puts one into a tangle without a hand and mace. He is one to punish without hands.

sections.heading: Different Ends of Rejectors
paras: There is one who says: “If there is God, where is he?” But he says: “He is nearby” when caught in a tangle. So also, one who says: “It is far off and strange to believe in God”! When caught in a tangle he sheds tears and says: “Oh, you are very close to me”! And yet the one, who has no other job than to reject God, ultimately has nothing but regrets, which are of no use. Consider the cases of Pharaoh and Th(s)amud, Lot’s people, Salih’s people and the community of Hood. Look at what happened to the oppressive Nimrod and at the end of the community of Noah, so as to know that God is hearing and seeing, and He does not have any fear and absolutely clean of apprehensions and worries.

The peacock continued: “I am removing the nails upon which the net hangs with the object that I should not fail. I have said all this keeping in view, your level of wisdom. Think over and do not turn your face from further enquires.”

chapters.title: Why Crow Was Killed
chapters.subtitle: Reason for H. Ibrahim’s killing of the crow was to Point out as to which of the Human vicious, Mortal character that He wanted to Finish

paras: There is no end and escape from this discussion.

sections.heading: Seeking of Long Life
paras: “But O Ibrahim, the friend of God! Please tell me: Why did you kill the crow? You may say, it was upon an order of God! But what was the wisdom behind this command? Please explain to me a little of these secrets?”

H. Ibrahim said: “Caw, caw is the noise and cry of the crow always to seek for a long life for its body.” This is what Iblis did, that he demanded a life from God till the doomsday. He said: “Give me respite till the day they are raised”: Anzhirnii ilaa yawmi yub‘ath(s)uuna: (A‘raaf: 7: 14). How good it would have been if he had said: “I repent, O God!” Life without the friend (God) results in its destruction. It is immediate death that is hidden from him. Both life and death are good along with the company of God; and without Him, even the life-giving water is fire. This prayer for long life by Satan was a product of his accursed state that before that Grandeur, he prayed for a long time. Seeking something other than God from God is an ignoble claim of degradation and total deprivation. In particular, a life which is sunk in unawareness about Him. It is showing foxiness before the lion. Seeking of long life is to go away from Him and to degrade yourself. It is to become a victim of curses. He is a vicious fellow who searches for curses.

sections.heading: Long Life for Closeness with God
paras: Long life ought to be for closeness with God to bring up the soul in a proper manner, as against the long life of the crow which is for eating filth. If it is not for a noble purpose, it means that it is for eating filth like the crow, declaring oneself as of baser origin. One not going after eating filth like the crow would say: Grant me relief from the filthy nature of the crow.

O God! You converted mud into gold and from another part of the mud, created the father of all humans. Your work is bringing about alterations and changes in the creations and providing them with new grants. But I resort to forgetfulness, wrongs and mistakes. Pray change my wrongs and mistakes into knowledge and my impatience into patience and composure of mind. You bring out bread out of saltish land and convert the dead bread into living. You provide guidance to the confused and make them guides; you make prophets out of unguided ones. You give life to dark mud and give it wisdom, sense, provisions and faith. You provide sugar to cane and fruits to wood and create beautiful beloved out of lifeless semen. You create flowers out of mud and sincerity in the hearts. A lump the fat of the eyes is enabled by you to see light and brightness. You make a part of the earth as a part of the sky and cause increase in the earth through the stars. One who makes this world itself as life-giving-water and object of life, meets one’s death well before the death of others.

One whose heart looks at the heavens with inner sight sees that creations are going on in them every moment. There are great physical and chemical changes going on there. These are like the darning of the torne clothes without threads. Know this, O man! The day when you came into existence, you were either fire, earth or air. If you had continued to be in that form, you would not have had any process of evolution. The coming together of all these elements brought about the change in you. Because of this change your earlier conditions ceased to exist and in their place a new existence came to be. In similar manner lakhs of creations have come about in existence, one after the other. And the later is better than the former. Therefore, look at the One, who is bringing about the changes, and not at their causes, because by concentrating upon the causes, you will go away from the Original Creator. The more are the causes looked at, the pleasure of going to the beloved gets reduced. Attention gets distracted and divided. Where there is no attention on the causes, the enthusiasm to meet the beloved increases. Knowledge of the causes reduces your astonishment because, it is the astonishment that leads you to His court.

sections.heading: Annihilations Granted Better States
paras: You have obtained the various stages of evolution with the annihilation of the earlier stages. Therefore, you should not hesitate to get annihilated. One annihilation leads to a further evolved stage. These annihilations have not caused any loss to you but given better states. Being ignorant of this, you are sticking on to this stage of existence. When your next state is better than the previous one, you should search for annihilation of the present state which will lead to better state and engage you in the worship of the evolver and get annihilated in Him.

You have passed through lakhs of stages from the starting of the creation to this day, of which you are careless and forgetful. You were at the stage of lifeless rock or mineral from which you sprouted in the form of a plant; and from plant you developed into animal. While in the stage of plant you did not have the need to move about in search of food but upon becoming animal you had to struggle and put efforts for food. And as animal, you went toward the development of five senses to differentiate material objects and then to wisdom to recognise intelligible things, within the six dimensions of left-right, back-front, up-down. And then there was your getting out of the five senses and six dimensions (of space and time) as wisdom has no dimensions.

sections.heading: Markings on Land, Not on Sea
paras: The markings of these developments are in the limited expanse of land which lead up to the seashore as footsteps; and once you enter into the larger expanse of the ocean, there will be no footsteps. This is because, the locations on the land can be marked by boundaries of houses, villages, and countries. But there are no such locations on the sea, because of the ever-moving waves. There cannot be walls and roofs on the sea. Here, there are no scopes for walking and leaving footprints. There are no markings of the houses, and locations nor any names for them. However, both land and sea are products of the lowly material world and locations. All these form this world in the space of this world. Yet there is another non-material, higher, non-spatial world (Laa -makaan) which is invisible to the eyes. There is a great distance between these two spatial and non-spatial worlds.

sections.heading: Evolutions of Life from Matter
paras: You have already been explained about the existence after annihilation or existence through annihilation or existence in annihilation. Such being the case, why do you attach yourself to this physical body which gets annihilated. Therefore, do not be like a crow craving for long life. Give up the lowly life of the crow and choose the high life of the falcon. Become a life-sacrificing brave man and face the alterations that God brings about. Give up old state and become fresh, as this year of yours is better than your earlier three years. Be like the date palm that gives its fruits to others; and see that after this, God blesses it with fresh fruits. If you cannot become like the date palm, go on collecting and keeping old things upon old things. Like the uncropped ripe fruits, what all you collect will become old, foul and rotten. You may present them before every lousy fellow. One who has seen new things will not come to you for your old, foul things. He is under God’s presence having devoted himself to Him. He will not fall into you trap. All those who come to you are flocks of blind birds. They will come to taste your saltish water so as to increase their blindness, as the saltish water increase blindness.

People devoted to this world are blind of heart, as they prefer to drink saltish muddy water. You will also have to drink this saltish water and roam about in the world in blindness as you do not have the life-giving water within yourself. Inspite of this, in this situation, you are crazy for long life. You are contented with your black face like the negro. The negro is happy and contented with his black colour, because he is black from his birth itself and that is as per his naturally given quality. One who was fair coloured in looks earlier, will try to get rid of black colour if he becomes black.

A flying bird trapped on the land feels pain and sorrow and cries. But a domestic bird roams about happily on land, picks up grains with pleasure and runs about smartly, as it is without flight from the beginning itself. The other flying bird was a flier with spread out feathers.

chapters.title: The Noble Prophet, May God’s Blessings Be upon Him Said: Have Pity on Three Persons: Honourable Leader of a Community Put to Disgrace, a Rich Man Fallen in Poverty, and a Scholar Ridiculed by the Ignorant

paras: The Prophet said: Have pity on that man who was rich earlier but having become poor later; On the one who was honourable, but then got disgraced; On that sincere scholar living among harsh troublesome fellows. The Prophet said: have pity for these three whether you are hard-hearted like the rack or mountain. That is: the one who honourable earlier but got disgraced later; that rich man who has no money with him; and thirdly that scholar who gets engaged among the fools of the world.

This is because, falling into disgrace from an honourable position is like the cutting off of a limb from the body. That cut off limb becomes lifeless. Freshly cut limb is restless for some time and then rests. One who has enjoyed life in the previous year feels the pain and sorrow of the losses this year. One who has never seen taste of greatness like a dog living in filth can never have the greed for command and governance. It is only a person having committed a sin, who resorts to repentance. He only takes a long sigh of regret, who has lost his path and possessions.

chapters.title: Torture of Unsuitable Companions
chapters.subtitle: Story of a young deer kept in a donkey’s stable and their making fun of the deer, quarrelling with and laughing at it; and its compulsion of going for dry grass which is not its food. This is the situation of God’s closely devotees in the midst of worldly, sensual fellows. The noble Prophet has rightly said: “Islam began as a stranger and shortly, it will again become a stranger.” This is happy news for the strangers

paras: A hunter caught hold of a deer and kept the hapless in a stable that was full of oxen and donkeys. He imprisoned it like a cruel fellow. The deer desperately ran here and there. The hunter put dry grass before the animals at night for their food. Every ox and donkey out of hunger started eating dry grass with greater pleasure as though eating sugar. The deer ran helter-skelter and turned its frowning face from it as though from smoke.

One who is left with one’s opposite-natured fellow considers it as death. This is what H. Sulaiman said: “If the hoopoe does not give a reasonable excuse for its being away, I shall kill it or I myself would give it such a torture, that has no limits.” What else can be that punishment than putting it in a cage along with a bird of other species.

Similarly, my son, you are also in the torture by being imprisoned in the body. The bird of your soul is entangled with one of the other species. Soul is like a falcon, but man’s temperaments are like the crows; and the body is very much injured by these crows of bad temperament. It is in great distress in their midst, like an Abu Bakr in the city of Sabz war.

chapters.title: Khwarizam Shah’s Order
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of sultan Muhammad Khwarizam Shah who captured the city of Sabzwar in a battle, the Inhabitants of which were Rafizis. They sued for peace. He said: I shall give you peace if you bring before me a man by name Abu Bakr

sections.heading: A Man of Abu Bakr’s Name as Tribute
paras: Muhammad Alap Ulugh Khwarizam Shah was engaged in a battle for the city of Sabzwar. His troops had laid siege of the city and busy in attacking the enemies. The residents of the city came out, fell before him and submitted to him to give peace, protect them and take them among his subjects. Whatever tribute and damages needed would be given by them, which could be increased after every season. They further said: “You are lion-hearted and our lives may be considered to be as your property. Let our lives be in our possession as your trust for some days.”

The king said: “You cannot rid your lives from my control, until you present before me one amongst you with the name ‘Abu Bakr’. The condition for peace is the presentation before me one amongst you with the name AbuBakr, as you are a misguided people; and he alone can be a tribute to me. If you do not do this, I shall cut you off like a ripened crop. I shall not take any money, nor shall I be fooled by your sweet, slippery words of flattery”.

They placed before him a bag full of ashrafis (gold coins) and pleaded not to demand Abu Bakr from their city. How can there be an Abu Bakr in Sabzwar? It is as impossible as a lump of mud remaining dry in a stream of water. The king turned his face from the gold coins and said: “Unless you bring Abu Bakr as a gift from you to me, it will be of no use. I am not a child to be wonderstruck with shining gold and silver. O worthless fellows! Unless you lay down your forehead in prostration in duteous prayer in the mosque, you cannot be absolved of your duteous prayer, even if you sweep your hips on every bit of area of the mosque. [The citizens of Sabzwar belonged to a sect of rebellious people who had deserted H. ‘Ali, the fourth Calif, at the ‘battle of camel’. Later they became so devoted to H. ‘Ali, that they refused to accept the khilafat of the earlier three califs — H. Abu Bakr, H. ‘Umar and H. ‘Usman, and called them all as usurpers of H. ‘Ali’s right. They resented these three names so much that they never tolerated a man of any of these names in their midst. — Translator]

sections.heading: Search for Abu Bakr
paras: They dispatched searchers in all directions, as they had no hope of getting one Abu Bakr in their city as it was a desolated place for one of such name. They ran about for three days to find one and found one very weak and broke person by name Abu Bakr. He was a traveller and had fallen due to sickness, lying in the corner of an infested ruin. He was like a precious pearl without anyone to take care of him. He was in such suffering as to exhibit the pains of his heart from his face. He was sleeping in a desolated corner. Looking at him they instantly said: “Get up! The king wants to see you. Our city will be saved from destruction because of you.”

He said: “Were I be with healthy, strong legs, and ability to walk, I would have been on the way to my destination and reached it. I would not have settled in this inimical place. I would have driven my vehicle toward my friends.”
They laid him in a litter and lifted on their shoulders and started running toward Khwarizam Shah so that he might see what he wanted.

sections.heading: Finding a Man of Heart
paras: This world is like Sabzwar and a godly man is unwanted and non-existent. God is like the grand Khwarizan Shah who expected a good heart from the degraded people. The Prophet has said: God does not look at your face and possessions. He looks at your heart and actions. He looks at you through the medium of a man of heart, and not at your appearances, your prayers and your charities. As you have considered your heart itself as heart, you have neglected to search for a man of heart, a heart which is so expansive that if seven hundred heavens of the size of the seven heavens enter into it, they will get lost and go out of existence. Do not call your heart and such heart like yours as heart. They are not real hearts. Searching for such a heart is like searching for Abu Bakr in Sabzwar. A man of heart is like a glass of six faces and God looks at it from six directions. That is, from all sides — right, left, front, back, and up and down.

sections.heading: Extra-Ordinary Features of Man of Heart
paras: One who has settled himself in this world of six dimensions and sees from all the six sides cannot look at other things than God even for a moment. When he looks at something, he looks at for the sake of God. His acceptance or rejection of anything is for God. As he is for God alone in every situation. He becomes a selected one of the God of Majesty. God does not give anything to anyone, other than through him. I have only said a little about him as I cannot tell all.

Whatever that God wishes to give to anyone, he first keeps upon his palm and passes on to the deserving. God, the river of all things is connected with him and he is a master of all qualities that cannot be explained by words. Attempts to explain them are impossible. Let there be no more talk of it.

sections.heading: God Sees the Heart
paras: O rich man! If you bring a hundred bags full of gold before God, God will tell: You are crooked. I don’t want all this. What I want is a heart. Bring it forth to me. If that heart is in consonance with you, I shall also have consonance with you. And if it is not happy with you. I am also not. I do not look at you, but I look at your heart. Therefore, bring a present from the heart to my door. I am the same as the heart is with you, just as the paradise is under the feet of mothers. Heart is the base and mothers and fathers of all are superstructures. That man is great who has identified the pulp from the rind. You will say that you have brought the heart to me, but the heart says: You have not. What you have brought forth is not of the worth of a farthing.

Bring forth that heart, which is the apex of the world, which is the heart of the heart of the heart of H. Adam. The king of the hearts is waiting for a heart full of light and virtues. Even if you search for such a heart for days together in Sabzwar, you cannot get it. You will have to carry a half-dead and forsaken heart on a litter and take it before the sultan and tell him: ‘O sultan, I have brought a heart for you, and there is none better than this in the whole of Sabzwar: [when the people of Sabzwar were so narrow minded as not to allow an Abu Bakr to live with them, they have only half-dead man forsaken hearts.] The king will tell you: “You wreckless fellows! Do not think my place is a graveyard that you have brought a dead heart before me. Take it back and bring a worthy one with royal qualities. As the greenery (Sabzwar) of the world is in peace only because of such a heart.

sections.heading: Scarcity of Men of Hearts
paras: You will tell him: “There is no such a heart in this world, which is a world of darkness, and such a heart is light. And darkness and light cannot be together. Such a world has enmity for such a heart from the very beginning of creation. The greenery of the world is its inheritance. Because such a heart is like a falcon and this world is a place of the living of the crows. Looking at one species with another species is very painful. If the worldly man shows softness, it is due to hypocrisy. He wants only to please the other with softness to gain benefits from him. He nods his head and says ‘yes, yes’ to an adviser only with the intention that he should stop saying more. Because this means crow is in search of a dead body and has lakhs of treacheries one upon the other.

The adviser gets rid of his troubles if he accepts their hypocritic ‘yes, yes’. In such a case they will consider their hypocrisy as very beneficent considering it as the proper way. Such is the case of the great men of heart, who with their grand, generous nature purchase even defective things from our markets. Such men of heart are of great worth. Search for them if you are not totally dead, and still have a little remnant of life. Be one with him as one of his own species, if you are not an opponent of this king. That fellow is your friend whose treacheries appear good to you, and not the man of God. Everyone who is in accordance with your habits and temperament is considered as a saint and prophet by you.

Give your selfish desires in order that the fragrance of God may enter into your nose. Give up the desires of your vicious self so as to cause goodness to you and enable your brain to enjoy the fragrance of ambergris. But you are in love with filth like the crow. The fragrance of musk cannot reach your brain. There is no limit to this discussion and see that our deer is running helter-skelter in the stable.

chapters.title: Left Over Narrative of the Deer in the Stable

paras: That male deer, possessor of the musk gland was held up in the stable of donkeys for many days. It was in the pangs of death like a fish out of water. This was like keeping of dung and musk in one box spoiling each other’s qualities.

One donkey said to it: “You are the father of the beasts, but you have the temperament of kings and nobles to maintain royal silence.” Another laughed and ironically said: “He has brought pearls from the impacts of the sea tides. He cannot sell at low price.” Another said: “because of your soft delicate nature you should sit resting upon the pillows of the throne.” Another donkey suffered from indigestion and had left its share of the dry grass and invited it for eating.

The deer shook its head to say ‘no’ and said: “I am not hungry. I have become very weak.” That donkey said: “I know, you are playing tricks and showing false reluctance. Or out of your false pride, pretending diet-control.” The deer said: “You may eat as it is your food, and your limbs are strong, lively and fresh with it. I have been familiar with the forest. I have rested under the shades of gardens. If fate has put me into difficulties, I cannot get rid of that fine habit and temperament. I have become a destitute, but I cannot become disgraceful. My dress might have become old, but I continue to be fresh. Hyacinth, lilac and sweet basil have been eaten by me with great pride and delicacy for a thousand times.”
The donkey said: “Yes, yes! Go on boasting. Much nonsense can be talked about in an unknown place.”
The deer replied: “My navel is an evidence of my claim, which puts to shame aloes-wood and ambergris.”

But where was anyone with the brain to smell the fragrance of these fine things. These are forbidden for the dung worshipping donkey. The donkey smells the urine of other donkeys on the way. How can I present musk in such a gathering? It is for the reason that the Prophet, the acceptor of truth has said: “Islam is a stranger in the world (Al-Islam fidduniya gharlib), because it is such that with its possession even one’s own relatives run away, even though angels are friends of one’s personality. Common people consider him as one among themselves and do not try to seek his fragrance. He is like a lion among the cows. Look at him from a distance and do not make probing enquiries with him. If you make many enquiries, will he remove your cow-like qualities? This lion will tear you off to remove your lowly humble qualities and make you strong like himself. He will remove your animal-like character and make you a man. If you are prepared to undergo these changes, you may make probing enquiries with him. And if you are happy and contented with your cow-like qualities, do not go for lionness.

chapters.title: Eating of Seven Fat Cows
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of Egyptian king’s telling: I saw (in a dream) seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows: Inni araa sab‘a baqaraatin simaanin yaa kuluhunna sab ‘un ‘ijaafun: (Yusuf 11: 42). These lean cows were created by God on the quality of hungry Lions such that they ate seven fat cows. The king’s thoughts appeared as cows in the mirror of his dream, you may consider them to be Lions in reality

paras: The king of Egypt saw in a dream something strange, as a result of the opening of the door of the secret hidden world for his hidden eyes. He saw that seven fat domestic cows were eaten by seven weak and lean cows. Those lean, weak cows in reality were lions, as otherwise, they would not have eaten cows. Similarly, there are many men who appear to be ordinary men engaged in routine jobs, but in reality, they are hidden lions that tear off men. They eat and destroy the bad qualities of men and make them unique and extraordinary. They clean a man of his impurities and make him pure, though, in this process that man undergoes some pain. But this single pain rids him of all other pains, and then he becomes capable of keeping his feet upon the sky. He becomes a king and gives up his beggarliness. He finds the lasting life of heart in annihilation.

If you want to change yourself on this line, you may offer the fatness of your body before such great man by reducing your fatness through austerities in all sincerity and fairness. As against this, if you reject and dismiss such great men, it amounts to a murder of a guest. You make yourself unworthy like an ass. Think over as to how long you would like to protect and fatten the cow of your body. Know this that ultimately the body of your cow dies and rots and then you will feel ashamed of yourself.

chapters.title: To Explain as to Which Hidden Vicious and Mortal Quality of Man That H. Ibrahim Wanted to Defeat and Destroy Through the Killing of the Cock

paras: How long can there be a talk like the funny crow? O Ibrahim, please tell me, why did you kill the cock? Please tell me as to what was the motive behind this killing, so that after knowing of it, every hair of my body may engage in the praises of God. H. Ibrahim said: “It was upon a command of God!” I said: “That is not enough for me.” Please tell me about the reasoning behind the command so that I may be a repeater of the article: there is no God, but Allah.”

H. Ibrahim replied: “The cock is full of sexual passion and always engages in sexual acts. It is terribly intoxicated with this poisonous, senseless wine. O the one for whom a will has been made, you should know that, if sexual desire was not needed for procreation, H Adam would have castrated himself to protect himself from this shameful desire. The accursed Satan prayed to God, the lord of justice. “I want to make a strong net to catch man in it as he is my prey.” In answer to his prayer, gold, silver and horses were shown to him so that he may catch man through a net made of them. But he said: “Okey!” But instantly, expressed dissatisfaction and sourness like that of lemon. Then, God placed before that accursed fellow gold and gems from great mines and told him: “You accursed fellow; you may take this as another net.” But he demanded something greater than this. Then He was given sweet dishes and costly fine drinks and many silk fabrics. But he said: “My God, I seek the support of still greater things so that I may put a rope made of the palm leaf fibre to tie around man’s neck, so that such of those strong and brave men devoted to You may break the knot with great difficulties. So that, with those ropes, those committed to sensual desires may be separated from others and become distinct.

He said: “O my God, the Maker of fate, I need a different kind of net in which even the strongest of men must be caught and defeated in it. Then God placed liquors and musical instruments. With these, he was a little happy and smiled. Then, he said to God: “You guide and also misguide your creatures as per your decision taken at the start of the world. I call upon Your misguiding quality to bring out the mischiefs of dust from the depth of the sea. I ask you: had there not been among your servants a man by name Musa, who had tied the curtains of dust around the ocean making its water to pull out its reins so as to fly off dust from its depths.”

When God exhibited to him the beauty of women, which flies off the patience and composure of men, he was immensely pleased and started dancing and said: “Please give this to me! With this I meet my object. “Then, he looked at their intoxicating eyes, which cause loss of sense to wisdom and intellect; and at the softness of their cheeks, upon which the heart of men burns and dances like black grains which burn to cast magic spells; and at the bright faces with black moles on them, with curved eyebrows and ruby like lips as the sun shining behind a thin curtain, in a tallness like that of the cypress tree and cheeks like fragrant flowers. When he saw their styles, he jumped over as though looking at the radiance of God from behind a thin curtain. With these beautiful sceneries their magic spells, mischievous, coquettish appearances, the world is in amazement and madness.

chapters.title: Rise and Fall of Beauty
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of ayats: We have indeed created man in the best of moulds, then we abase him to be the lowest of the low — Laqad khalaqnal insaana min ahsani taqwiim. Th(s)umma radadnaahu asfala saafiliina (Tin(fig) 95: 4 and 5) And: wa man nu ‘ammirhu, nunakkishu fil khalqi afalaa ya‘qiluuna: if we grant long life to any, we cause him to be reversed in nature: will they not then understand? (Yaseen: 36: 68)

paras: Men, jinns and angels fall in prostration before these beauties; and later these beauties get degraded, like H. Adam, after the passage of youthfulness. The beauty said: “Ah! What a tragedy? Destruction after construction!” she was told: “You have committed a wrong! You have lived long!”

Jibra’iil is dragging her by catching her tufts telling her: “Come out of paradise and the company of beauties.” Then, she said: “Why this disgrace after honouring!” Jibra’iil said: “That was a grant for you, and this is justice.” The beauty said: “O Jibra’iil! You were prostrating me with all heart and soul. Why do you pull me out of the paradise of beauty? I am being put into great trial and my beautiful apparel is getting torne, just as the leaves of the tree fall down in autumn.”

sections.heading: Decline of Beauty and Youth
paras: That face which was bright like full moon, has become thorny like the back of the lizard. That head and the parting of hair upon it were shining beauties, and in the old age are becoming ugly and bald. The tall height which used to dance and show styles like shaft of the spear has bent down in old age like the bow. Hairs black like the feathers of the crow have gone white like snow and the face has become full of the markings of wrinkles. The red colour like lilac has turned yellow like saffron; and the strength like that of the lion has become weak like the frailty of women. Eyes resembling narcissus have dried up. Heat of the body has gone cold. The one who used to wrench strong fellows in his armpit is in need of the support in his armpit while walking. These are all the symptoms of sorrows and decline and each one of them is a foreboding of death.

chapters.title: Exceptions to Decline Read Only
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of except such as believe and do righteous deeds: For they shall have a reward unfailing: Illa allaziina aamanuu wa ‘amilu ab, ssaalihaati falahum ajrun ghairu mannuunin (Tins (fig): 95: 6)

paras: But, if the light of God accompanies a person, he will not feel any anxiety and trouble in old age. His weariness due to age is like the inebriation of a drunk which is so pleasing that even a strong man like Rustam would feel jealous of. When he dies, his bones sink into a pleasurable taste. Every particle of his body is full of the rays of the light of enthusiasm. One who does not get this light is like a garden with fruitless trees which is further upset with autumn. Its flowers wither off and the thorns go black. It turns yellow without any content like a heap of grass. One wonders asking: “O God what wrong has he done that the beautiful apparel you had given to him has been taken away from him?” The answer would be: “It has looked into itself and considered all its beauty as of its own creation and not from God. This is a calamity which it should have expected and considered its pride as life taking poison.”

sections.heading: Beauty: a Temporary Grant
paras: That beautiful beloved in whose love the world was in the pangs of separation has been chased by that world itself, as it has beauty no more. What wrong is there if those devoted to beauty run away from beauty when it has ceased to continue. This beautiful beloved’s wrong was that it considered the jewels given to it for a short time as its own and was proud of it. These jewels were given by Me, and I take them back to establish that the beautiful jewels belonged to Me. I am the owner of the stockpile of harvest and others have been provided with a little part of it. So that, the beautiful may know that the dress of beauty they wore was a borrowed one from Me. It is just a reflection of the sun of the Ever-Existing God. His beauty, vigour, excellence and accomplishment just travelled from the sun of His beauty toward the beautiful one. All these virtues vanish when this sun rises again, just as stars vanish when their sun rises. The brightened walls become dark. Reflection of the sun went away from that place and every wall became black and dark.

sections.heading: Seeing Through Coloured Glass
paras: That beauty of the beloved whose face had flabbergasted you is like the sun’s light passing through a tri-coloured glass. Colourful glasses exhibit the sun’s light in different colours. When these colourful glasses are not there, the colourless light puts you in amazement as to what has happened. These coloured glasses are not lasting. Therefore, try to cultivate the habit of seeing the original pure light in place of seeing through coloured glasses, so that you may not be disabled to see if the glasses are shattered. You have remained contented with what you have acquired with learning from others. It is like seeing through the lamp of another. When he takes away his lamp from you, you will know that you are only a borrower and dependent upon others. You are not an independent bold man.

If you depend upon your own self and be thankful to God and put efforts, you will not have to worry. You will get hundreds of things of beauty. As against this, if you do not use your faculties and be thankful, you will have to shed tears of blood later, when the beauty given to you by God vanishes. Efforts of the community of the rejectors are spoiled by God and those of the noble believers will be put on the proper path. Good qualities and abilities go away from a thankless fellow in such a way that he will not see them again. His connections with himself and with others, and the thanks upon grants get lost in such a way that, he will not even have their memories. Know this, O rejectors; even their good deeds go waste, even though searching for things is the aim and object of every worldly man. The same efforts by the thankful and faithful are followed by success and good results.

sections.heading: Pay Loan to God to Get More
paras: The wealth that is lost, does not provide any strength, and the wealth that is to come has its own benevolent properties. God has told to give loan to Him. Iqridhuallaha qardhan hasnan (Maida: 5: 12) and therefore give him a loan, in order to see hundreds of occasions of wealth in its repayment. Reduce a little of your drinks in your own interest, so that you may drink from the spring of excesses (Aab-e-Kauth(s)ar). God will please their hearts and improve their conditions. Aslaha baalahum: (Muhammad: 47: 2). And return to them whatever they had spent along with much excess. O death! And O that Turk returning (from the loot of villages), return to the people whatever you have snatched from those thankful people and be thankful to Me. Death will return to them, all that they had, but they will not take back, because by then, they would be rich with the wealth of the soul. They would say: “We have become sufis! We have rid ourselves of all that we had including our old clothes. When we have given over all things, we shall not take back. We have been rewarded with all that and in such a great, generous manner, that all needs greeds and desires have gone away from us. We have come out of the saltish water of the world and settled ourselves with the wine and water of kauth(s)ar.” They will say “O world, whatever you had given to us, comprising of unfaithfulness, trickery and ostentation is thrown upon your head, for the sake of God as we are the martyrs of the (Jihad) struggle in the fight of truth so that you may know that the devotees of God are along with God, in the noble attacks that He carries on. We pull down the moustaches of the treacheries of the world and hoist His flags on the fort of His support and victory. These martyrs have become the victorious fighters once again because they are the ones who have attained everlasting life after their annihilation in God. They have once again engaged themselves in order to help those who are held up in the prisons of the world. The locks of difficulties are now open with their efforts resulting in the life and death struggle of the rejectors.

sections.heading: World of Non-Existence (‘Adams)
paras: The despair that had come about is now converted into hope. This idol home is converted into the masjid of God. They had been lost into the world of non-existence (‘adam) but have once again come out of it as real existents. They tell the people: Look at us and see the great changes all around as you are not blind, so that you may know that the world of non-existence (‘adam) has many suns in it and the suns of this world are small like stars.

O brother! You may wonder as to how there can be existence in non-existence (‘adam)? How can an opposite exist in its opposite? But you may know this: it is God who brings out the living from the dead: Yukhrijul hayya minal mayyiti: (Ruum: 30: 19). Therefore, be sure that He creates the living out of the dead. All His worshippers repose confidence in ‘adam.

This is like the case of a farmer whose farmland is empty of crops and produce. This land is like ‘adam for him. Is he not happy in the hope of getting a harvest from that barren land? He is sure that crops will certainly come in it and puts efforts for them. This example ought to be sufficient for you to understand.
