Therefore, be in the wait always for the ‘Adam, so that you may remain satisfied, hopeful, tasteful of understanding of hidden things and be intelligent to see the invisible beyond the visible.

sections.heading: All Secrets Not to Be Revealed
paras: I am not entitled to reveal all the details of this secret, as otherwise I would have taken you on a long journey of understanding and converted an intellectually barren place like Anjaz in Turkey into Baghdad, the great centre of learning. The place of the making of all things of God is ‘adam because, it is from this place only that He goes on granting everything. God is a Creator, and a Creator is one who creates the branches without roots and base.

chapters.title: Visible, Invisible World
chapters.subtitle: Example of the visible world which is non-existent and of the non-existent world that is visible

sections.heading: Motion of Rivers: Inferred
paras: The Great Honourable One, God, has exhibited a non-existent as existent and given a shape of non-existence of the existent. The large expanse of the ocean is kept hidden. No one can see the other side of the sea. But on the coast lines surf is visible to indicate that it is a product of the oceanic action. So also, air is invisible, but dust storm is visible. The whirlwind whirls around carrying dust particles vertically like a minaret. Otherwise, how can mud go upward on its own? You see dust going up and its particles moving about in the air as an evidence of the existence of air, but you do not see air. You see froth and scraps moving about on the surface of flowing water, which only make you know that the river is moving, otherwise without froth and scraps, you cannot see water in motion, because these cannot move other than through the motion of water. You see the froth and scrap with your eyes but recognise the rivers motion through arguments. So also, your thoughts are hidden but can be known only through the words spoken by you. Thus, we consider the non-existent as existent and the existent as non-existent which is due to the fault of our eyes.

sections.heading: Existents Disappear in Sleep; Non-Existents Appear
paras: When the eyes are impacted by sleep, they cannot see anything other than the products of thoughts and non-existing things. What we see are the images of our thoughts. They cannot see the really existing things. Thus, we are estranged in misguidance, as the realities are hidden and only thoughts are clear. Thoughts have set the non-existents into our eyes and hidden the real existents. Thus, thoughts are more dominant than actually seen objects. This is a great magic.

Power of God that He has hidden the reality from those who turn back their faces. They are shown only the left-over grassy substances and not their worth, value and truth. There are sorcerers in the world who present moonlight as fabrics, measure right before them and sell to the customers and take away their money as sale price. They swirl and turn this confusing fabric of moonlight so well and so fast that the customer falls into the trap and gives his money for it. He loses the money and later he sees that the purchased fabric has vanished from his hand. This world is like that sorcerer, and we are its customers, who buy this non-existing fabric for a price. We ask it to measure five hundred yards of cloth, produced by magician by his magic on moonlight. This is what and how you do all through your life. You lose the possessions of your life. Your wealth is lost; you got no cloth and your purse got emptied.

sections.heading: Seek God’s Help to Protect from Treacheries
paras: Therefore, you should be constantly praying to God to protect you from the mischief of those who practise secret arts, and reading the surah: Qul a‘uuzu birabbil Falaq (113) [There were witches during the days of the Prophet who used to put knots on the ropes and blow some magic spells on the knots. Such secret arts used to cause psychological terror. They may be what is called black magic or secret plotting’s, or display of false and seductive charms, or the spreading of false and secret sermons or slanders to frighten men or deter them from right action. There is a fraud in such things, but men are swayed by it. [Abdullah Yusuf Ali in The Holy Quran, page 1808]. Even in our days these are the tactics that are adopted by enemies through fake news, false propaganda, WhatsApp messages and organised treacheries, so called social media. And also diversionary activities carried on by secretly funded non-governmental organisations to distract attention from important issues to non-issues. They are so rampant and colossal that the lesser and lowly people can think of no other course than seeking the help and protection of God. This certainly yields result provided that right actions are taken. The activities of all the prophets of God have been against such evil sources which ultimately yield good results. The Math(s)navi is full of references to the prophets and also to saints. One of the objects of the Math(s)navi is the same —Translator]

Those witches used to blow upon the knots. O God, the Hearer and Responder to the grievances! Protect us from those treacherous designs. But merely praying to God is not enough. Give support to your prayer with action also, because the tongue, speaking words, is not that strong. It needs physical supports also.

sections.heading: Three Types of Friends
paras: You have got three types of friends in the world; one of whom is sincere and the other two are treacherous. Of these two types some are your friends, and the others are of your wealth and materials. The sincere friend is your good acts only. Wealth and materials collected by you do not come out of your house upon your death. But your human friends will come up to your grave only. At the time when you meet your death, your friend will speak through body language: I am not a friend of yours beyond this place. I can only stay at your grave for a little time. Your acts are your sincere friends. You may take them as your protectors because they only be with you in the depth of the grave.

chapters.title: Companian in the Grave
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the statement of the Prophet: A friend is required to be buried along with you, who should be living in your grave. If he is noble, he will honour you; and if he is mean, he will run away from you. This friend of yours is your actions and deeds. Therefore, keep them good as much as possible

sections.heading: No Learning Without Master
paras: For this reason, the noble Prophet said: No companion is more sincere than your action! If it is right, it will last for ever and if it is wrong, it will be a snake for you in your grave. your actions, earnings and the right paths cannot be found out other than through a master. Even the most lowly of the jobs which prevails very much in the world cannot be learnt other than through a master. The first thing to do in any job is first to know its ways and then to practise, so that it may be fruitful for some time even after death. Therefore, O wisemen, take the support of the noble and competent in learning about any profession. Search for the pearl in the oyster; and arts and crafts from their experts. If you come in contact with wise advisers, maintain silence, learn from them and do not be haughty with them. A tanner wearing torne, old clothes does not get lost or reduced in his nobility. A blacksmith wears torne clothes while engaged in his work of blowing air on fire but does not get his honour lost. Therefore, do not consider clothes as symbols of honour. They are symbols of pride. Remove them off when you are in the process of learning jobs. You acquire knowledge through oral teaching, but the way of learning a profession is by practical means.

sections.heading: Learning of Esoteric Matters
paras: The means of learning about esoteric matters is by remaining in the company of their masters. Neither your tongue is useful in this regard, nor your hands as in other sciences and professions. The repository of the lights of God is the heart. This cannot be achieved by reading books or by hearing lectures. This knowledge passes from the heart to heart and not from books and spoken words. A searcher for such knowledge may possess the words relating to this science, but he will still be without their understanding and connotations. This will happen only when clarifications are caused by special light on the heart. It is to emphasise on this point that the surat Inshirah, or the expansion is revealed, (which says as an address to the Prophet: “Have we not caused your bosom to dilate? Alam nashrah laka sadraka (Inshirah: 94: 1).

That is: We have given clarifications about it in your heart or bosom. We have kept all explanations and details of the matters in your heart. That is: all such esoteric aspects are placed in your heart through which you can know of the inner aspects of all things.

sections.heading: Learnings from One’s Inside (Alam Nashrah)
paras: But you are in search of all knowledge from outside or from others or through logic and intellectual discussions. All knowledge cannot be acquainted from outer sources. Searches are to be made within your inside also. You are like the place of the origin of milk, with which you have got be contented. But you go to others to draw milk from them. There is an unfathomable spring of milk within you, but you go in search of milk from small pits. You have got a way to an ocean of water, but you do not feel ashamed of taking water from small ponds.

The statement of Alam Nashrah (Have we not expanded) is not for the Prophet alone. It can be an expansion of your breast also. Instead of going into its expanse and search for knowledge, you go to others like a beggar to seek knowledge. You should concentrate upon the potentials of your heart and knock at it to know about things which others cannot reveal. You must look into it, as otherwise you will fall into the category of those about whom God has said: Laa Yubsiruuna: They do not see. (Baqarah: 2: 17).

chapters.title: God Is with You
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of ayat: He is with you wheresoever you may be: wa huwa ma ‘akum aina maa kuntum: (Hadeed: 57: 4)

sections.heading: Curtains of Ignorance
paras: There is a basket full of bread upon your head, but you are going door to door to beg for bread. Cast your attention upon your head and forget this nonsense. Go to your heart and knock at its door. Why do you knock at other doors? You are in water up to your thighs. You are ignorant of this and in search of water here and there. Bread is there upon your head and your feet in water, but you are suffering from hunger and thirst. There is flowing water in front of you and on your back, but there are walls in front of you and on your back.

The rider is sitting upon the horse, and strangely he is searching for his horse. People tell him: “What is this other than a horse under you.” But still he says: “Where is my horse.” People again tell him: “Look under you. you are sitting upon the horse.” Yet, he says: Of course, this is a horse. But has anybody seen my horse?”

There is another person, whose beloved is right before him. He is unaware of the water inspite of being in flowing water. Another is in love with something, and that thing is right before him, yet he is unaware of that thing and the details about it. This is like his knowing that pearls are to be found in the sea floor and yet he is asking. “Where is the sea?” His knowledge itself is like a wall before him, hiding the sea from his sight. His very questioning as to where it is, itself is a curtain for him. Sun’s light becomes a cloud for him that hides the sun. His defective sight is a curtain for him and the advice for removal of the wall before him becomes an obstacle for him to hear. Such being the case, cast your attention on God as these misguiding curtains and walls will make you mad. You have distributed your sense in all directions instead of casting on one thing and these useless thoughts have lost all their worth.

chapters.title: Too Many Fears and Sorrows
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the Prophet’s statement: God takes care of him who combines all his fears and sorrows in one; and God has no concern for him who has plenty of sorrows and fears and the valley in which he gets ruined

paras: Every root and thorn is drawing the water of consciousness. In such a case, how can this water of consciousness reach the fruits. When ordinary grass is drawing the water of consciousness, how can your consciousness reach up to God. You are engaged in too many unworthy issues. Therefore, you should be careful enough to cut off that useless branch of the tree and keep yourself away from its concern; to provide water to the fresh and good branch only.

sections.heading: Protect the Good, Ignore the Bad
paras: When both the branches are green and fresh, take care of the one that yields good results in the end. It may initially appear to be bad but may be capable of giving fruits. Know that water is permissible for the good one and prohibited for the bad one. You should be careful to distinguish the difference between them. Justice is in giving water to the trees. Giving water to the thorns is cruelty. Justice is in expending of the grants at the appropriate places and not to every root that sucks water. Cruelty is in expending at inappropriate place and time, as this will become a fountain of nothing but calamity. Give the grants provided by God to your wisdom and soul, but not to the instinct full of twists

Do not allow the silly problems of the worldly matters to go up to the heart. Make them ride upon the body only and not upon the heart and soul as they will spoil them. As against this, you are doing the opposite. This is like putting the burden of loads upon the head of H. Isa and allowing his donkey to pleasurably run about in the garden. Applying eyeblack in the ear is foolish. So also attempts to take the job of the heart from the body. If you are entirely a heart, you may feel proud of it and there is no need for you to feel lowly. As against this, if you are only a body, you need not go to eat sugar but take poison; in such a case, poison is profitable to the body and sugar is harmful. Such a body will be good if it is not provided with any support.

sections.heading: Subtle Differences Should Be Studied
paras: Body is the fuel for hell and therefore reduce it; and if it goes on increasing, it is better to uproot it in full. Otherwise, you will be fuel and carrier of fuel for hell both in this and that world like the wife of Abu Lahab, as stated about her in the Quran: Wamratuhu hammalatal Hatab: (Lahab: 111: 4). You may identify firewood by comparison with the branch of the lote-tree beyond which none can pass: Sidratil muntahaa: (Najm: 53: 14). [Sidrah is the Lote-tree which is thorny, but under cultivation it yields good fruits and shade, and is symbolic of heavenly bliss. Sidratil muntaha, as the highest point of esoteric knowledge beyond which none can pass, to mean that nothing can be known beyond this limit of knowledge. Knowledge beyond this is known only to Go— As explained by Abdulllah Yusuf Ali, page 1444, in the Holy Quran — Translator]

Your effort should be to catch the branch of Sidratil Muntahaa and not of a tree which is fit for firewood only, as both appear to you to be fresh and green. The root and base of this tree is only fire and smoke, but the root of that tree is upon the seventh heaven. Both are similar to look at for the ocular sense as the physical eyes are imperfect based upon wrong perception. But these are clear for the eyes of the heart, and they see everything in full and feel the difference. Put efforts well to get this as the saintly people do. Man should always put efforts to know things in full. Does not matter if you do not have the legs to walk, but be shaking yourself so as to see the efficient and deficient from the sides. Because movement is the key to prosperity and efforts and movements will certainly cause benefit to the heart.

chapters.title: Lowly People Search for Popularity
chapters.subtitle: There is a Quatrain which says: If you walk on the path, more paths will be shown If you annihilate yourself, you will go towards everlastingness If you make yourself lowly, you will be so large as to feel the world narrow Then, you will be shown things beyond yourself without yourself

paras: Zulaikha, who seduced H. Yusuf (Joseph) shut all the doors to hold him inside, but Yusuf shook himself and found out the place to go out. When he relied upon God and put efforts, lock of the door opened and the way was clear.

sections.heading: Ways Open for Searchers
paras: Though there appears to be no passage for escape in the world, yet one should run about recklessly like Yusuf, so that the lock may open, and the route of escape may appear; and there be a way for you toward La-makaan. (Meaning of La-makaan has been already explained in previous pages). You are under trial in the world. You came into the world, but you did not see the route through which you came. You have come from a place which was your country. But you do not know anything about its way. Just because you do not know the way, do not ever say that there is no way. Be also sure that we have all to go back through the same way. You go about happily on the right and left in your dream without knowing where to go. But you do not know as to where is the way for that field. Shut your eyes and submit yourself to yourself in full and then you will see yourself in that old place from which you came.

sections.heading: Petty Minds Search for Popularity
paras: But when you shut your eyes, for the purpose of seeing only yourself, you will still have hundreds of other eyes and situations of unconsciousness of which you are not aware. These become curtains to prevent you from seeing that left back world of your origin. While you shut these two physical eyes of yours, you still have four hidden eyes of love for your customers upon whom you seek to maintain your leadership and dominance. You are so much engaged with your customers that even in your dream you look for them, just as a silly owl which does not see anything other than ruins. Every moment you search for customers here and there. This is because, you do not have anything worthy to sell. What you have are only meaningless words. You do all this to become famous among the people. Only he searches for popularity among the people, who does not possess anything worthwhile. One who has worthwhile things does not go in search of people just like a well-fed man does not go in search of food, or like a person who has stocks of food in his bag.

chapters.title: Talking to the Senseless
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a person who proclaimed of his prophethood. He was told: “what have you eaten, that you behave like a fool and talk senseless.” He said: “If I had found out something to eat, I would have eaten and not talked foolish and non-sense. This is because every good thing spoken to the worthless fellows, becomes senseless, even though he may be appointed by God to say what I am saying”

paras: One fellow was telling among the people that he was a prophet of God, and he was greater than all other prophets. People caught hold of his neck and took him to the king telling that he claims to be a prophet from God. People gathered around him like ants and locusts to find out as to what his tricks and spread-out-nets were, saying: “If he says that he is a prophet as he has come from the world of non-existents (‘adam), then we are also prophets and honourable because we have also come from ‘adam’. That is our native place, and we are only journeymen here. There is nothing special about you. That simpleton said: “O blind, senseless, foolish fellows! You cannot realise that you have come here with your fate, blindness and ignorance. You have come here like sleeping babies. You were not aware of your destination and your way to it. You have passed through many midway stations in unconsciousness and without observing the ups and downs of the way. But, we prophets, have traversed the way in full wakefulness and pleasure from the place without the five senses and six dimensions toward this place of five sense and six dimension. (That is from non-material world to the material world). We have seen our destination from its roots and foundation, like the guides with all awareness and information about it.”

sections.heading: Soft Treatment Brings Out Truth
paras: The people told the king to put him in the wrench, so that none like him may ever talk like him. The king found that he was very weak and frail, so frail that he would die with a single slap on his face. Such a fellow cannot be beaten or thrashed, as his body is brittle like glass. “But I shall talk to him mildly to find out as to why he talks nonsense rebelliously. Because harshness is of no use here. Mildness will give the desired result of his reasons just as the snake comes out of its pit with soft tunes.

He made the people go away from him, as the king was of very soft and joyous nature. Then, he made him sit by his side and asked about the place to which he belonged, and about his profession and place of residence. He said: “O king I belong to the place of safety and security that is high above and came to this lowly, dishonourable place. I do not have any place of residence, nor a friend. Where has the moon made a house upon the earth?” The king jokingly asked him: “What food did you eat today and what do you have for tomorrow’s breakfast. Are you hungry? What did you eat for breakfast that you are so intoxicated, boasting and full of pride?”

sections.heading: Hunger Leads to Talking
paras: He said: “If I had fresh or stale bread with me, why would I make a claim of prophethood. Making a proclamation of prophethood among these fellows is as hard as searching for a heart in a mountain. Nobody has searched for wisdom and heart in the rocks and mountains. None has searched among them for a man who has the sense to understand subtle points. Everyone says the same thing that you say and laughs at the ignorance of others considering himself to be wise like you. Where is this community, and what concern does it have for the God’s message? How can anybody hope to see life in a stone? On the contrary, if you carry the message of a woman, they will place their gold and silver coins and keep their heads before you. They do like this if you say: there is in such and such a place a lovely woman who had fallen in love with you. She knows you very well.

“But on the contrary, if you take the message of God, sweet like honey telling them: “O men of promise and commitment, come over to God, march from the world of death and destruction toward the world of plenty, with scope for everlasting life; and not to put yourself to death in the world and go to the world of everlasting life, they will go after your blood, life and head. Not out of the desire to protect the honour of their religion and faith, but because of their close connections with their houses and properties. Hearing such things appear very bitter to them.”

chapters.title: Why People Hate Godly Persons
chapters.subtitle: Reasons for the enmity and dislike of the common people for the godly persons, who call them toward God and to provide to them the water of everlasting life

paras: Bandage on the wound of a donkey is sticking hard and if you pluck it piece by piece, the donkey will certainly start kicking due to pain. That man is in peace who does not try to remove its bandage. And in particular, when there are fifty wounds and every bandage is stuck hard with sticky, dried up puss.

sections.heading: Possessions Are Bandages
paras: A man’s house and property are like bandages, which are upon the wounds of greed. One who has more greed has more wounds. The house of the owl is located in ruins. It does not know of the beauty and greatness of cities like Baghdad and Tabas. If a royal falcon after passing through its path speaks of the grand affairs of the king, of the capital city, its gardens and streams with all details, then every owl becomes its enemy and laughs at it. They all will say: “The falcon has brought old narratives and is speaking of nonsense and boastings.” They are old and it is they that are everlastingly, rotten. Otherwise, the information given by the falcon would make them fresh and different. It would give life to old dead bodies and provide the crown of wisdom and the light of faith.

sections.heading: Love of Petty Things
paras: Do not keep yourself away from the soul-Inspiring beloved, as He will make you ride upon a grand horse. Do not keep your head away from the One who would grant a crown to you and raise your head up, Who will open hundreds of knots from the feet of the heart. To whom am I tell all this? Who is the living person in this village? Who is the one who can run toward the life-giving water? You are the one to run away from love upon receiving a single disgrace, because you do not know anything about love, other than having heard this word. Love has hundreds of styles and prides. It is available only after meeting with hundreds of escaping and avoiding styles. As love is honest and sincere, it is a buyer of honesty and sincerity. It never ever cares to look at the insincere. Man is like a tree, and sincerity is like its root. The root requires to be well nurtured and protected with great efforts. Insincere promise is like the rotten root, cut off from pleasing fruit. Branches and leaves of the tree may be green, but they get no greenery if the root is bad. On the contrary, if the leaves have gone dry but the root is intact, then hundreds of fresh leaves will sprout later. Do not remain contented with this much of knowledge but go to fulfil your promise to seek more. Knowledge is like the rind and sincere promise is like the pulp of the fruit.

chapters.title: Jealousy of the Vicious
chapters.subtitle: To explain that when a man of vicious character settles down on viciousness and looks at the impacts of the wealth of nobility of the noble people, he adopts the character of Satan and comes in the way of their generosity out of jealousy and desires like Satan; because one whose harvest is burnt down desires that the harvest of all others should also be burnt, as stated in the Quran: Do you not see one who forbids a votary when he truns to pray?: Arayatallizii yauhaa, ‘abdan izaa sallaa?: (Alaq: 96: 9-10)

paras: When you find honest persons useful to others, you become jealous of them like Satan. A man with sickly nature and temperament does not like that any other person should be healthy and fresh. If you do not want to have the jealous character of Satan, you may go away from the door of false claims but go toward sincerity. If you do not have sincerity in you, do not take even its name as any talk about it generally involves false claims and pride. Your remaining silent results in the entry of sincerity in your heart and its increase. It becomes the pulp of your good qualities. Instead of keeping it within yourself, if you start speaking of it, its pulp gets out. Therefore, do not allow it to go out and keep it in full within yourself.

sections.heading: Give Little to God, Get More
paras: Thoughts of a less speaking person are weighty and like the pulp. Your talking is like the rind of the fruit. When the pulp of talking increases in size due to your talking, the pulp of thought gets reduced (as talking and thinking are different). Increase of rind results in decrease of pulp and its reduction increases the pulp. You may see this fact in three ripe fruits: apricots, almonds and pistachios. One who commits sins becomes a devil and becomes jealous of the wealth of nobility of others. You may recall to your mind that you have given a promise of sincerity to God at the occasion of alast. If you remain honest to the promise, God will take care of your promise. But you have shut your eyes towards the promise of sincerity. Have you not heard this ayat: Remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me and reject Me not: Fazkuruuni azkurukum washkuruulii walaa takfuruuni: (Baqara: 2: 152). You may keep your ear towards this ayat: awfuubi ‘ahdii, uufi bi ‘ahdikum: fulfil your covenant, I shall fulfil my covenant: (Baqara: 2: 40). You may keep your promise and God will keep His. Keeping the promise and giving of a loan to God is like giving their benefits to ourselves like putting a seed in farmland. This does not result in the increase of anything for the land but brings riches to the landowner. Here also is a point to ponder that God has brought out the seed from the world of non-existence in the form of a general grant. You eat all the grains but bring one as a seed, to plead to God to provide more such grains.

sections.heading: Prayer Combined with Action and Sincerity
paras: Be wise enough! Stop making dry supplications. Spread the seeds and then pray for the trees. A supplication without action is of no use. It is like a rotten seed. If you do not have the seed, you are helpless. In such a situation you should make a sincere supplications pleading with pain of deprivation, when God will grant you dates, as this prayer is highly sincere. This, he had granted to H. Maryam, as she had pain but not the seed. The Master of Creativity converted her pain into a fresh date-palm. This was because, she was sincere and therefore God rewarded her with hundreds of grants.

That group of people with sincerity were provided with excellence over all other groups. Seas became their protectors as happened in the case of H. Musa and H. Yunus. Rivers and mountains were made obedient to them. All the four elements (air, fire, water and earth) became their obedient servants. Large fields could not bear their secrets. There were great miracles for them so as to show their might to the rejectors. They had such hidden miracles which could not be understood by senses and could not be explained in words. They possessed such qualities which last for ever continuingly, without interruption and going back. Rather they are always in progress because their Grantor is Generous.

chapters.title: Need of Law to Cut Sins

sections.heading: O Provider of Food, Courage, and Constancy! Prevent the People from the Commission of Mistrust. Provide Constancy to the Hearts of the People in Respect of Jobs Which Require to Be Held on; and Dont Make Them Turn Away from Their Commitments and Give Life to Their Hearts. Give Them Patience, Make the Pan of Their Balance Heavy on the Doomsday and Protect Them from Buffoons. O Generous! Protect Them from Jealousy so That They May Not Become Like the Rejectable People
Vicious Role of Jealousy
paras: People burn themselves in the fire of jealousy for the sake of perishable materials — wealth and physical bodies, possessed by others. Look at the kings marching their armies against their own kith and kin out of jealousy to finish them. Lovers for the sake of petty dolls, go against each other’s blood and commit murders. Read the story of the love of Ramin for the beautiful waise, and of Khusro and Shireaen, and see what those fools did out of jealousy. This resulted in the destruction of both the lover and the beloved, as they were worthless: so also, their object of love. But God Who is Absolute and not liable for destruction, destroys the destructible beloved and makes another destructible fall in love with her and get destroyed. Love itself becomes a cause of destruction of both. The lover says that he has lost his heart for the beloved, yet possess a heart full of jealousy, which causes anxiety to both the existents and non-existents. Women who are generally kinder and more affectionate feel highly jealous of co-wives and go after each other’s life. When such is their case, in what place do men stand who are generally hard-hearted. If the law were not to provide the means to trap men, just as jinn’s are supposed to be imprisoned into bottles through magic spells, everyone would tear the body of another. Law provides the means to eliminate mischiefs first. It traps the mischief maker in prison like the imprisoning the devil in bottle.

sections.heading: Only Law Settles Disputes
paras: Law demands a claimant to produce evidence and if he does not have evidence, he is asked to swear his case upon oath. This oath is a spell to trap the devil in the bottle. This is like a balance that pleases both the opposing parties, and both agree with each other in its efficacy in seriousness or necessity. There cannot be any other convenient method. Therefore, consider the law to be a measure and balance with which two opponents get rid of their enmity and quarrels. They cannot get rid of opposition and quarrels if there is no such a balance imposed upon them; as otherwise, they will resort to treacheries and cruelties. Thus, you are personified cruelty, jealousy and quarrelsomeness in this deadly, vicious and unfaithful world.

sections.heading: Jealousy for Non-Material Qualities
paras: When this is the case of jealousy in respect of the material world for you, consider the case of the jealousy of men and jinns in respect of the possessions of the other world’s prosperity and non-material wealth. Devils are in jealousy since long and they never remain without committing misguidance even for a short time. Those children of Adam who sowed the seeds of sins have also become like devils out of jealousy. Read in the Quran that the devils among men have been converted into the species of the devils by God. When the devil feels himself to be helpless in placing turmoil, he seeks the support of such men telling them: “You are our friends, come to our help, join with us and show your solidarity with us.” When both of them jointly misguide someone, both these devils feel immensely pleased. And if someone saves himself and goes higher in faith, they feel jealous and cry upon their failure. Both of them bite those, out of jealousy who have been shown good manners by his master.

chapters.title: Grades of Inspiration and Grants
chapters.subtitle: The King’s questioning with the claimant of false prophethood: What does a real prophet, upon the establishment of his prophethood, possess, which he can grant to someone in his company and service, other than mere words of oral advice

paras: The king asked him: What did you gain by inspiration? Or what does the real prophet get? Or what does he give to anyone through his talks except that you should do or should not do this or that? What profit does one get by remaining in his company or by rendering service. And what elevation does one reach up to by totally devoting himself to him?

sections.heading: Different Levels of Inspiration
paras: The false prophet said: “What is it that he has not received, or which is the wealth that is not provided to him? I admit that the inspiration that I received is not from the lord of treasure, yet it is not less than the inspiration upon the heart of the bee. As it is said that the bee was inspired by the lord consequent upon which, its dwelling was filled with sweet honey. The ayat is: wa awhaa rabbuka ilannahli anittikhizii minal jibaali buyuutan wa minal shajari was mimma ya ‘rishuuna: And your Lord taught the bee to build its cells in the hills, on trees and in men’ habitations: (Nahl: 16: 68). And the bees with the light of this inspiration from God filled the world with honey and wax, for candles of light.

The Lord’s saying: wa laqad karramnaa banii Adama wa hamalnaahum fil barri wal bahri: we have honoured the sons of Adam; provided them with transport on land and see: (Bani Isra’iil: 17: 70). This goes at a higher level. How can this inspiration be lesser than the one given to the bee?

sections.heading: Sincere Devotees Drink from Kauth(s)ar
paras: Perhaps you have not read this address to the prophet: Innaa a’tainaka alkawth(s)ar: to you have we granted the fountain of abundance: (Kauth(s)ar: 108: 1). If you have read it, then why are you dry and thirsty? [Kauth(s)ar is the heavenly fountain of unbounded grace and knowledge, mercy and goodness, truth and wisdom, spiritual power and insight, which was granted to the holy Prophet, the man of God, and in some degree or other, to all men and women who are sincere devotees of God. The fountain quenches the highest spiritual thirst of man: it confers overflowing benefits of all kinds — Abdullah Yusuf Ali, p 1798]. Or perhaps, you are a Pharoah and your Kauth(s)ar is like the Nile, which became blood and distasteful for you and made you sick.

sections.heading: Follow the Sincere Follower of Muhammad
paras: Repent and get disgusted of every enemy who is not provided with the water of Kauth(s)ar so that you may not be impacted by him. And whoever has quenched of his thirst with the water of Kauth(s)ar, is of the nature of Muhammad. Follow his conduct, so that you may become one among those who love God, as He has with Him an apple from the tree of Muhammad, he has said: whoever loved for the sake of God gets his faith fully accomplished. One who comes with dry lips from the fountain of Kauth(s)ar may be considered as an enemy like fever and death. This is for the reason that he is an Abu Jahal or Abu Lahab. Run away from him so that you may not be caught in difficulties. Such a person may be your father or mother. Yet he is one to drink your blood. Learn this from H. Ibrahim as it was his father of whom he was disgusted first (as he was an idol maker and worshipper). So that you may stand before God as one, who is wrathful with others who are away from the path of God. So that your love for God may be only for Him and not out of envy for other’s love. So that you are not put into troubles. Until you say with full sincerity: “there is no God”, and then continue to say: “except Allah”, you will not enter into this path of sincerity.

chapters.title: Narration of Love and Sincerity
chapters.subtitle: Story of a Lover who narrated before his beloved about his services, faithfulness; and counting his long nights to separation like of those: “their limbs do forsake their beds of sleep: fatajaafaa junuubuhum ‘anil madhaaji‘i: (Sajda: 32: 16). And of the lack of his necessities and the thirst of his soul for a long time, and further said: “I know of nothing other than this service, and if there is any other service required may be told to me, which I shall be obedient to do first as H. Ibrahim’s entry into fire and H. Yunus’s entry into the mouth of the crocodile; and getting killed seventy times like Jarji’is and becoming blind like H. Shu‘aib due to constant weeping and also of the sincerity and faithfulness and uncountable sacrifices of the prophets; and the beloved’s answer thereto

paras: A man told his beloved by narrating his acts and services for her that: “I did such and such acts for you and I was hit by arrows and spears in this struggle. I lost my wealth, strength and name, and in your love. I had to meet many failures. No morning found me in sleep or in happiness and by no evening did I get anything worthwhile.”

sections.heading: Lover’s Narrations Never End
paras: He was narrating one after another, about the bitter residue of drinks that he had drunk. All this, he narrated not as his graces for her but only as evidences of his love for her. One hint is enough for the wise to understand, but the thirst of one in love does not end at that. Without hesitation, he went on repeating just as the fish that never gets satisfied with the hints about water but goes on swimming without getting tired. He spoke of his continuing pain in hundreds of ways. And I have not narrated even one of his lamentations and grievances in full.

sections.heading: Cases of Lovers
paras: He had a fire within his inside, but he did not know as to what it was. But he was weeping and shedding tears like a candle in the pain of burning fire. After crying about all this, he told her: “all this happened from my side. But you may tell me of anything else as a good friend. I am prepared to do what all you tell me to do. I have readied my head and feet to obey your commands. I shall do everything that you ask me to do, whether it is to jump into fire like H. Ibrahim, or shedding my own blood like H. Yahya, or to become blind due to constant weeping like H. Shuaib, or to enter into the mouth of the fish like H. Yunus, or to get imprisoned in a well like H. Yusuf, or to become a destitute like H. Isa, son of Maryam. I shall not turn my face away from you, nor shall I go away from you. My soul and body are at your command.”

The beloved told him: “You have done all this. But you may open your ears and go deep into the matter. You have not done that which is the foundation and root of friendship and love. What you have done are only their branches.”

sections.heading: Real Love: Annihilation
paras: He asked her: “Tell me what the root of love and friendship is?” She said: “It is dying and getting annihilated. You did everything but did not die. You are still alive. You may die if you are one to sacrifice life for friendship. If you die in this manner, you will get perfect life and your name will remain alive till the doomsday.”

When that unconscious lover heard this, he too a long, cold sigh from his body and soul. He laid down and gave up his life, with all pleasure, and joy, and offered his head like a flower. That smile of his face will last for ever, just like the wisdom and soul of a lover of God without any hesitation.

The light of the moon never gets polluted whether it falls upon good or bad things. It remains unaffected and clean and returns to the moon just as the light of wisdom and soul returns to God. Cleanliness is a trust of moon light, even when it passes upon the dirt of the ways. These dirts and pollutions of the ways do not pollute it. Sunlight heard the command of God. Come back to your Lord, — well pleased (yourself) and well pleased unto Him: Irji ‘ii ilaa rabbiki radhiyatin mardhiyatin: (Fajr: 89: 28), and instantly, it returned to its place of origin. It did not carry any marks of furnaces nor of the colours of the gardens. Light of the eyes returns to the eyes; and fields and forests which were seen by it remain only in imagination. As this pure light passed upon this ruined world, it returned without its impacts to its source. And eyes continued to wait for seeing more and more for the forest of the eyes.

chapters.title: Cries During Salat
chapters.subtitle: A person enquired with a Scholar and ‘Aarif, (knower of God): “If someone while in salat takes a loud sigh and cries loudly, will his Salat go wrong or not?” It was answered: “Tears of grief are called as the water of the eyes as well as the water resulting from the impacts of what is seen. If the crier has seen God with enthusiasm or cried with the grief of sins the Salat will not go wrong, rather it becomes perfect as there is no Salat without full attention of the heart. Laa salaata illa bihudhuril qalbi. On the contrary, if it is due to physical pain or separation from children, the salat goes wrong as its real purpose is to keep away the body and children like H. Ibrahim; that he sacrificed his son for the perfect Salat and offered his body to the fire of Nimrod. This is the conduct that is ordered for the Prophet Mustafa: Follow the ways of Ibrahim the true in faith fa ttab i millata Ibrahim Hamifan: (Nahl: 16: 123) And: there is for you an excellent example to follow in Ibrahim: Qad kaanat lakum uswatun hasanatun fii Ibrahim: (Mumtahana: 60: 4)

sections.heading: Crying for God
paras: A person asked a mufti: If a person cries loudly in Salat; whether his Salat would be void or it would be permissible and perfect? He said: Why is the water of the eyes called as the “seeing water”. It is this water that keeps the eyes wet and living. You have to see as to what the eyes saw, and why it shed tears and cried. What has the water of the eyes seen behind the eyeball that it started shedding tears in the form of a stream. If it is due to the enthusiasm of seeing of God or due to sense of shame and humility upon his sins, and due to the fear of God, it is very good as this water extinguishes the fire in you and brings about coolness to heart. In such a situation, the Salat attains perfectness. This will inevitably result in nearness with God. If that committed person sees the other world, his cries decorate and beautify his Salat.

sections.heading: Crying for Self
paras: And if it is due to sickness of the body, its pain and grief, it results in the breaking of the thread as well as the spinning wheel. If he cries out of the sorrow for the children, it means that his soul and heart suffered the pain. Such a Salat is not worth two grains of millet, as his heart is engaged in things other than God. This renders his Salat null and void without doubt. His crying has no good result. Because the main object of Salat is to ignore the physical body and sincerity for it, and to keep away one’s own self and one’s children. Learn this lesson from H. Ibrahim and sacrifice your children for God. Keep your body on the fire of Nimrod. The sum and substance are that there is much difference between this crying and that crying.

chapters.title: Passing from Imitation to Reality
chapters.subtitle: A disciple approached a shaikh (old man). By shaikh I do not mean an old man in age but one senior in wisdom and gnosis, even if he is in a cradle like H. Isa and in a children’s school like H. Yahya. He found the shaikh weeping and he also followed him and wept. After this he came out. Another disciple more aware of the situation of the shaikh followed him from behind and said: My brother, I tell you, do not, for God’s sake, think and say that the shaikh wept and you too wept. [Because to come to the state of the shaikh, you will have to struggle hard and pray for thirty years without being seen by others and passthrough different ways, rivers full of crocodiles, lofty mountains full of leopards and lions. Upon this you may reach the shaikh’s level to weep, or you may even not reach. If you reach, you should be thankful as the noble Prophet had said: the earth was folded up for me and I saw its easts and wests. That will be an occasion of thanksgiving as it is a weeping with the total attention toward God. What you did was only imitation

paras: One disciple went nearer to the elderly shaikh, who was crying and weeping. Looking at him thus, the disciple also started crying and tears started flowing from his eyes.

A man with good ears, laughs once and the deaf man twice, when he hears friends exchanging jokes. He laughs for the first time artificially and joins others. He laughs without knowing the reasons for the others laughing. Then he makes enquiries about the reason for laughing and upon hearing the reason, he once again laughs. The blind follower is also like the deaf with the pleasures that he has in his head.

sections.heading: Imitative Action and Intentional Action
paras: Reflection of the shaikh is a fountain from the shaikh. Gains and pleasures of the disciples are from him and not otherwise. Reflection of the shaikh is his followership, which is a result of his seeing the shaikh’s support and pleasures. This is like a basket filled with water floating on water and reflection of light in the mirror. If the disciples think that their pleasure is of their own, it will be wrong. When the basket comes out of water, it will be clear that the water was of the stream and not its own. So also, when the moon sets, mirror will know that its brightness was actually the moon’s reflection.

When the disciple hears the command to get up, as was given to the Prophet, he gets up. The command was: “Stand to prayer by night, but not all night”: Qumillaila illaa qaliilan: (Muzzammil: 73: 2). This command will open his eyes. He will smile for the second time, just as second true light that comes at the true dawn after semi-light of the false dawn in the morning time. [Well before sunrise, there will be a semi-bright light on the eastern horizon called false down. Later there is greater brightness, which is called true dawn]. He will laugh at his own false laugh also, which was due to his blind followership. He will understand that his realising of truth was far away, and he was unaware of the truth and the secrets behind it. That is, in his blindness, he was only expressing his pleasures and joys from a long distance. There was much difference between what he was thinking about and what the reality was. His slow and imperfect sense showed only imperfect scenes.

sections.heading: Exoteric and Esoteric Knowledge
paras: A child in the path of the seeking of knowledge of truth cannot be capable enough like grown up men. He cannot know where his thinking is and where is the truth? He cannot think like an elderly man. The child thinks of milk and foster mother, or of currants, apricots, or of crying and shouting. A blind follower is like a sick child, even if he has some evidences and arguments. He cannot go into the depths of matters and ponder deeply on arguments. He has no insight to know the truths. That capacity which can act as the eye black of his inner eyes is lacking in him, and as such, he can only talk of difficult points without knowing their meanings. O blind follower, you are living in the city of Bukhara which is known for exoteric learnings of well-known learned scholars. Come out of its grandeur and go toward humility and seclusion so as to become a strong knower of matters, as strong as a lion in physical vigour. In such a case you will see another Bukhara and see those scholars of Bukhara as those who have no capacity to understand. They are like fast runners on land, but when they enter into the river, they become helpless like cripples.

God has said that He has honoured the sons of Adam; provided them with transport on land and sea: wa laqad karram naa bani adama wa hamalnaahum fil barri wal bahri: (Asraa: 17: 70). They are walking on the land and see only apparent things (exoteric things). This is the meaning of providing transport on land. Transport on the sea means the seeking of the knowledge of esoteric matters. Those who go into the sea are certainly braver than others. God graces them very much. But you are caught in doubts and imaginations and become bent under their weight.

chapters.title: Rest of the Affair of the Blind Follower

sections.heading: Tears Shed by Lovers
paras: That simple disciple also started weeping like the other honourable one is in blind followership. In blind followership, he was like the deaf fellow. He saw someone weeping and he followed. After weeping for long, he saluted him and left. Another closer disciple went after him. He said: “O uninformed fellow, you looked at the shaikh’s weeping and also started weeping like the clouds. You are a sincere follower and want to gain something by blind followership. But do not say that you cried because the shaikh cried and you became one like him. By saying so, you are degrading the esteem of the shaikh. Your crying in ignorance and followership and without certainty cannot be, like that of that great honest shaikh. Do not consider your crying as his, because there is a great distance between them. His crying is after struggles and efforts for thirty years. He has reached a spiritual stage, where wisdom can never go. There are a hundred more stages for wisdom to reach that level. Do not consider wisdom to be unaware of those difficult stages.

sections.heading: Tears Shed by Lovers
paras: The weeping of the shaikh is not due to fear of hell or for the joys of paradise, but it is purely in the love of God. Lightless eyes cannot see this. His laughter and cries are only due to the love of God, which have nothing to do with wisdom and sense. The water of his eyes has already seen Him. But a blind man’s eye has no such water to see. It is no eye at all. What such a lover of God sees cannot be touched either by wisdom or by senses. Night cannot see the happenings of the day; because when day arrives, night runs away. Mosquito flies far away when the pleasurable wind starts blowing and therefore, it cannot know of the pleasures of the morning in fresh air.

When the eternal things arrive, the created things become worthless, and therefore, the created things cannot know of the eternal. [The eternal wipes out the created things which get highly perturbed, and later the eternal makes the creations like itself. If you want to know more about these matters, you may take a hundred examples, because I cannot explain all those details, as I do not have much time. The eternal are like ideas, which are mental and non-material. They have no limits. Tangible material objects come out of them. Again, the tangibles give rise to more ideas, which result in further creations. The process goes on and on for ever. Tangibly created things get destroyed, and replace new, but the ideas never. This is one example —Translator]

sections.heading: Abbreviated Letters of Quran
paras: The Abbreviated Letters of the Quran like Alif- Lam-Miim and Haa miin contain so much hidden information as the staff of H. Musa. Though other letters are apparently like these letters, but they do not contain those qualities which the Abbreviated Letters have. These Abbreviated Letters are eternal and other letters are created. A person may hold a staff in his hand to follow H. Musa’s example while speaking, but it can never be like H. Musa’s staff. Breath of H. Isa is not like other breaths, which come out in joy and sorrow. These Abbreviated Letters have come to humans from the Master of humans (God). Every independent letter like Alif and Lam cannot be like the combined Abbreviated Letters. This cannot be identified by the eyes. This requires to be seen by the soul. Though they are in the combination form of independent letters, yet their combination is not made by the people.

sections.heading: H. Muhammad’s Body
paras: Prophet Muhammad is made of flesh and skin similar to any other man’s body. Everybody has flesh skin and bones, but its making is not like the making of H. Muhammad’s body. Such miracles came about in its making that all other makings fell flat before it. Similar is the combining of the letters Haa and Miim in the Quran which are very highly elevated while others are lowly. The making of his body brings about life just as the bugle of soor brings about on the doom’s day.

sections.heading: Contents of Abbreviated Letters: Haa Miim
paras: God has put such impacts in these word, that become pythons to tear of the sea. The Abbreviated Letters Haa-Miim are like H. Musa’s staff granted by God. Its appearance is like the appearance of other letters, but the roundness of the bread is far away from the roundness of moon.

The cries, laughings and talkings of the shaikh, and his understandings, morals and makings are quite different. So also, his wisdom, imaginations and feelings. These are not his own but are the makings of God. As the foolish look at and understand the apparent affairs, their intricacies and subtleties are hidden from them. Inevitably they are hidden from the objectives and the realities. Seconds are lost in the degree of the circle or in the time of an hour. There is no end to this talk. Let us see what that maid did with the donkey of the mistress.

chapters.title: Misuse and Misunderstandings
chapters.subtitle: Story of a maid who used to have sex with her mistress’s donkey and had taught it to have sex like men by fixing a pumpkin on its penis to limit the length for penetration. Her mistress came to know of it but did not see of the pumpkin to limit the size. She sent the maid away on a far-off errand and had sex with the donkey without the pumpkin and died in disgrace. The maid returned soon and found and started crying: O my soul the light of my eyes, you saw the penis but not the pumpkin. You saw one part but not the whole. All imperfect things are accursed. God has said: It is no fault in the blind nor in one born lame, nor in one afflicted with sickness: laisa ‘alal a ‘maa harajun walaa ‘alal a ‘riji harajun wa laa ‘alal mariidhi harajun: (Nuur: 24: 61). No fault is spoken of in respect of the sin but not in respect of God’s curse, wrath and contempt

paras: A maid lay a donkey upon herself because of the sufferings she had due of excess of sexual craze and passions. The donkey became habituated to sex and learned to do it like men. That cunning maid had fixed a dried hollowed pumpkin of suitable size on the donkey’s penis. That old maid used to dress it with this pumpkin so that only half of the penis might penetrate. If the entire penis were to enter, it would tear her womb and intestines. The donkey became weak, and its owner was anxious upon this. She showed the donkey to the shoer and enquired about the cause of its weakness and getting thin. He found out no inner or outer cause, and the reason could not be known to anyone. She became curious and herself went on searching for the reason.

One’s life should always be a slave of searching as a searching soul reaches success. When she started searching for the donkey’s condition, she found the maid sleeping under it. When she further keenly observed, the maid was under the donkey and the donkey above her. She found this situation from the holes of the door. She found this to be a fascinating situation. The donkey was having sex with the maid in a way that men do with women in a usual and careful manner. She got jealous and said: if this is possible, I am more entitled to do it as the donkey is mine. The donkey is well trained and disciplined. The dining sheet is spread out with dishes and the lamp brightened to start eating.

She knocked the door as if unaware of what was happening telling the maid: “how long do you take to sweep the house.” This was only to impress upon her that she was unaware of her acts. She asked her to open the door as she would like to get in. she remained silent and did not say anything more because of the secret desire creeping in her. The maid set aright and hid all the things of her affair and opened the door. She pretended a sullen face, and her eyes were full of tears, her lips hanging down as if she was fasting. She had a broom in her hand to pretend that she was sweeping the stable. With the broom in her hand, she opened the door. The mistress said to herself under the lip: “How cunning, you have made your face bitter holding the broom in hand! Why is the donkey away from grass heap? With only half job done the donkey was in anger and profusely shaking his organ with eyes toward the door expecting your return.” All this said under her lips and hid from the maid, but still not angry for all that happened, taking her as helpless and in difficult circumstances.

Then she told her to put her mantle on her head and go to so and so’s house and give her message full of so many points, which I have skipped to narrate to shorten the story of the two women. You may also not bother about them and take into consideration the sum and substance of the story that, that domestic old women sent the maid out to meet her own purpose. After sending her out to meet an object she was in great torpor in an excitement of sexual pleasure. She shut the door and told to herself: “I have found out seclusion and I shout in thankfulness that I got rid of a problem in a very cheap manner. In her torpor, her sexual excitement increased by a thousand times, and she was highly anxious with the fire of sexual urge with the donkey.

sections.heading: Sexual Urge Blinds the Heart
paras: What a peculiar sexual craze of the women, which made her utterly foolish. Making a fool of a duffer is not strange and rare. Desires and sexual urge render the heart blind and deaf to such an extent that the ferocious wolf appears as innocent Yusuf, and fire appears as light. Many intoxicated by this fire and light consider their own selves as absolute light. The only exception is the one who having been absorbed by God comes to the proper understanding, and the pages of his misunderstood matter are turned over, so as to make him know that those thoughts are fiery, and last for a short time. Greed presents bad things as good. Nothing is so calamitous in the path of knowing of truth as sexual urge. Lakhs of well-known good people are put to disgrace by it. Lakhs of wise persons have been turned into fools. Her sexual urge presented the donkey as one as handsome as Yusuf of Egypt. What else can that rebel do? His spells make dung appear as honey. When such ugly things appear as beautiful how more beautiful, the beautiful be made to appear.

sections.heading: Sexual Urge Blinds the Heart
paras: Sexual urge arises out of food. Therefore, eat less to keep it under control or go after marriage to protect yourself from mischief. After you eat nourishing food, it will take you toward the women’s apartment. This is inevitable as its expenditure is required to meet the income of urges. Marriage acts, as the saying of La howla wala quwwata: No movement and strength except with Allah, the Elevated and Great. This will not allow the devil to put you in difficulties. You should go for marriage soon, if you are greedy of eating much. As otherwise, the cat will come and catch hold of the tail. You should immediately keep a heavy load on the donkey when it resorts to jumping high and low. This is what you should do with your desires and passions to keep them under control. Do not consider its fire to be cold and do not go around it and maintain your wisdom and sense. When you do not know how to deal with cooking, do not resort to it as both the embers of fire and the cauldron would be lost. You should keep cold water and knowledge of cooking while cooking as when the contents of the cauldron boil. You may sprinkle cold water to control the boiling contents from spilling over. Without knowing the profession of blacksmith, if you go near its fire, you get the hairs of your head and beard burnt.

sections.heading: Sexual Urge Blinds the Heart
paras: That woman shut the door and dragged the donkey toward her in all joy and finally tasted a bad result. She dragged it in the middle of the house and lay flat under the donkey upon the bench in the way she had seen the maid doing to meet her object. The donkey penetrated its penis into her, and this set a fire within her. The well-trained donkey pressed the lady under itself up to its testicles and the lady instantly died. With the piercing penis of the donkey, her liver tore off, the intestines broke away from each other. The lady fell down on one side, and the bench on the other side. She lost her breath and met her death. The flat floor of the house was full of blood and the lady lay upon it upside down. She met her calamitous time and died. Look at this! You have heard of disgraceful deaths of a hundred types. Have you ever heard of a martyr of the penis of the donkey? You may hear about the penalty of humiliation in this life as stated in the Quran: Linuziiqahum ‘azaabil khizi fil hayatid duniya: (Ha-Mim: 41: 16). But do not meet such humiliation and sacrifice your life.

sections.heading: Man’s Bestial Self Is a Donkey
paras: Know this: this bestial self of man is a donkey. It is full of defects and remaining under its control is all the more mean and defective. If you meet your death in the indulgence of your vicious self, you may know that you are like that woman. God has given the character of a donkey to our vicious self, and as such, it makes its shape as that of its character. If a man dies in the stage of life of indulgence to the dictation of his self, he will meet with a humiliation worse than that of this lady on the doomsday. His secrets will be revealed then. Therefore, for God’s sake, keep yourself away from the body that is like a donkey. God warned the rejectors with the fear of fire, but they said: “Fire is better than the disgrace of accepting what the Prophet says and subordinating themselves to his advice.” But God said: “No. Fire is the root of all disgraces, like the fire that set that lady on fire. She did not take the morsel of food as per the size of the passage of her throat due to her greed, and that bigger morsel choked her throat and killed her. Therefore, be careful to put as much in your mouth to eat as the space in the mouth allows, even if the food is delicious like the sweet meat made of figs.

sections.heading: Search for Entirety Destroys Entirely
paras: God has given a truth-speaking-tongue to the weighing balance. Read about this in the Quran. He has said: And the Firmament has He raised high and has set up the balance (of justice), in order that you may not transgress (due) balance: wa alsamaa’a rafa ‘ahaa wa wadha ‘al miizarn alla tat ghaow fil miizaani: (Al Rahman: 55: 78). Be careful! Do not ignore the balance out of your greed, as desires and greed are your misguiding enemies. Greed searches for entirety but always remains deprived of it, as the saying goes — Search for entirety destroys in entirely. Greed is the commander of every weak minded. Know this! Do not be a weak-minded son of a weak minded.

sections.heading: Greed Traps Men
paras: The maid returned and cried out: “Ah, my lady! You sent away the master (of the art). You tried to get your job done without a teacher and therefore, you had to lose your life like the one ignorant of profession. You stole incomplete knowledge from me. You felt ashamed of making enquiries about the tricks of the trade. You did not think that the bird got its neck caught in the thick thread when it picked up the grain from the harvested heap”.

Eat less so that there may be no need to cure. When you read the word “eat” (kulu) in the Quran, read also “do not waste” (walaa tusrifuu) as stated: eat and drink and waste not by excess, kulu wa ashrabuu wa laa tusrifuu: (A‘raaf: 7: 31).
When you do not eat the grain, you do not get caught in the net. This is what common sense and contentment teach. Goodbye!

sections.heading: Fate of the Wise and Foolish
paras: The wise man eats the delicious things of the world and not the sorrows, but the ignorant and foolish misuse the grants and are put to shame. Grants of the world have to be used wisely to meet good ends and not foolishly to suffer. When they get their neck caught in the rope by rash eating, others also feel disgusted by looking at their condition. When the bird picks up the grain spread out upon the net, it picks up not grain but poison. A foolish and ignorant man picks up such grains, which are a net for men in which they suffer. But wisemen like careful birds avoid picking up such poison-like grains. They find out this poison in the grain and net. They do not fall to them like blind birds. The spreader of the net cuts off the head of the victimised foolish birds; but takes alive the birds with pleasing sounds among the gatherings of men. The meat of the foolish birds is good and therefore they are slaughtered. But as sounds of the other birds are musical and pleasing with high and low pitch, they are allowed to live.

sections.heading: Half-Knowledge Leads to Disaster
paras: The maid saw the house-lady fallen dead under the donkey from the keyhole of the door. She cried out: “What was this, O foolish lady? You learnt only a part of what your teacher did. You looked at the apparent aspect of the teacher but did not see the secret behind. You opened a shop without learning from a master and made yourself a master. You looked at the penis of the donkey like delicious honey and sweet meat, but in your greed, you did not look at the pumpkin. Or your love for the donkey blinded you from seeing the pumpkin. You looked at the visible qualities of the master and resorted to become a master with great joy as though you learnt everything in full.

sections.heading: Fools Get Cheated Even by Wisdom
paras: In like manner many foolish duffers and mischievous fellows see nothing, but the woollen garments put on by the sufis. So also, many shameless fellows imitate a few words learnt from the great masters and resort to boasting and juggling of words to fool others. Everyone holds a staff in his hand and claims to be like H. Musa and blows his breath upon fools as though he is H. ‘Isa. What will be his tragical situation when the truth of the truthful will put him to hard trial to test his worth. To avoid all this, make enquiries with the great masters and learn. Do not be like the greedy fellows who with their confusing and false-ostentatious-words cheat the people. They are greedy deaf and blind. You have, in fact tested many to learn from, but were disappointed, because they are fools like a flock of sheep, and victims of wolves. You heard a little and became their spokesman. And you are ignorant of the meanings of words, like parrots which repeat a few words without knowing their meanings.

chapters.title: How Man Teaches Parrot to Talk
chapters.subtitle: Illustration of the teaching of God through the shaikh to his disciples and of the prophets to his followers (as the disciples and followers do not have the capacity and relationship to learn directly from God). This is just as a parrot which cannot learn to talk directly from man as it has no relationship with man. Therefore, God keeps the teacher like a mirror before the disciples just as a mirror is kept before the parrot by its master. He teaches the parrot to talk from behind the mirror. God said: move not your tongue concerning the Quran to make haste there with: laa tuharrik bihi lisaanaka lita ‘jala bihi: (Qiyamat: 75: 16) And: it is no less than inspiration sent down to him: in huwa illaa wahyun yuuhaa: (Najm: 53: 4) This is the beginning of the neverending issue (problem). Thus, the reflection of the shaking of the parrot’s beak in the mirror makes it feel that the shaking is not its, but of the parrot in the mirror and it has no control on it. This shaking of the beak is synchronised with the words spoken by the teacher who is talking and teaching, invisibly, from behind the mirror. The live parrot in front of the mirror thinks that the parrot in the mirror is talking and learns the sounds of the words spoken, as if it is learning from the parrot. Thus, the teacher teaches the parrot through the beak of the parrot. This is only an illustration of the matter and not a replica equal in all respects

paras: The parrot sees itself in the mirror: that is, its own reflection has kept its face directly towards it. Behind the mirror his teacher is hidden talking well-articulated, sweet, slow words. The parrot thinks that this low tone is the speech of the parrot in the mirror. Thus, it learns to talk from one of its own species unaware of the design of the old, experienced wolfish teacher. Thus, it is taught to speak from behind the mirror, as it would not learn from anybody other than of its own species. It leans to talk from the expert teacher but is unaware of the meanings of the words learnt. It has learnt words one after another from man, but the parrot does not know that it learnt from man.

In similar manner, in the mirror-like-body of a saint, his innocent disciple sees himself but not the total wisdom, which is behind the mirror. He hears only what the saint is speaking and narrating. He thinks that that talking is by man. He is unaware of the One who is speaking through him. He learns the words spoken by the saint, but not the meanings and secrets hidden within these words. He does not understand whether the teacher is a parrot or the man behind the mirror, just as the parrot.

sections.heading: Sounds of Birds, Words of Saints Reproduced Without Knowing Meanings
paras: Similarly, some men learn the sounds of the birds as these sounds enter into their throats and mouths. But they are unaware of what the birds mean by those sounds. The only exception has been H. Sulaiman in this regard. Many persons have learnt the words of the dervishes, and with their words, they make their speeches and gatherings grand and colourful. But they do not know the meanings. Their fate is only in the learning of words. There is a possibility that God’s mercy may come to guide them to know the inner meanings.

chapters.title: Meaningless Lectures Are Barking of Dogs
chapters.subtitle: In forty days, meditation in seclusion, a good-hearted person saw in a dream a pregnant bitch from whose womb its puppies were barking. He was astonished for the reason that dogs bark for guarding, and it cannot be so in the mother’s womb. The barking is also for seeking help or milk. But there is no scope for this also in the mother’s womb. After waking up he prayed to God to know the reason as: But no one knows the hidden meanings except God: wa maa ya ‘lamu taa wiilahu alla Allah: (Al-Imran: 3: 7). He got the answer: this refers to those people who have not come out of curtains, the eyes of their hearts are not opened, but they make claims of insight. They go on giving lectures, which do not give them strength and support, nor guidance and instructions to the audiences

paras: A saintly person in his forty-days seclusion saw in a dream a bitch on the way. Unexpectedly, he heard the barking of puppies that were hidden within her. He was astonished at these sounds as to why the puppies barked in the womb. No one has seen in the world puppies crying in the mother’s womb so far. When he woke up from sleep, his astonishment went on increasing moment by moment. There was none along with him in the place of seclusion, who could solve the problem. He had only to approach the court of God. He submitted: “O God, because of this difficulty and confusion, I am getting deprived of meditation upon You in my seclusion. Spread out my wings so that I may fly in the garden of Your thoughts and pluck the apples. A hidden voice came over to him: “Consider this as the boastings of knowledge of the ignorant fellows. They would not come out of curtains and barriers. They shut their eyes and blabber senselessly.

sections.heading: Talking Nonsense Before the Senseless
paras: The dog’s barking in the womb is of no use. It is neither for hunting nor for guarding. It has not seen a wolf so as to chase it away. Nor has it seen a thief to prevent him from stealing. An ignorant teacher, out of greed for money and desire for leadership is with dull eyes, but very bold in talking. In order to get customers and well-wishers, without any insight, he steps into the field of senseless oratory. Without seeing the moon, he speaks of its signs and presents its brightness in a perverse manner. For the sake of his customers, he speaks of a hundred signs of the moon without seeing any of them, in order to flabbergast them of his knowledge. He speaks of a hundred signs of many other things without any knowledge. He blabbers, claps his hands and drinks buttermilk but poses as though intoxicated with wine.

sections.heading: Let God Purchase You, Not Men
paras: The purchaser of the faithful is only One, that is, God. But the ignorant teacher has many doubts and suspicions about Him. In the search of worthless purchasers, the groups of such people have lost that Great Purchaser. Our purchaser is God and therefore go away from the search of other purchasers. God has said: God has purchased of the believers their persons and their goods: Innallah ushtarra minal muu ‘miniina anfusahum wa amwalahum: (Tauba: 9: 111). Therefore, forget all other purchasers and go before Him. Search for that Purchaser Who is in search of you, who knows you form beginning to end. Do not pull every purchaser with your hand. Falling in love with two beloveds is bad. The purchaser other than God, does not give any profit. He has nothing to pay for the price of your wisdom and intelligence. He is himself not of the worth of a half horseshoe. And you are showing him rubies and gems.

sections.heading: Faith of Worthless Pretenders
paras: Greed has made you blind and kept you deprived. Devil will make you worthy of being stoned to death, just like the people of the elephant, (Ashab-e-fiil) and the community of H. Loot, (Lot), who were pelted with stones by God. Patient people have found out that Purchaser, as they did not run after other purchasers. He who turns his face away from this Great Purchaser, gets his fortune, prosperity and life lost from himself.
The greedy have always been unsatisfied and craving just as what happened to people to Zarwaan for their jealousy.

chapters.title: Invisible Prosperity
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the People of Zarwaan and their jealousy for the poor, saying that their father out of his simplicity, gave a large portion of the produce of their farmland to the poor. He gave one-tenth part of grapes, one-tenth of currants, one-tenth of grape syrup, one-tenth of sweets prepared out of the things. So also, one-tenth of the raw harvest, one-tenth of cleansed harvest, one-tenth of wheat separated from husk, one-tenth of wheat flour, one-tenth of malt and one-tenth of prepared bread. Thus, God had given such prosperity to his farmland, that all people connected with it were benefitted in its direct produce and the money received by the sale proceeds of its products. None used to be deprived. Children of the landowner looked at the repeatedly-given one-tenth portion at every level but not at its invisible prosperity, like that unfortunate woman who looked at the donkey’s organ and not at the pumpkin attached to it

paras: There was a noble godly man with perfect wisdom and awareness of the ultimate end, in Zarwaan village nearby to Yemen. He was well known for generosity and charity. Poor people considered his street as their Ka‘aba. All needy people used to come to him. Without any intention of showiness, he would give to the poor one-tenth of the raw crop in the ears and also upon separation of the wheat grains from husk. He would give one-tenth of the flour as well as one-tenth of the prepared bread. He would never ignore to give one-tenth of any kind of income. He used to give the finished product of the crop at four levels. One-tenth of grapes, currants, grape syrup, sweets made out of these. He would not give anything less or more of all these.

sections.heading: Spread of Grains for Further Gains
paras: Every time he used to advise his children to continue to do as he does after his death with regard to the needy, and not to stop this out of greed, so that products of the land and gardens might always be with them with continuing protection from God as an act of worship.

sections.heading: Profits Come from Hidden Sources
paras: Incomes and fruits come from hidden sources, which God sends without any doubts and measures. If you spend at the time of earning, it is kept in the God’s court as your gains. You will always be in gains. The farmer sows a good part of the harvested grains again in the land, which is the root of further gains, and gets benefitted again. He sows more and eats a little as there is no doubt in the growing of the seeds into fresh crops. He spreads over the grain on the land as it is from the land only that he got the grains.

So also, a cobbler spends what is left over after meeting his immediate expenses of food, for the purchase of soft and hard leather and articles of his trade thinking that these are the base of his earnings. These only open the closed door of the provisions. Inevitably, his earning comes from this expenditure only. This only graces and grants him. He thinks that his shop and the leather are only apparent reason, but the provisions come only from God.
