On the contrary, a fee willer is not a rejector of senses, but considers senses to be supporters of wisdom to understand the acts of God. Senses are not considered to be acts of God by him but only as supporters to him to act. Rejector of free will of the free willer by a predestination is based only on logic and rhetoric and not on reality and observation. It is something like telling that there is smoke but not due to fire and there is light without lamp. In fact, he sees fire, but denies its existence. He sees his clothes burning but says there is no thread for it. Actual observations and the specific reasons behind each of them are of no concern for the predestinations.

sections.heading: Skepticism Worse Than Atheism
paras: (Skepticism pessimism cognitive value of sense perception intellectual dogmatism nonrational ground for preferring one courses of action to another phyrro sutigolte to worry.) This is skepticism rejecting all kinds of knowledge, which is worse than atheism. An atheist believes in the existence of the world, even though he denies God its creator, with the application of his mind but unconsciously sometimes, he calls upon God, in matter of helplessness. He does not reject the existence of the world, though rejecting its creator but the sceptic is in utter confusion, caught between thoughts of existence and non-existence.

sections.heading: People Follow Free Will
paras: All the people of the world follow the path of free will, by issuing positive and negative commands upon others as well as upon themselves. They have demands for certain things of their choice and refuse to accept some other things. Were they to believe that others have no free will of their own, they would not impose commands for his and that.

The predestinarian further says that there is no need for issue of positive and negative commands. These are of no worth and use as there no scope of any choice by men. Every act occurs of its own. The predestinarian rejects even sense perceptions, even though even animals follow them. It is very strange that even the free willer, who considers mean to possess all powers, also refuses to believe in rational perception because they are very difficult to understand and penetrate into. Our free will is dependent upon perception and choice and therefore, we are liable for our acts.

chapters.title: Consciousness and External Sensations
chapters.subtitle: Inner consciousness such as of assertion of authority and its rejection, anger and coolness of mind, eating and hunger dominate over external sensations such as finding difference between yellow and red, small and large size, sweetness and bitterness, pleasing and displeasing smells of musk and dung, softness and hardness, cold and heat, hot and warm, wet and dry, touching of a wall and bark of tree. One who denies these inner sensations is a denier as well of external sensations, rather worse, as inner sensations are more assertive and effective than external senses. This is because, external senses can be controlled and prevented from impacts, but it is impossible to prevent and control inner sensations. These hints are enough for a wise man to know the realities.

sections.heading: Inner Consciousness as Predestinations
paras: Inner consciousness occupies the place of external senses and both flows together like in a single stream. [Inner Consciousness are the hidden commanding instructions of the soul that come about, of their own, without man’s willingness or otherwise like exercising or otherwise of authority, feeling of helplessness, worry, anger, self-control. These are opposed to external, actions and feelings such as finding of sweetness or bitterness, color, size, state etc. — Qazi Sajjad Husain]

Finding a thing as good or bad and to do or not to do an act, issuing a positive or negative command and explanations of matter in words arise from the inner consciousness or faculties. [These come about of their own and can be considered as matters of predestination].

sections.heading: Expectations from the Living
paras: But one’s telling: “I shall do this or that tomorrow are matters and examples of free will. Your feeling sorry for having done something wrong is evidence of free will and this feeling of regret puts you on the right path.

All positive and negative commands in the Quran are instructions and warnings to you as you are a man. These commands are not upon rocks and materials. This is similar to the fact that no wise man would express his enmity and anger upon a stone or lump of mud. He never tells it. “I had told you to do this and not to do that”, and never asks as to why it did it or not. He never asks lifeless things to do or not to do this or that. Wisdom never gives instructions to stone or wood. A musician does not think of playing on a picture of the musical instrument. No commander of an army tells a slave who has lost his leg, to hold the spear and go toward the battlefield. The Great Creator who has made the heavens and stars has not given any positive and negative command to them as they are incapable.

The predestinarian, by considering man’s self and Satan as dominant upon man thinks that God is helpless, and man is dominated by them. This is only due to his ignorance, confusion, foolishness and misunderstanding. There is no scope for helplessness in the belief of free will, as helplessness is worse than ignorance and foolishness. Because he considers man’s actions as predestined by God, he considers man as helpless, and God’s issuance of commands to the helpless is contradictory and meaning less. Man’s free will does not mean God’s helplessness, as it is given to him by God’s own wish.

sections.heading: Laws: for Protection from Evil Effects
paras: Take the example of the Turk. He invites a guest to come to his door without his dog and torne clothes, saying: “My dog hates these things. Be careful to come to my house through the other door so that my dog may keep its mouth and teeth shut.” Thus, God has made certain laws which are inevitably followed, like the Turk’s keeping of a ferocious dog at his door. At the same time, the Turk has kept escape routes by instructing his guest to come through a particular door in a particular manner to protect himself form his Dog’s attacks. If you do not follow the Turk’s instructions, you get bitten by his dog. Similarly, positive and negative commands are given by God to protect yourself from certain undesirable consequences. If you follow these commands, there will be no scope for Satan to interfere in your affairs. If you dis-obey those commands, Satan will get the scope to cause misguidance to you. There is no compulsion upon you to follow the rules and also upon Satan to play his role. Satan is just like God’s dog who acts upon the job allotted to him, and troubles only those who deviated from God’s instructions. Therefore, proceed on the way shown by God like an obedient slave, so that His dog may become mild and friendly. As against this, if you take with you haughty dogs or wicked foxes which make his dog go against you, you will suffer at its hands.

sections.heading: Punishment, Advice on Free Will Basis
paras: When you as predestinarian, consider everyone to be helpless excepting God, there is no meaning in your getting angry with criminals. But what is seen is that you are angry with your enemies. Why do you consider them to be wrong and sinful? If a wooden rafter of your house breaks and falls upon and injures you, you do not get angry with it, and think of punishing it telling it: “why did you fall on me and break my hand and tumbled me down?” you do not call it as your enemy, hateful of your life and being deliberately after you. You chastise your children to teach them and do not do so with elders, because you feel that as against children, elders are responsible for their acts. If someone steals your materials, you tell the police to catch the thief, imprison him and cut off his hand. If someone casts a vicious eye upon your wife, you get angry with him. On the contrary, if the same materials are swept away by flood, you do not get angry with it and think of punishing. If a fast wind blows off your turban you do not get angry with it. Your getting angry with the thief and not others speak of your accepting of authority on his part and not on the flood and wind. You do not pardon the thief on the basis of his predestined acts.

sections.heading: Animals Too Recognize Free Will
paras: You may also see that, when a camel driver hits the camel, the camel feels ill of the driver and not of the stick that struck it. This shows that even a camel knows that the camel driver’s authority struck it and not the stick. So also, if you hit a dog with a stone, it turns against you and not against the stone. But if it happens to go against the stone, it is due to its anger for you, you being far away from its zone of action and beyond its control. When the animals sense understands this much about free will, it becomes a matter of shame for a man to believe in predestination.

sections.heading: Predestination, as an Excuse
paras: These matters are quite clear, but a man who wants to eat his food after true dawn out of greed as against the timings of Ramadhan fasting, which is prohibited after true dawn, does so, by keeping his eyes closed toward morning light. As his inclination is toward eating, he turns his eyes away from light and toward darkness. Just as greed has hidden the sun from his sight, there is no wonder that he would turn his back from clear evidences. In order to understand this, you may hear this illustration and do not reject it at the time of the trial of your free will.

chapters.title: Punishment Not Warded Off
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a thief who said to the police officer that what he did was predestined by God and the police officer’s answer thereat; and explanation of the reasons for the people’s acceptance of free will and also to explain that fate and predestination become the causes of promoting free will and not destroying it.

paras: A thief told the police officer: “O king! What I did was under the command of God”. The police officer said: “My dear, what I am doing is also as per God’s command”.

If a man takes away a radish from a shop, saying that it is under the command of God, then you may give two three blows on his head saying: “O incompetent fellow: under God’s command, you may keep it is its place. O foolish fellow, when this excuse is not acceptable in the case of a vegetable for the vegetable merchant, you rely upon this belief and go toward scorpions and pythons to suffer injuries! With such foolish and senseless concepts your life, wealth and wife can all be taken away from you. Everyone can pluck your mustacheos and project himself. As helpless in doing so being under the command of God. If the excuse of God’s command in respect of sins is valid. You may give satisfactory evidences to me so that I may be bold enough to commit them. As I also feel like committing such sins. I also have hundreds of desires and wishes, which I have kept under control with the fear of God. Therefore, please teach me excuses in respect of them and untie my hands and feet of their knots.

sections.heading: Free Will Resorted to in Greed
paras: “Of so many professions in the world, you think of adopting a particular one and while doing so, you think that you have the option and ability. As otherwise, why you adopt that one also, why not another? This shows that you have a free will of yours. But when the pressure of your selfish desires exerts, you get the strength and free will of twenty men. If a friend takes away a farthing worth of material from you, you develop a free will and let yourself free for a strong fight. But when it comes to expressing thanks for the gifts you have received, you feel yourself to be helpless and lesser than a stone. Thus, you may consider that when you burn in the fire of hell, it will also say that it is helpless in the matter of burning you. The hell will tell you: “with such arguments of predestination that you had, you could not protect yourself from the hand of an executioner in the world, as he was not convinced of your argument. The command of the Great Ruler of the world became known to you only now, when you entered into my burning fire.”

chapters.title: Predestination Rejected by All Communities
chapters.subtitle: Another illustration in answer to the predestination; and in support of free will; and to establish the correctness of positive and negative commands. And to explain that no community accepts the concept and faith of predestination as a ground for escape from punishment. Even Iblis could not free himself when he said to God: O my Lord! Because you have put me in the wrong, …: Rabbi bimaa agh waitanii …: (Al-Hijr: 15: 39). So, this saying goes: a little evidence is enough to prove a big issue.

paras: A person climbed upon a tree and started telling many fruits like thieves. The owner of the garden came over and said: “O mean fellow! Do you not have any sense of shame before God upon what you are doing!” That fellow replied: “From the garden of God, a servant of God is eating the fruits which are provided to him by God. Why do you condemn me like a senseless lowly fellow! You are showing miserliness upon the dining sheet spread over by God, who is not selective in making provisions.”

sections.heading: If Crime Is Predestined, so Also Is Punishment
paras: The owner of the garden told his servant to bring a rope so that he could give a suitable answer. He caught hold of him and tied him tightly to the tree and started beating upon his back and calves with a stick. The thief said: “Now you may feel ashamed before God that you are mercilessly beating an innocent person in this manner.” The owner said: “with this stick of God, this servant of God is beating on the back of another servant of God. The stick is His, back and sides are His and I am His, slave and also His tool.”

sections.heading: Free Will Controlled by God’s Free Will
paras: Upon this the predestinarian thief repented. There is free will here, free will there and free will everywhere. Your free will is created by God’s free will. His free will is like dust overlapping a horse rider. His free will creates our free will. All positive and negative commands are dependent upon man’s free will. The power to command upon every creature lacking free will, is in the command and authority of man, with free will in such a way that he traps and drag towards himself all those without free will. He possesses the means and ways to trap and drag them. But the free will of God, the totally independent of all is such that it traps the free will of others within His grip without any means and tools. This is the special authority of God that He keeps servant under His control as a prey, without the support and need of any net to catch, and as a tamed dog to drive the game toward the net, as mas does in hunting. God controls everything without tools as against man who cannot do without tools. A carpenter becomes a ruler upon wood. A painter becomes a ruler upon a beautiful painting. Blacksmith is a ruler upon iron and a builder upon his tools. This is a strange fact that with all commands and authority upon their respective possessions, all His servants are under His command and control without any directly visible tools and means.

sections.heading: Man’s Control on Lifeless Objects
paras: Your control upon lifeless materials is because of your special powers and authority and it does not negate their lifelessness. [every lifeless material has its own peculiar property. It does not deviate from it. For example: wood has its own property, and iron its own. They cannot adopt the property of each other. So also, they cannot get rid of their respective properties. Their properties are specific to each of them. They are all under the authority of God — Translator]. Their possession of their respective properties does not negate the authority of God upon them. Similarly, man’s authority and control on them does not negate God’s authority on man. It is one’s expertise in a particular field that gives one control over things. A carpenter has authority on wood and a blacksmith on iron and not vice versa. If this fact of authority and limitation is accepted, there will be no scope for confusion and misguidance. [this is how God controls the authority of man over things and brings man’s actions and desires under His control as the Quran says: you will not wish (will) except what God wills: wa maa tashaauun illaa an yashaa ‘allah: (Insaar: 76: 30). As it happens that a carpenter with full confidence and wish turns toward wood to act upon but not upon iron. So also, a blacksmith toward iron and not wood. In this manner everyone with expertise in some field has authority in his field not and another. This is in respect of man’s authority of lifeless materials — Translator]

sections.heading: Deniel of God: Due to Free Will
paras: Coming to himself, if a predestinarian says that his infidelity and rejection of God is as per God’s own willing, he admits that there is a willing of his own as well, which is subject to God’s willing, because acceptance or rejection is a mental act; and mental act is under the control of will. That is, he has control over his will, which is due to his own authority. That is, he has free will of his own. There cannot be infidelity without application of mind as infidelity is a product of his willing and there cannot a will without his authority or free will. Talking of infidelity without willing is like bringing together two opposites.

sections.heading: Incapable, Helpless and Unconscious
paras: Giving commands to a helpless is vicious and undesirable and expressing of wrath on a helpless one is very bad and in particular from God, the Merciful. If an ox refuses to bow down its head to carry the yoke, it is beaten to yield. But it is not compelled to fly, as it is helpless and incapable in the matter of flying. When an ox is considered to helpless in this, how can its master be not considered as foolish and helpless. If he expects the ox to fly. A predestinarian should not seek any treatment for his sickness and leave it at it. But he does not do so but takes treatment. From this simple point itself he should proceed to drink the cup of God’s truthfulness and then get intoxicated with the wine of His gnosis upon which he will get into another kind of weakness and helplessness. Then a time will come when that wine will have total control on you and you will be semi-unconscious and helpless. Then what all you say, will be the saying of that wine, and what all you spill, will be the wine’s spillage. Such an unconscious will not do or say anything other than the right and perfect as he would be one drunk with the wine of truth.

Magicians told Pharaoh, when their hands and legs were ordered to be cut off: “Go ahead! The unconscious have no care for hands and legs. Our hands and legs are intoxicated with the wine of God, the bringer forth of everything. Our visible hands are just a shadow and counterfeit. When the wine from His gnosis fills up the head, it engulfs the heart fully from all sides.

chapters.title: God’s Wish Alone Comes About
chapters.subtitle: Meaning of “what God wished, came about? (Maashaa Allahu kaana). That is, wish is His alone and consonance with what came about is consonance with Him. And one should not regret upon the anger of and rejection by others. The word “wished” (Kaana) is in past tense, but in the act of God, there is no past and future. There is “no morning and evening for God”

paras: A man’s telling: “what God wished came about” is not to mean to become lazy and inactive on your part but to make you to seek more, and to sincerely try for your object so that you may be benefited from His court as well. [Cursorily, this interpretation appears to be in opposition to the plain meaning that what God wishes comes about]. If it is interpreted according to your wish, of remaining in-active, it will be in accordance with Your wish and not God’s wish. This interpretation (as of your wish) will entitle you to inactivity and to do what you wish and act for. But if the meaning is taken as it is according to God’s wish alone, it is taken absolutely as according to His command, and this is not in one case alone but in all cases. Then, you will move around His sources with a hundred-fold vigor and enthusiasm. You will surrender yourself like a slave before Him. (So that He may wish as you wish).

sections.heading: Interpretation and Misinterpretation
paras: If a king declares that the minister is at full liberty to do whatever he wishes in giving grants as well as in punishments, you will go to him with a hundred fold vigor and enthusiasm, so that he may spill over his benevolences upon your head. And you will keep yourself away from his palace, it means that you do not want to seek help. You made yourself inactive by misunderstanding the situation.

Predestination took the omnipotence and authority of God for his laziness in worship by making perverse interpretations. He failed to understand the meaning of the omnipotence as something that should make him go closer to Him and sit with Him. Go to the Master and be with Him as His writ runs large and He is capable of chasing away the enemy and protect His friends. He is capable of doing everything as per wish and provide to you. Do not talk nonsense about Him but prefer to go to His court for solace. And not that you should avoid to go to Him which would blacken your record and make your face pale out of fear. Hold on to Him as He is the Ruler and none other than Him has any authority and power. That ought to be the correct interpretation which would make you hopeful smart and decent. If an interpretation makes you dull, it should be taken as misinterpretation by interpolation of contrary versions.

sections.heading: Understand Quran Through Quran Itself
paras: This statement: “what God wills comes about” has come to enthuse you and encourage you so that you may not feel fearful and dejected. Quran’s meaning has to be understood through the Quran itself and not through the understanding of the greedy, self-loving fellows. It should be taken as interpreted by one who surrenders and sacrifices himself before the Quran and is strictly obedient to it, to such an extent that his soul becomes entirely in accordance with it in all respect. Smelling a flower that has entirely dissolved itself in oil, or the oil is the same. If you cannot understand the Quran yourself, try to find a person of those abilities which are entirely in accordance with the Quran so that your heart may brighten from the light of his heart.

chapters.title: Meaning of Jaffal Qalamu
chapters.subtitle: Similar is the interpretation of the Prophet’s statement: the pen dried after up writing about fate, that obedience and disobedience are not the same; so also trust and theft. The pen dried up after writing that gratefulness and rejection are not the same. So also, the pen dried up after writing: God does not destroy the reward of those who do good: (Tauba: 9: 120)

sections.heading: What the Pen Wrote
paras: Similarly, is the interpretation of the phrase — “the pen dried up” (Jaffal qalaamu) in order to enthuse one to engage in jobs of importance. The pen of Godly commands, instructions and explanations) wrote down about all actions, in accordance with their impacts and components and dried up. It wrote down that if you go on the wrong way, you will meet wrong results and if you go on the right way you will meet your object and succeed. The pen dried after writing down that you will meet misfortune by doing cruel acts and you will be rewarded will upon doing just acts. So also, it wrote down that your hand will be cut off, if you commit theft, and you get intoxicated if you drink wine.

sections.heading: Grade of Actions Fixed
paras: If you interpret the meaning of (Jaffal qalaamu) that God has written down about everything and let it go on its own, it means that He has lost all His powers. As such everything has gone out of His control saying: “do not come before Me and do not cry before Me, (as I have exhausted myself of all power). “The pen dried up” means that justice and cruelty are not the same before Me. I have kept difference between good and bad. I have kept a difference between bad and worse. Even if a particle’s worth of etiquette in you is more than that in your friend it is well-known to God. You will be given more in accordance with the size of that particle, which will come about to be seen as of the size of a mountain, when you stand before His throne. May there be dust upon the head of the king before whose throne, there is no difference between the honest and cruel, and between the one who is shivering out of fear before him and the one who makes unpalatable remarks upon his kingship. Such a king who does not differentiate between them is not worthy of being called a king as needs to be thrown black dust upon his head.

sections.heading: Deliberate Misinterpretation
paras: An increase of a particle’s worth is your efforts will be weighed in the balance of God. As against Him, the other kings for whom you suffer for your whole life are unaware of traitors and the lights of heart. Upon hearing the words of a back-biter against you, he will make your services for years go waste. But before the great king, who is all Hearing and Seeing, nothing from the backbiters holds any value. All backbiters become helpless before Him like the Devil. Having failed before Him, they come before us and say that “His doors are shut through the drying up of the pen. There is no need to go to Him to show your faithfulness for Him.” They speak to us of His cruelties and tell us to avoid Him as the pen dried up after writing down everything, and there is nothing more to be written or rewritten.

How can this be the meaning of “the pen dried up” that cruelty and honesty are the same. But it has dried up after writing down that the reward for cruelty is cruel treatment only, and the reward for honesty is honest treatment only. They also confuse us by telling that God, anyway, is a waiver of sins. This is of course correct, but it is only waiver. It does not possess the hope of that grandeur and of that bright face, that one gets upon performance of acts of piety and nobility. If a thief is pardoned, he saves his life. He gets only this much but not the humor of becoming a treasurer and minister. The former is a case of pardon, and the latter is a case of grant.

sections.heading: Promise Rewards for Good Acts
paras: “O honest to the faith: come forward! Honesty rewards you the crown and flag of honour. If the son of a king commits misappropriation, he becomes liable to be punished with the severing of his head. If a Hindu (slave) shows honesty, he becomes entitled to the wealth of a long life. What to speak of a slave? If the dog at the door shows faithfulness, its master develops hundreds of affections for it in his heart. For its faithfulness, when the dog’s mouth is kissed, imagine how much honor a lion gets for its faithfulness.

Earlier I have said that a thief upon pardon gets protection of life but not honor. But there are exception. If a thief after receiving pardon renders faithful service, his faithful service and truthfulness remove the impacts of his earlier cruelties from their roots. Such a thing happened in the case of H. Fuzail bin ‘Ayaadh, who was earlier a dacoit. But after true repentance, he ran toward God with the vigor of ten men and became a great saint. So also, the magicians of Pharaoh blackened his face by their true repentance, patience and faithfulness. They offered their hands and feet in recompense for their sins, for which they attained a state which cannot be achieved with worshipful acts for a hundred years. But you can live only a life of about fifty years, even if you devote all fifty years for worship, you cannot attain the level of those magicians.

chapters.title: Petty Gains Misguide
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a Darvish who saw the slaves of ‘Ameed khorasani in Herat, well dressed, seated upon arabian horses, wearing long coats made of fabrics made of cotton threads, mixed with threads of gold and silver, and shining cops upon their heads and other decorations. He asked the people as to of country they are the lords and kings. He was told that they are not lords and kings. They are the slaves of ‘Ameed of Khorasan. The Darvish turned his face toward the sky and said: “O my Lord! Learn the ways of taking care of slaves from ‘Ameed”. In that place the prime minister was called ‘Ameed

sections.heading: Informal Talks of Friends
paras: When a fearless, smart Darvish saw the slaves of a great man well dressed, wearing costly dress with golden waist belts, he faced toward the sky and said: “O God! Why do you not learn from this benevolent master of slaves as to how to look after the slaves. Learn the lesson to take care of the people from this lord and honorable leader of our city.”

The darvish was poor, destitute and deprived and shivering without clothes in chilly-wintery wind. With the loss of self-control, he became bold and behaved informally in a grand way to talk like this. He was confident of receiving thousands of grants from God, as he was one among those very closely to God, like His great gnostics. This was a statement from such a closely one to God. This does not entitle you to say so.
The king’s courtier talks boldly with the king. It is alright for him as he has liberty and encouragement from him. But you do not have that liberty and support

sections.heading: Lessons of Mastership and Slavery
paras: You should consider that God has given you a waist, which is much better than the waistband of Gold. If someone gives him a crown, it is to wear upon the head given by God. God did not give reply to the bold statement of the darvish at that time. Later, when the king got angry with the prime minister, he made accusations against him and tied up his hands and legs. He tied up his slaves and asked them to show the place where the prime minister had hidden the misappropriated wealth. He told them: “speak of his secrets to me, O lowly fellows, as otherwise, I shall cut of your tongues and throats. He tortured them, day and night for a month putting them under great pressure and pain. He cut them all into piece, but not a single slave revealed the secrets of his master.

Then a hidden voice came from God to the darvish in his dream: “O bold fellow: you had told me to learn from ‘Ameed as to how to treat the slaves. Now you may learn from the slaves how you should be like a slave.”

sections.heading: Your Acts Recoil upon You
paras: O tearer of the leather coat of the innocent helpless like Yusuf! If a wolf tears you up, you may think it as a result of your acts of tearing up others garments. You wear whatever you weave for one year. You eat what you plant and grow for one year. The troubles of life that come to you are your own makings. This is the meaning of “the pen dried up”. Our practice does not deviate from the right. No change will you find in the practice of God: Lan tajida lisuuaa tallahii tabdiilan (Ahzab: 33: 62). Good is for good and vice for vice as stated in the Quran: Is there any reward for good – other than good: Hal jazaa ‘ul insaana alla al ihsaanu: (Al Rahman: 55: 60)

Go on working like obedient jinns of H. Sulaiman, as his sword will cut to pieces the devils, as H. Sulaiman is not dead for them. God, the real ruler, is observing the acts of your vicious commanding self. If you control your commanding self and make it obedient to you. It gets converted into an angel. You will remain in peace and protected from the sword of H. Sulaiman. You will not have any reason to fear. There is no need for the good to be afraid of H. Sulaiman, as he is an enemy of devils and not of the angels. His command and control is upon devils and not an angel. All kinds of troubles are upon the earth and not on the sky.

sections.heading: Predestination: Belief of Lazy Fellows
paras: Remove the concept of predestination from your mind as it is a hollow drum. This is needed in order to know the secret behind this concept, that this is a concept of the lazy fellows. If you come to know of this secret, you will value your own life which is very precious and highly valuable. This will make you an active lover as against being a passive beloved. A lover goes after the beloved activity, but the beloved passively exhibits designs and styles and teases the lover by mischievous, stealthy, pretending glances.

sections.heading: Meaningless Words Cause No Impacts
paras: You are more silent than the night in speaking of the meanings of words. You produce only the sounds of words and search for their buyers. They hold their heads and swing on this and that side, upon hearing your meaningless, decorative sounds, and learn nothing from you as you do not have anything to teach them. You waste your life in order to make them your admirers. Upon hearing this from me, you may not consider me to be jealous of you. But that is not so as no one can be jealous of the possession or dispossession of worthless things. If you consider yourself to be influential, you should know that teaching the worthless fellows is like making fine painting on a lump of mud, which neither accepts the painting marks nor retains them.

Try to teach yourself the lessons of observation and understanding of truths of matters and to love them, as they are the strong markings on a body of hard rocks. Your self will become thankful and faithful to you, and this only is yours. Rest of the things do not belong to you and they are destructible. Your efforts should be to educate and elevate yourself. There is no meaning in searching for them. So long as you try to make others scholarly and elevated, you will be making yourself indecent and empty.

sections.heading: Command of Speak (Qul)
paras: When your heart gets connected with eternity and the unity of God, you may go on teaching without fearing of losing what you possess. It is such great men who have resorted to teaching and caused great impacts. Their resorting to teaching should not be a model for your hollow, meaningless words to be taught. It is for them the word “speak” (Qul) has come. Correct yourself of misconception. They have been commanded to speak with an assurance that their teaching will not reduce their weight and worth, as they are like the ocean. That is what is said in the Quran: though the see became ink for the words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though we brought the like of it thereof to help: Laow kaana albahru midaadan likalinaaa ti rabbi lanafidal bahru qabla an tanfida kalimaatu rabbi wa laow ji ‘naa bimith(s)lihi madadan: (Kahaf: 18: 109).

sections.heading: Command of Listen (Ansitu)
paras: For incompetent persons like you the command is “to pay heed and listen” (Ansituu) as stated in the Quran: when the Quran is read listen to it with attention and give ear: wa izaa quri ‘al quraanu fastami ‘u lahu wa ansituu: (A ‘raf: 7: 204). And do not pollute it with your senseless words. Be careful, not to reduce its worth as the garden of your heart is dry and waterless. There is no end to this discussion. Do not engage yourself in oral talks and pay attention to the meanings and their impacts upon your final end.

sections.heading: Pseudo-Scholars Beg for Hearers
paras: I feel ashamed when I see those fellows standing before you to hear your lectures. They stand before you, not out of love and regard for you but to laugh at you. Those who love you are behind the curtain of gracefulness to grace you. You can see them, if you put efforts, continuingly praying for your reformation moment by moment. Forget these deceptive lovers standing before you and fall in love with those genuine lovers who are for your permanent good. Do not go after the temporary, timely, pseudo-lovers standing right in front of you. They actively destroy you with their deceptive praises and inclinations. You have been with them for years together but did not get a particle’s worth of gain. How long do you want to organize gatherings for them on public ways. You tried to meet some unknown object, which you never got.

Everyone is a friend and helper when you are in good health; and at the time of sufferings, pains and sorrows, none can be with you other than God. None can be of any help when you suffer pain in your eyes and teeth, except God, the only listener and curer of pains. Always keep these pains and sicknesses in your mind and learn lessons from Ayaz, who held on to his leather coat of sorrowful days, in his days of happiness. Ayaz used to seek solace from the old torne garment, and you may do so from your past troublesome days.

chapters.title: Endless Debates End with Love
chapters.subtitle: Further arguments of the predestinarian infidel with the faithful follower of Muhammad, who invited him to Islam to give up his concept of predestination; and elongation of the debate from both sides, as the base of matter cannot be altered by except with the true love of God, as God has no concern for beliefs. This is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills: zaalika fadhlullahi yu ‘tiihi man yashaa ‘u: (Hadid: 57: 21)

paras: The predestinarian infidel started his arguments before which the opposing speaker was stunned. If I narrate all their opposing arguments, I would narrate all, but would remain away from what I have to say. I have to speak of more important matters than their arguments, which would make your understanding better. Therefore, I skip their arguments, I have spoken a little of what all they said, as a little (sample) can speak of the affair of the entire lot.

sections.heading: Arguments to Continue Till Doomsday
paras: Between the predestinarians and free willers, there have been such debates and they will continue till the doomsday and the day of resurrection. They fear that, if they fail to counter the arguments of their opponents, their own perceptions and faith would be falsified. Were they to fail to give counter arguments, they would have had to run away from the field of their respective destructivenesses. But as God’s only takes care of their respective arguments and counter arguments. So that every group may not free itself from the defense of its concepts and protect them from the opponents. So that, these seventy-two communities made by God may remain forever thill the doomsday.

sections.heading: Life’s Honor Is in Debates
paras: As this is a world of both appearances and disappearances it is in need of a shadow to show the light, and that shadow is caused by earth. [In order to create darkness, rotation of the earth is required, which becomes dark upon the setting of sun, which is again bright upon sun rise. Both light and darkness are required for the earth’s sustenance — Translator]. So also, these seventy-two groups are required to exist, so that new and newer arguments may not cease to come forth. The honor of a treasury depends upon the treasures it contains and greater are the treasures in it, more and more locks are put on it. Arguments and counter arguments are the wealth of this world. they are like treasure and locks. Both are required for the honor of life.
Destination after hard Journey more Valued

Honor of an object is dependent upon the difficulties on its attainments. Curves and ups and downs of the road and the risk of confrontations with dacoits increase the worth and value of the place to reach. Honor of the ka’aba at Makka is because of tis distance from the people and the large deserts on the way and the thefts committed by the Bedouins. That is an unworthy path which has no curves, obstacles and dacoits. Right destination is achieved after overtaking these hurdles. Thus, the path of those at the wrong place are full of enmity and opposition to those on the right path. They put their blind followers in utter confusion. They consider the arguments of their respective paths as true and remain satisfied with them. If each party has no counter arguments, there is no quarrel at all up to the doomsday. But they do not accept the other’s arguments. If they fail to counter, they say: “We do not know much: we are not that competent. But our elders are. They know the entire truth!”

sections.heading: Insinuation Never Stops
paras: the only muzzle to keep their mouths shut while considering these insinuations is love, because insinuations are things which can never never be stopped. Therefore, fall in love and find out one who can put you on the path of love. Search for one such beautiful beloved just as a hunter search for beautiful geese from stream to stream. You cannot get rid of these insinuations through these arguments. They will rather deprive you of your own sense. You can get more convincing grand and precious things in love than these reason-based-arguments. Apart from the wisdom and reasoning that you possess, there are other kinds of wisdom, which are the organizers and managers of the heavens. Through love, you will get such grand provisions, with which you will make the stages of the heavens as your resting places.

sections.heading: Love Ends Arguments
paras: When you stake your wisdom with love, you will get ten to seven hundred times of stake value. When women staked their wisdom for Yusuf, they climbed upon the parapet of the love of Yusuf. What the cupbearer of love suddenly snatched away their wisdom there was no need for wisdom any more for the ret of the life. Beauty of Yusuf and of a hundred like him is just a reflection of the beauty of the Master of Majesty and Grandeur. Therefore, sacrifice your life for this grand beauty, as you are lesser in worth in love than a single woman out of the group of many women whose senses were snatched by Yusuf’s beauty. Love puts an end to all arguments, and intellect becomes a silent receiver and solver of all grievances of words and speeches. Its silence is the solace for all problems as the saying goes: “one who understands God becomes speechless. His tongue loses the words to express through.

sections.heading: Love Silences
paras: Love bewilders tongue in such a way that it forgets as to what to speak. It fears that if I wag myself to speak, the precious pearls of love and beauty held within the mouth will fall down and I shall be put to great loss. It shuts the lips hard from all good and bad, fearing that these pearls will fall down from the mouth. This is what an honorable companion of the Prophet reported that the Prophet while speaking out before the incompetents like us, expected us to be with extreme attention and poise. “We used to sit before him with such silence and composure as though a bird was sitting on the head which would fly off with the slightest of your shaking causing great loss to us.” In the matter of love, you will not dare to move even slightly, fearing that your beautiful bird will be snatched away by the wind. When you have such fear, you will even control your breaths and coughs to prevent the grand bird from flying off. How much ever one may talk sweet or bitter before you, you would not say anything but simply keep your finger on your lips to signify that you would not talk, or he should not talk. Bewilderment of love is a bird that silences you. It puts a lid on the mouth of your cauldron and causes greater boiling in you. This is what happens to a searcher or lover of God that within lies inside, he is highly enthusiastic but, on the outside, totally silent and dumbfounded

chapters.title: Via Media and Direct Observation
chapters.subtitle: The king’s deliberately asking Ayaz as to: why you speak so much to the leather coat and sandals which are lifeless objects about your joys and sorrows? This, the king asked to make Ayaz speak out to him; as otherwise Ayaz would not speak out, of his own

paras: King Mahmood asked Ayaz: why do you love your sandals so much just as an idol worshipper loves his idols. Like Majnun who had made Laila’s face, you have made your sandals as your religion and faith. You have mixed up tow old things with your life that you have hanged them both on the walls of your room. How much do you want to talk to these two things? You try to pour out the breath of your old secrets upon two lifeless materials. Like the Arab for his camps and dunes, you enlarge the talks of your love. Of what destination of Asaf, (the prime minister of H. Sulaiman) are your sandals? You consider them as the shirt of H. Yusuf which gave back light to the eyes to his father, H. Yakub. You count before your sandals like the Christian does of his sins of fornication, misappropriation and enmities of one year before the bishop to seek pardon, thinking that the bishop’s pardon is like God’s pardon.

sections.heading: Magic of Belief and Love
paras: The bishop is not aware of crime and justice, but it is the belief and love for him in the Christian’s mind that does the magic. Love, in its imagination, creates hundreds of Yusufs. It is a greater magician that Haroot and Maroot. It creates an image of the beloved within itself, and the attraction of this image compels you to talk to it. You speak of thousands of your secrets before this image, just as a friend does with a friend. There is neither a picture nor an idol before hm, but love gives rise to hundreds of questions and answers.

sections.heading: Child’s Grave as a Solace for Grief
paras: This is like what a sorrowful mother does before the grave of a recently dead child. She goes on speaking with efforts of her secrets. That lifeless grave appears full of life for her. She considers its mud living and holding. Look at this great magic of love. In her view, every particle of the dust of the grave possesses ears and consciousness giving consolation to her grief. She considers the dust to be all hearing, considering it to possess ears and eyes. In this manner, she keeps herself busy in crying and keeping her face on the dust of a fresh grave in such a manner that she had not kept her face on the son’s face during his lifetime. After the passing over of a few days of mourning, the fire of her love for the son gets cold. Love with a dead person is not lasting. Therefore, one should make love with ever living God who enhances the enthusiasm of one’s soul. After days the another feels peace like sleeping with that grave comfortably. Her lack of sense gets increased in the company of the sensationless mud of the grave. The spell of her love slowly loses its effectiveness and totally vanishes, because fire, after tis fast burning gets converted into ash.

sections.heading: Love for God Exhibits God
paras: What ever ignorant young man sees in the bright mirror is seen by an elderly, godly person in a dull brick. Your love for God is your elderly, godly guide, not the old man with white beard, your love for God can guide not only you but other lakhs of desperate persons like you. Love creates so many images of the beloved in separation from the beloved, which upon meeting appear like the actuals, each of which declaring: “I was the base of your consciousness and unconsciousness. What all you saw in your imagination was actually a reflection of my actuality. Now I am lifting the curtains that are between myself and you, exhibiting my beauty in all clarity. This is my grace for you as you had been trying to find me through my reflections. Earlier, you did not have the power to see my beauty and therefore, booked at them from behind the curtains, in the form of my actions and attributes. But now you have become strong enough to look at My essence itself in a direct way.” [a hadith says: since response in worship should be like your seeing God Himself; and if you cannot see, you should feel that God’s seeing you. Sufis consider this to mean as though you see God’s essence and not just his actions and attributes. At this you cease to exist and get annihilated in Him, upon which you feel that God is seeing you. The curtain between yourself and God is the curtain of your body or self — Qazi Sajjad Husain]. Earlier you were seeing Me through the impacts that I had cast upon you. But now, you are not seeing or feeling the impacts, but you are directly seeing me.

sections.heading: Good Acts of the Pious Are Sins of the Godly
paras: At this stage, the lover start seeking forgievance for the mistake of seeing of God through curtains. This mistake is forgiven by God and along with forgievance, he is given the reward of God’s own appearance before Him. This is the situation of the saying: Hasanaatul abraari sayyi ‘aatul muqarribiin: sincere responses of the good ones are the evils of those nearby to God.

When water gushes forth from a rock, the rock disappears in water collected around it in the fountain. Upon this no one calls the rock as rock, as its pearls get out of it in the form of drops of water. Consider their worship as the reflection of God in cups, in which whatever is put by God makes them attain higher levels.

chapters.title: Liala Was Not That Beautiful
chapters.subtitle: Telling of the relatives of Majnun to him: “Liala is not that beautiful. There are many more beautiful’s in the city. We can present, one, two or ten before you so that you may choose one among them and secure relief for you and for us.” And Majnun’s repley to them

paras: Some ill-witted fellows in their ignorance, told Majnun: “Laila’s beauty is no that much. It is just normal. There are lakhs of more beautiful beloveds than her in our city with moon like faces. There are thousands of graceful beauties like Houries. You may choose one among them for you. You may relieve yourself and us of anxiety about your affair and also put an end to this madness of love and save yourself from blame for the love of one from another place.”

sections.heading: Beauty a Matter of Taste
paras: Majnun said: “Face is like a vessel and beauty is like wine in it. God provides me wine to drink from that vessel. But he is giving you vinegar from the same vessel, so that her love may not pull your ears as of maddened fellows. With the same vessel he gives both honey and poison to different persons. You look only at the vessel and poison to different persons. You look only at the vessel, as wine does not show its face to indecent eyes. Just as chaste maidens restraining their glances (Qasiraatu altarfi) (Rahman: 55: 56) are the taste of the souls, who do not show themselves except to those of worth and taste. They are always hidden in their tents like the wine in vessels from the eyes of the unworthy.

“Similarly, a river is like a tent full of life for the duck, but it is death for the crows. Poison is a means of food and life for the snake, but for others, it is pain and death. Every effort and its result are like hell for one, and paradise for another. Everything that you see has food and poison which you cannot see. Everybody that you see is like a cup and bowl, in which there is food as well as things that burn the heart. There are provisions of food in the bowl which are hidden from the eyes. It is only the eater who knows about the contents.

sections.heading: Different Impacts on Different People
paras: “H. Yusuf’s face was like a vessel containing pleasing wines, from which his father, used to drink varieties of drinks. But it was a poisonous water for his brothers, which was increasing the poison of hate and jealousy in their hearts. And from the same, Zulaikha extracted sweetness through her love as a different kind of wine. Apart from what H. Yaqub had from H. Yusuf, there was a different food for that maiden. There are varieties of wine, but in just one vessel, so that you may not have any doubt about the invisible wines. Wine belongs to the hidden, unseen, world and very much hidden from us, but the vessel belongs to this material world and quite clear before us. These wines are very much hidden from the eyes of the disinterested, underserving people, but are quite clear to be seen by the worthy and converted people. [the underserving and disinterested are intoxicated with a different kind of wine which takes away their sense of seeing].”

sections.heading: Effects Reveal the Cause
paras: O God! Forgive us; as our sins have become so heavy that they have weakened our eyesight. You have filled up with light all the space between the two easts, yet you are hidden. You are the revealer of our hidden secrets. You gush forth rivers, but you are hidden from us. You are like water, and we are like the water wheel. You are like the air and we are like dust. The air is invisible, but the dust is visible. You are like the spring season, and we are like the green, fresh gardens. You are hidden but Your grants are clear before us. You are like the soul, and we are like the hands and feet which are opened and closed by the soul.

You are like wisdom and we like tongue, which gets the capacity to talk from wisdom. You are like joy, and we are joyous, being products of the pleasure-giving joy. Our movement at every moment are the proof of the fact that they are due to the grant of the everlasting Grandeur. Motion of the grinding stone gives the proof of impacts of the water of the stream.

sections.heading: God: Imagined Through Examples
paras: You are far beyond our thinking and speaking. I am just giving examples and similarities to speak about You which is an attempt for which I need to be chastised and disgraced. Man is helpless and compelled to resort to examples as he cannot remain contented with thoughts alone. He cannot imagine Your beautiful, pleasing essence. He considers himself to be under your impacts at every moment. He is obliged to think of You in his limited capacities and senses, like the shepherd who was telling you: “O God! Come before this loving shepherd of yours, so that He may pick lice from Your clothes, stitch sandals for You and hold on to Your lapel.”

There was none like that shepherd in the extent of his love and devotion to God but in the matter of praising Him and talking about Him, he was totally wrong. His love for God had pitched his tent upon the sky, his honorable soul had become a petty watchful dog at the tent.

The shepherd said all this because his love for God was in his heart so full fo turmoil as the ocean. The great motion of the ocean of love had dashed his heart making him to say what all he said. But the same motion did not touch your heart but only your ears. You cannot understand the gravity of his love for God.

chapters.title: Physical and Spiritual Impacts
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a buffoon putting on women’s mantle, sitting in a gathering of women audiences during a sermon and committing a funny act, which made a woman know that he was a man and he cried out at that

paras: There was a popular speaker under whose pulpit there were men and women to hear. A buffoon with a covered face and mantle on his head projecting himself as a woman sat along with women in the gathering. A person asked the speaker in low tone as to whether the pubic hair caused defect in salat. The speaker said: “long pubic hair are a cause of dislike in salat. You should remove them with a blade or hair remover so as to make your prayer perfect.” The question again asked him: “up to what length it is alright for the perfectness of prayer?” the speaker angrily said: if they become long enough to the size of maize, you chronic questioner! It becomes duteous to remove them.”

A woman was sitting in front of the buffoon who was hearing the speaker with full attention. The buffoon told her: “sister, please check up! My hair might have gone to that size, please, for God’s sake, see whether they have grown to the length of disliking “. The women inserted her hand in his trousers, thinking him to be a woman and happened to touch the male genitals. she gave a cry of surprise and shock. Hearing this from the pulpit, the speaker thought that she was giving a cry of applause upon being impressed by hearing his speech and was highly pleased. He told the audience: “You should learn to appreciate the truth of statement from that woman that have impacted upon her heart.” The buffoon said: “the impact was not upon her heart by upon her hand.”

sections.heading: Impact of on Hand and Heart
paras: You may think over if you are wise, as to what the impact would be upon the heart instead of upon the hand. The impact upon the heart is uncomparable. There was a little impact of H. Musa upon the hearts of the magicians because of which their hand became as good as sticks. Cutting of their hands and legs was the same as cutting off of wood. Logs of hand and legs did not cause even that much anxiety for them as the loss of walking-stick from the hand of an old. The magicians announced when their hands and legs were ordered to cut off: No matter: La dhaira: (Shu ‘ra: 26: 50). This announcement reached upon the sky. They meant: “Okay! Cut them off our soul got rid of the pain of life. We have come to know that real life is not of the body but of the soul. we live with soul, not with the body

sections.heading: Show Business of Pseudo Saints and Scholars
paras: Know this: whoever understood himself, understood God. He built an everlasting palace in the peaceful surroundings. A child cries for walnuts and currants which are of little worth for the wise. Body is like walnut and currant for the heart. A child does not reach to the level of the wisemen. One who is not aware of his worth is like a child and a really grown-up man will not care for the bodily tastes. If a person is a man merely by his possession of beard and male genitals, then it may be seen that the goat also has these things. A goat marches ahead of other goats in taking them nearer the butcher. It is a bad leader. There are many such men who go on combing their beards as a mark of sophistication and superiority to present themselves as leaders. They ae of course leaders, but toward pain and sorrows. Be careful not be like them. Ignore the beard and resort to proper means to lead, and give up your pride, arrogance and showiness. You have made your beard itself a matter of laughingstock. Your beard is a sign of maturity and arrival of wisdom. It is not a matter for false pretention as is done by many Pseudo-saints and scholars. You should be like the fragrance of flowers, which leads the lovers toward garden. And the fragrance of men is nothing but wisdom and intellect, which is the best leader toward the garden of eternity.

chapters.title: Faith Is Nothing but Advice
chapters.subtitle: The king’s further order to Ayaz to explain clearly about his attachment for leather coat and sandals, so that his colleagues may get clear guidance as faith and sincerity are like advice

paras: The king told Ayaz: “reveal the secrets of the sandals as to why they are so attractive for you, so that the other slave sunqar and colleagues may hear about it. O Ayaz! Your slavery got light from you and ran toward the heavens from its low level. It has become so honorable that free people crave for slavery, as you have given a different life to slavery. A man-of-faith is so strong in the ups and downs of the tides that the infidels feel regret for their deprivation.

chapters.title: Real Faith and Appearing Faith
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a Zoroastrian during the days of Shaikh Bayazid, (may his secrets be holy), who was told to become a muslim and his retort there on

paras: There was a Zoroastrian during the days of H. Bayazid, who was told by a noble muslim to become a muslim. He told him: it would be very good if you follow Islam so as to get hundreds of deliverances and success.”

He said: “O good disciple! If faith is that which the master of the world, Bayazid has, I do not have the strength to adopt it, as it is beyond the struggles of the soul. Though I do not have faith and confidence on the religion of Muslims, but I have full faith in his faith. I have a faith that his faith is far above the faith of all others. He is a person of high sensibilities, frankness, and grandeur. I have a faith upon his faith in secrets, but there is strong seal upon my mouth, and I cannot reveal it. And if you mean by faith, your faith, I have no inclination toward it nor any desire for it. Even if a man with great inclination looks at you, his inclination would vanish, because your faith is only in name. it has no meaning and spirit. This is like people calling a forest as a place of refuge. When he looks at your faith, his love for becoming a muslim will simply go cold.
“Know and remember well this narrative, if you are sensible, and ignore two external appearance and hear about the truth and meaning.

chapters.title: Muezzin with Crude Voice
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a Muezzin with crude voice calling for prayer in a country of infidels and an infidel’s offering him gifts

paras: A muezzin had a very harsh voice. He used to tear off his own throat by reciting loudly for the whole night. He had spoiled the sound sleep of the people. All sane and sundry suffered headache with his voice. Children panicked and woke up from sleep. Both men and women were victims of his torturous voice.

To get rid of this headache and trouble, people joined together to collect funds. They called him and gave him the money saying: “My dear sir, we have enjoyed your voice. You have graced us with it day and night. Because of the richness of your voice, we have lost our sleep from many days. In order to have some comfort for yourself, you may be pleased to keep your mouth shut and in its place, you may concentrate on inner spiritual matters.”.

The muezzin took the money with pleasure. At that time, a caravan left for ka’aba. He joined the caravan and went with it. On the way, the caravan camped at night in a region of infidels. The muezzin, in love with his own voice, wanted to give the Azan call, inspite of the advice of many not to say the Azan as it might result in many quarrels and enmities. He rejected this advice and gave the Azan call. People feared that some mischief may ensure; but an infidel came over with a lamp, sweets and costly garments as presents like a friend, making enquiries about the muezzin whose voice gave them great relief. They were surprised as to what relief could that nasty voice given by reaching into their temple, an asked him about it.

He said: “I have a very nice, and beautiful daughter. She was very desirous of becoming a muslim. This madness never went out of her mind, even though many infidels advised her against it. The love for the faith had become very strong in her. This worry was like a fireplace, with me in it, like agarwood. Caught in this grip, I suffered great pain and trouble, as her inclination toward this desire was persistent and continuous. I was not finding any means of getting out of this trouble when this muezzin recited his Azan. The girl enquired as to what was this frightening voice, two or four bits of which had fallen into her ear, saying” in my entire life I have not heard such a ferocious sound in any fire temple and idol home.” Her sister said: “this is a call of Azan which is announcement symbol of the Muslims”. But she did not believe it and enquired with another. He also said: “that is the truth, my dear moon.”

“When she got it confirmed, her face became pale, and she got disappointed with muslimness. I got rid of my anxiety and troubles and had the occasion to have sound sleep last night after a long time. This ferocious sound gave me a great relief with my daughter’s change of mind. I want to express my thanks to the muezzin and give him gifts. Where is he?”

When that man looked at the muezzin he said: “please accept this gift, as you have given me great relief and help. For the gratefulness and obligation, you have put me into, I have become your slave forever. Were I to be an exceptional person in wealth, possessions and rulership, I would have filled your mouth with gold”.
The Zoroastrian who was called upon to become a muslim told the inviter.: “your faith is mere treachery and worldly. It is a dacoit and deviator from the right path like that type of Azan.”

chapters.title: Are Body and Soul Different?
chapters.subtitle: Return to the narrative of the infidel and the muslim in the matter of faith

paras: The infidel continued: “But by considering the faith and sincerity of H. Bayazid, many desires and ambitions came into my heart and soul. These are as unusual on the right side as that woman’s desires on the wrong side. Who looking at the coupling of the donkeys had cried out: Ah! What a wonderful male the donkey is? Considering this coupling that the donkey does, what husbands do with wives is nothing but passing urine on our private parts.” (This story of the woman’s affair with donkey is earlier narrated).

H. Bayazid fulfilled all the rights and demands of faith in entirety. All praises for such an unusual lion! If a drop of his faith enters into an ocean, the entire ocean would sink into his drop. It is like a sparklet of fire in the forest that destroys the entire forest in entirety. So also like a thought in the mind of a king who along with his army wages a war and destroys the enemies.

sections.heading: Impacts of H. Muhammad’s Light
paras: “When a single star of God’s support appeared into H. Muhammad, it destroyed the infidelity of every infidel and jew. A single star arose into H. Muhammad and spread its light so much that entire infidelity from east its light so much that entire infidelity from east to west vanished. One who accepted his religion entered into peace, and the infidelity of the rest fell into doubts and suspicions. Their infidelity turned into something different from its earlier state. Their earlier pure infidelity could not continue. Either it got muslimised or got mixed up with uncertainties. Either they become zimmies (those under the protection of Muslims) or namesake Muslims, only in appearance. I can cite the faith of Bayazid only as an example to compare with yours. But this comparison is virtually uncomparable. It is like mixing together oil and water with efforts. These examples are uncomparable with each other even to the extent of a particle of light.

sections.heading: Impacts of Soul Through Body Alone
paras: “a particle is nothing in comparison with the entire body. It cannot be a distributor of the entire invisible light. Speaking of a particle may be considered as the unexplainable hidden secret of the body. It is not the secret bearer and expresser of the ocean, but only of its foam. If the bright sun of the faith of the master (shaikh) rises from the eastern side of his soul, spreading its light, all lowly vallies including the inner contents of earth, will be filled up with treasures, and the elevated portion would become green and fresh like the gardens of paradise. He possesses the soul of a brightening light though with a body made of worthless mud. I am in great puzzle to call him as his body or that soul. You may tell me, if you know, as my study of the shaikh has put me into great confusion and search. If he is this, body, my brother, then what is that soul with the light of which all the seven heavens have become bright. Has this been done by his body or by his soul? If you say, it is due to his soul, then, what is his body. How strange! What is this of the two or who is this of the two.

chapters.title: Body and Soul Go Together
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a wife who said to her husband that the cat ate away the meat. Husband weighed the cat in a balance and found it to weigh half a measure. He told his wife; the meat was of half a measure in weight or a little more. If what is weighed out is meat where is the cat’s weight? And if its is the cat’s weight, where has the meat gone?

paras: A homely man had a wife, who was very talkative, ill tempered and thievish. She used to spoil everything he brought home. The husband tolerated all this silently but at last, he lost his temper. One day, after hard work, he brought meat to treat his guests. The wife made fried chops and ate it all with liquor. Upon returning home, the husband told her that the guest has come, and it is required that delicious dish must be placed before the guest. He asked her to keep it ready. The wife said: “the cat ate away all the meat. If you want meaty dish, you may bring meat again”.

The husband told the servant to bring the weighing balance telling that he would weigh the cat. He weighed the cat, and it weighed half a mann. (a measure of those days in that region, as it was different measure in different countries). He told her: “what you say is not right. The meat was more than half a mann and the cat weighs just half a mann. Meat was more than half a mann and the cat is just half a mann. If this weight is of the cat, what happened to the meat that it ate. And if this is the weight of the meat, what happened to the weight of the cat? Where is the cat? Show me the cat!”

In this manner, if we consider H. Bayazid’s body as H. Bayazid, what is his soul? And if he is soul, what about his body? If we think over this, there are wonders in wonders. This is neither your job my friend or mine. Neither you can know nor can I. the simple answer could be, that the body and soul are: one like the harvested crop and other like the farmland. Seed is the base and plant is the product. Grain is the base and flour is the product. (They cannot come about without each other). God’s wisdom has tied together these two opposites. Neck and the kidney are far away from each other in the body, but the butcher knows that they are connected with each other and dependent upon each other. Soul cannot do any job without the body and the body without soul is cold and frigid. Know this my friend that a body without soul is more lowly than mud. Soul is like the pulp and body is like the rind. A body without life is of no use. ] therefore you should try to give life to your body. Your soul is hidden but your body is visible. The jobs of the world go about by them in togetherness.

If you hit dust on someone’s head, it does not break the head. So also, if you hit the head with water. If you want to break the head, you have to mix the dust and water and make a lump. When you break the head, the soul as its base and life, goes away from it to its place; and the mud of the body goes towards mud. This is what that happens on the day of judgement. They get separated. God’s wisdom in bringing them together met its object of the separation of the good and bad through the respective obedience and disobedience. When they were together in the world.

There are therefore, there are other combinations which no eye has seen and no ear heard. If the ears were to hear about them, they would not be ears and more and lose the hearing faculty and be not in a position to keep them under control. If the sun puts its glances on ice and snow, there would be no ice and snow. They would convert into water without any kind of control and resistance and get impacted even by soft, mild breeze to form ripples appearing in the form of coat of mail. Then it becomes the life of every tree providing medicine to treat all sicknesses and make it fortunate to boom. The frigid, humble ice had warned the trees: “touch me not”. Its body does not love anyone, nor it is worthy of being loved. Its functioning is nothing but miserliness and self-interest. Yet it is not totally useless. Its coolness freshens the liver and heart of man, though it is not a messenger of the king of Greenery to give life to plants.

O Ayaz! Your star is in great heights. It does not like to ride upon any constellation. Your boldness cannot appreciate every sincerity. The level of your cleanliness cannot be resorted to by every cleanliness.

chapters.title: Drinking and Denial of Wine
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the slave of a rich man who orders him to go out and bring a flask of wine. On the way a pious man gave him advice against wine and hit a stone on the flask and broke it off. The rich man came to know of it and went out to punish and kill the pious man, and the pious man ran away from his sight. This narrative relates to the days of H. Isa. When wine was not yet prohibited. But the pious man considered wine as vicious and was preventing people from pleasures and enjoyments.

paras: There was a rich man of pleasant nature, fond of drinks, very helpful to every needy and was a liquor addict. He was generous, benevolent, just, helper of the poor, and large-hearted. He was like the king of the brave, and leader of the faithful, protector of the pathways, knower of secrets and far-sighted. This was during the days and period of H. Isa Masih, when people were kind, soft and away from mischiefs.

One night, without prior information, a guest came to his house, who was also of the same nature like him, commanding and pious. As per their usual, they were in need of wine and in those days, wine was a permissible, usual drink. The host had deficiency of it and so told the slave: “Bring a flask of wine from so and so priest, as he sells wines of special qualities to provide relief to all and elite. One sip of that priests’ wine has such impacts which thousands of pots and flasks of others do.

A great treasure is kept hidden in wine just as a powerful king is hidden in a royal dress. So also, saints are hidden under torne clothes. Do not look at his blackened torne old apparel. He is like gold plated with black paint.

To avoid the evil impacts of the wrong people he has made himself dislikable, but he is a ruby covered up with smoke. You may know that treasure and gems are not to be found at homes but are to be found in ruins and discarded places. As the wealth of H. Adam was hidden and buried under the mud of his body, it became a curtain for the eyes of the accursed Satan. He looked contemptuously at the mud, but his soul told him; “my mud is a hiding wall for you.”

sections.heading: Impacts of Wine on Man
paras: The slave took two empty flasks from his house and ran fast and soon entered into the church of the priests. He paid gold to that priest and purchased wine sparkling like gold. This was as though he gave a stone to the seller and in return purchased a gem. The wine that impacts upon the head of the kings, keeps a crown upon the head of the cupbearer. It raises many mischiefs and turmoil’s and brings about mixing up of servants and masters. After drinking wine, man loses the possessions of his bones and flesh and becomes the soul in entirety. Both the throne and the scaffold become the same for him. People are different and distinct from each other in their senses like oil and water, which never mix; but under intoxication they get mixed up like body and soul. This is just as meat and wheat sink into each other in soup (Harisa) which are no more forward and backward against each other and not at all distinct and different. There is no difference between the ingredients of soup. All differences sink into each other.

After buying the wine, the slave was carrying the wine flask toward the mansion of his master, a forlorn monk full of sorrows, pains and upset dry mind came before him. His body and heart had melted in the fire of the love of God containing nothing else in the heart other than God. Because of excessive worship and devotion to Go there were thousand of their markings on his heart. He used to undergo the harsh impacts of austerities every moment being attached to them day and night. For months and years, he was overlapped with his own blood resulting in the running away and loss of patience and contentment at midnight time.

When he saw a slave of good conduct running fast at the dead of night, he enquired with him about the contents of the flask. He said: “It is wine!” He asked: “for whom?” He replied that “it is for that great lord. It belongs to that great seeker of God’s grandeur.” He said: “what is this? A seeker of God’s grandeur engaging himself in the pleasure of wine. He ought to prevent himself from delicious foods and drinks! He drinks the wine of devil and yet holds on to sharp senses of godliness? Normal senses themselves are so dull decimated without wine. Your efforts should be to sharpen your senses and consciousness by clubbing them with other senses and consciousness. Instead of this if you intoxicate yourself with wine, you will be nowhere. You should know that you are caught in the thirst of wine just as a bird is caught in the net spread over by the hunter.”

chapters.title: Pride of Tallness
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of Zia Balkhi who was tall in height and his brother shaikhul Islam (great scholar teacher) who was of short in height. The shaikhul islam used to feel ashamed of his brother for his tall height. One day, Ziabulkhi came to the class of shaikhul Isam where great scholars of Balkh were present to learn. After some time, Zia Balkhi left the class. As was his usual Shaikhul Islam stood up to honour him by standing half of his height upon his knees. Zia sarcastically said: “you are quite tall by stealing half of the height

paras: Zia Balkhi, brother of Shaikhul Islam (great scholar and teacher) was very humorous. People used to be with shaikhul Islam for his great scholarship, to seek knowledge. He was like the crown of scholarship in the city of Balkh. But he was of very short height like of a chick. The shaikh was unique in scholarship and highly learned, and therefore very proud and dominating inspite of his short height as against his brother, Zia Balkhi who was of tall height, but liked by the people for his humorous nature. The shaikh used to feel ashamed of his brother Zia Balkhi who was also a great scholar and teacher.

One day Zia came over to the shaikh’s class which was full of judges and very eminent, selected scholars and judges. The shaikh stood up at half his height (on the knees) with all pride to honour his brother. When Zia found pride occupying his mind, he put him to shame by saying: “You are tall in only making money from your admirers with which you have even stolen some height from your cypress like height.”

chapters.title: Wine Not Needed for Elites
chapters.subtitle: Return to the narrative of the monk and the slave of the rich man

paras: The monk continued to speak to the wine-carrying slave: “where are your senses and wisdom so as to drink wine, O enemy of wisdom! You may apply a blue dot on the face of a fair, beautiful face to make it more attractive. Applying the same blue dot on the face of a black Abyssinian is a matter of laughter. But, when the light of consciousness itself has not come in you, mistaken fellow, why do you want to control it through the darkness of the intoxication of wine? The practice is to search for shade during the daytime, but you are searching for shade in a clouded night. Wine is made permissible for the common folk, but it ought to be prohibited for those in search of truth. Lovers of God drink the blood of their own love and heart and set their eyes on the path and place of God. The way for the search of God is through frightening forests, but you are trying to lead the people with a wisdom held behind hundreds of eclipses. You ere throwing dust into the eyes of leaders and thus misguiding and destroying the caravans.

sections.heading: Xxxx Showed Be Crushed (Page 457--- Not Visible)
