paras: xxxx Bread of Corn, though a lowly food is xxxxxxxx visible to eat, but even this is not worthy for xxxxxx self. It has to be fed with a still more lowly bread of husk. Your mischievous, misguiding self is your enemy on the way to God. Put it to shame and weaken and dishonor it. Do not provide the pulpit to it to speak of its misguiding sermons. Instead of the pulpit, it is worthy of standing at the scaffold. You should try to cut off the had of the thief. If you are not capable of cutting it off, at least tie it down. if you do not tie his hand, he will tie down your hands. If you do not break his legs, he will break yours.
Instead of doing this, you are providing wine and sugarcane to the enemy. Why do you do this? Tell him to drink poison and fill his mouth with dust.”

So saying, the monk took a stone and hit it on the flask and shattered it, without caring for the consequence. The slave threw down the broken flask and took to xxxxxxx and ran fast to his master (page 458------- not visible)

chapters.title: Harsh Words Treated by Xxxxx
chapters.subtitle: The lord’s going toward xxxx in extreme anger to punish xxxx

paras: The slave went before xxxxx xxxxxx hands, and the lord enquired xxxxxxxx (pg 459) slave, started about everything that happened one after another. The lord became fiery and got up saying: “show me his residence so that I may hit upon his head with this heavy mace and smash it off. A head that is devoid of wisdom, born of an indecent mother. What does that doggish know of the command of enforcement of good acts. He is after cheap popularity, name and fame, to make a place for himself through treacheries and designs. He does not have any capacity to come up in life excepting by playing tricks with this and that man. If he is taken as mad and mischievous, the only treatment is with the whip made of the bull’s sex organ, so that his devil is chased out of his head. A donkey does not mine without the beating of the master.”

So saying, the lord came out with the mace in his hand and went to the monk at night in a half inebriated state. He wanted to kill him in at most anger, but the monk hid himself under the heap of corded wool. He was hearing his angry words from under the heap of wool of the coir makers saying to himself: “viciousness of man spoken word by word can be faced by a mirror or steel, which keeps its own mouth shut. To face such a person, a man has to have a face as hard as that steel mirror and be able to say to look at his own ferocious ugly face in it.

chapters.title: Meaning Less Sounds to Increase Anger
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the Clown who defeated the king, syed shah of Tirmiz, in chess game

paras: The king played chess with a clown, who defeated him in the game upon which the king felt great anger for him. The clown started saying “shush, shush”. Upon this the arrogant king started hitting him with the chess pieces saying: “take this as a reward for your “shush, shush”, o nasty fellow!” the clown kept quiet and sought the king’s pardon.

The king asked him to play another game and the clown started shivering like a naked man in winter. He played another game, and the king lost the game again, resulting in the occasion of saying “shush, shush”, once again. The clown jumped away from the place and went into a corner and put on six blankets to hide himself under them out of fear of beatings. The king said: “what is this you have done?” the clown said: “O great King! Shush, shush, shush, shush! How can truth be said other than from under the blanket, in particular before the king like your majesty wearing a bright dress decorated with anger and fire?
Your majesty was defeated in the game, and I was defeated by your majesty’s beatings. I can say shush, shush, only from under the clothes.

chapters.title: Unplanned Actions Result in Loss
chapters.subtitle: The Lord’s arriving at the monk’s door and topping it with kicks Prophet Muhammad’s attempts to drop himself from Mount Hira because of despair and delay in sighting; and Jibra‘iil’s appearance and entreating him not to drop himself as great tortures and successes are in wait for him.

paras: When the people of the locality heard the Lord making challenges, accusations upon the monk and the sound of beatings on his door, they came out of their houses from the right and left side and told the lord: “O Lord! This is a time for maintaining patience and consonance! The brain of the monk has dried up and his wisdom is lesser than that of children. Because of his old age and deprivation, he has gone very weak and further, denial of worldly pleasures has not given him any expansion of the heart. He has worked hard on this line but has not been rewarded for his pains. He has done his job but has not received his wages. Either his work itself was of no worth, or the time of reward by God has not yet come. Either his efforts were useless like those of the Jews, or the reward is to come at a time, which has not yet arrived. The troubles and pains he is undergoing are themselves enough for him as he is helpless in the valley of love which is much blood sucking.

sections.heading: Bad Results of Unplanned Actions
paras: “Because of these deprivation, his eyes are in pain compelling him to live a secluded life with swollen face and hanging lips. There is no physician to treat the pain of his eyes by applying appropriate medicine nor he has the wisdom to go in search of the physician or medicine. He is carrying on his efforts without certainly of thoughts but only on doubts and suspicions. Until he comes to realize the truth of matters, he will be in such doubts for this reason, the path leading to the destination of the beloved is still far away for him, because what he is in love with is only the rind of the fruit and not the pulp resulting in an imbalance of mind. as a result of all this, at times, he is angry with God as he has not received anything other than sorrows from His court. Sometimes, he quarrels with his own fate as all others in the world are flying high while his feathers are all cut off.

“Whoever that is entangled in the material world of colors and fragrances lives a life of hardship and narrowness, even if he is pious and monkish. So long as he is held up in this narrow camp, he cannot get outward good conduct and inner expansion. That is why it is necessary that a monk and pious person should not be provided with a sword and knife in his loneliness, until attained the expansion of his breast, as there is a fear that out of the constriction of his heart, failures and sorrows, he may tear off his own belly.
Failures in the achievements of worldly gains is better than success as successes make him ill-tempered and arrogant.

sections.heading: Despair Results in Desire for Death
paras: (on the first occasion, H. Jibra‘iil brought the message of God: the first five verses of Surah Iqra (Alaq: 96) directing him to 1) read in the Lord’s name who created in general (all creations), 2) created man from clot of coagulated blood, 3) again to read in the name of the generous Lord, 4) who taught with the pen, and 5) taught man what he know not. The noble Prophet was as dumbed at the strange event and message.

He was taken by his wife to Waraqa, a Christian monk who told him that this revelation was only for him; and later many more will come for the purpose of all others, subsequent to this, for a long time, there was no revelation. This period is called Fatarah (intermission) which came to end with revelation of surah (Muddath(s)ir-74) in which he was ordered to get out and proclaim the message of God. This period of interruption has great significance that the Prophet was to contemplate on creation (of everything). Material, non-material etc.), creation of man in particular from clot (coagulated blood), teaching by God with pen to all men or humanity, what initially man did not know.

sections.heading: What Is “Pen”
paras: This word “pen” also signifies the need of something to write upon, Pen is of no wroth without something to write upon: slate, leather plate, paper etc. if we contemplate upon this we can ascertain that everything of everything: sun, moon, earth, plants, animals, universe, air, water, animal soul, human soul — material, non-material, mental, intellectual, spiritual — all is written down upon all things themselves about everything relating to them and interrelating to each other with the invisible pen of God. That is to say: all knowledge of everything is written in the thing itself. For example: all knowledge about the eye: its structure, qualities, properties, its different parts, their individual and collective functions, their defects, sicknesses and cures and medicines etc., are all written in the eye itself. By studying all these from the earliest time to our days volumes and volumes are written down by various men with their physical pens on paper all clubbed together under the subject of ophthalmology.

Similar is the case of all chemicals: Sulphur, copper, oxygen etc, under the subject of chemistry. About rocks, minerals, their origin, properties, applications etc., under the subject of geology. And there are hundreds of subjects to study nature and to study the creator of all things, God. Subjects like physics, Astronomy, Botany, zoology, oceanology etc. there is a never-ending process. All knowledge is from the study of those very objects and subjects. This is what the Prophet was directed to read, study, through contemplation, which he did during this long period of Fatara (intermission)] which is taken as from six months to four years by different authorities. Whatever the time, long or short, the Prophet contemplated, and all the questions and answers were revealed in subsequent revelation of about 20 years till his death containing points, questions and answers which are aplenty in the Quran, which can be taken under various subjects of our days like Astronomy, Geology, Botany, zoology, psychology, politics, economics, sociology, law, morals, etc, etc, from which further volumes and volumes have been written.

sections.heading: Great Progress of the Quran
paras: Great works of many of the scientists of the period of muslim glory of muslim world received inspiration and guidance from these points, questions and answers in the Quran, which because the source of scientific and intellectual progress in Europe after these Arabic books were translated initially into Latin and later in germen, French, English etc., when Europe entered into modern age from the 16th century AC onwards after a long period of dark ages of about 1500 years ever since the collapse of Greek and Roman Culture.

Scientists, Philosophers, Jurists and Social and political reformers are not historians, and historians are not scientists, philosophers, jurists and political reformers. Therefore, a great curtain hangs between the Muslim achievements and modern progress. Plus, there was a deliberate attempt to hide and distort facts for political and economic reasons from sixteenth century onwards. Further, Muslim the critical knowledge developed into high technology of those days resulting in loss of theoretical knowledge and loss of interest in reading and teaching of books. Commercial systems including banking) metallurgical, medical systems, guns, weapons military victories, legal processes, establishment of judiciary, rules of evidence. Political and administrative systems, various types of fabrics cutlery, perfumes cousins, etc., etc., of those days were their gifts, which penetrated into modern civilization everywhere and after Muslims defeats from 16th century onwards, spread throughout the other dark parks of the world by their European conquerors.

Just as military victory of the Romans over Greeks was a cultural victory of the Greeks over the Romans and through them to many other parts of the world, European victory on muslim world would result in the victory of Islamic culture and civilization on Europe; and through Europeans particularly the English, French and Dutch peoples took Muhammad’s civilization and culture all over the world.

sections.heading: Extraordinary Knowledge Needs Extraordinary Training
paras: Thus, when the Quran became a source and promoter of so many sciences, its receiver had to be an extra-ordinary personality, unique in history, without one like him earlier and later. His mind had to be the most fertile, well-watered and well manured soil to germinate the seeds of all these sciences. And that was accomplished by Fatsa (intermission) for a long period of time during which he underwent a strange mental and spiritual exercises, sometimes resulting in despair to the extent of his feeling like dropping himself from the top of the hill, which is narrated in the following lines by Rumi. We do not hear or read of any other scholar or leader in the world undergoing such agony in making attempts to kill himself to get rid of it. Here also Muhammad is unique — Translator]

When the Prophet felt extreme constriction of the chest during the period of intermission, due to non-receipt of further messages from God, he used to feel like dropping himself from a top the hill of Hira which he had made as the center of information in which he had received the first message. H. Jibra‘iil used to prevent him from doing so, saying that God has kept many treasures for him in His command of Kun (be). The Prophet would stay quiet at the time. Yet again, the feeling of separation from the Beloved after the earlier meeting again attack him. Again, he would, out of great sorrow and pain, think of felling himself upside down from the hill. Again, H. jibra‘iil would come and tell him not to do as you are an exceptional and unique king of knowledge. This was his trial and pain until the time when he got the unmatchable pearl (of extra-ordinary wisdom and knowledge) into his pocket.

sections.heading: Man Sacrifices Himself for Some Cause
paras: This is how men put themselves in death-like situation of all kinds of troubles, yet they bear with them. Despair and lack of confidence is the root cause of all troubles. Godly people in their love for God, similarly, put themselves in the situations of self-destruction and people feel strange at this. This is inspite of the fact that everyone of us has this tendency of sacrificing himself for some cause. That man is worthy of admiration, who sacrifices his body for the sake of the cause that deserves this sacrifice. A searcher of truth sacrifices himself for such achievement, which have a hundred lives in one sacrifice. Love, lover and the beloved are always considered as fortunate and worthy of appreciation.

Everyone in the world is engaged in sacrificing himself for something which involves him in it for the whole life and up to the death. His loss of life in his efforts to meet his object; or in actual achievement of the object is the same. Dying in efforts is like death in the separation from beloved, and death in actual meeting is like getting himself lost in the beloved just as the east and west get lost in each other. In the latter case there does not exist the lover nor the beloved. Both become one mingled into each other. Therefore, O graceful people! Have pity on the lovers as their end upon death is like entering into death itself. This is particularly so in respect of the lovers of God.

sections.heading: Persuasion to the Haughty Lord
paras: So, saying the people of the locality, told the Lord to pardon the monk by looking at his pain as misfortune his separation from God, so that God may also pardon you for your crimes and further make grants upon you after pardon of minor wrongs. [There is a hadith: have pity on the people of the world so that the One in the sky may have pity upon you]. They continued: “You have shattered many pots in your wreck lessness and engaged your heart in the hope of forgievance from God. Pardon him, so that you may get pardoned in recompense, so that God’s grace may open. Its authority to relieve you of pain”.
Be careful about the people who raise doubts in the matter of God’s authority and keep on narratives in mind. you may also hear the narrative of other Lord so as to get hundreds of information in it.

chapters.title: Oath for Taking Revenge
chapters.subtitle: Reply of the Lord to the intercessors of the monk, and asking as to why he committed that wrong by breaking his flask; and telling: I shall not accept any intercession as I have taken oath that I shall punish him

paras: In reply to the intercession of the neighbors the lord said: “who is that fellow to pelt a stone upon our flask and break it? Even when a lion passes through my street, it passes with utmost caution and in fear. Rather, it leaves off its paws out of my fear. Even a python becomes a lowly ant before my wrath. Such being the case, why did he cause sorrow to my slave’s heart and put me to shame before my guests? He flowed down that wine, which was better that his own blood, and now he runs away and keeps himself in hiding like women. But how can he escape and save his life from my hands, even if he flies high above in the air like birds. I shall hit the arrows of my wrath upon his feathers. I shall tear off his wings and feathers and kill him even if he goes away to the far-off ends of the desert. If he enters into water like a fish, water itself will rise high and go low, out of my fear. He cannot save his life from my sword even if he plays hundreds of tricks, treacheries and designs. Even if he penetrates into a hard rock to escape from my efforts. I shall drag him out of the rock. I shall make such hitting’s upon his body which will be warning for others. What all that treacherous fellow does is only a show the object of which his cheap popularity. He plays such tricks with others, and now he plays even with me! I shall reject him and do justice to him and also to a hundred like him. I shall give so much hitting’s upon his head with my mace that his life and soul will get out of his body.”
That lord’s blood-hungry wrath went out of control and fire spewed from his mouth.

chapters.title: Further Intercession
chapters.subtitle: Intercession of the neighbors for the second time with the Lord by flattering and kissing his feet

paras: Because of the lord’s great claims and challenges, the neighbors further entreated him by kissing his hands and feet and saying: O our lord! Taking revenge does not suit a person like you! Wine may go away from you; but you are fine without wine. Wine gets its wealth from your fineness; and water craves for your refinement. Be kingly and pardon him with a kingly grace. You are a lord, son of a lord, son of a lord. Every kind of wine is a slave of your great state. Your beautiful cheeks and your intoxication even without wine are such that all the intoxicated ones feel jealous of you. You are not in need of any rosy wine. You may keep the color of rose away as you are rose-colored yourself.

“O the one with the cheeks, bright like the mid-day sun! Redness of color stands like a beggar before you! Wine, that is with commotion in the pot, is in commotion due its enthusiasm to look at your face. You are like a ocean! Of what worth is the dew for you? You are life in entirety! Why do you search for the one who has no life, that monk has lost his worldly life? You are a full moon, and you have nothing to do with dust, and that monk is like dust. Your face is so bright that even the sun goes pale-faced before it. You are joyous beautiful and a mine of all joys and there is no need to be obliged to the wine for joys for you.

sections.heading: Man’s Greatness in Universe
paras: “The crown of honor is placed upon your head because of your status as man, as stated: we have honored the sons of Adam: wa laqad karramnaa banii Adama: (Asraa’: 17: 70) and also the grant of abundance around you as stated: to you have we granted the Fount of Abandance: Innaa a ‘tainaaka alkawth(s)ar: (kauth(s)ar: 108: 1). Though this Fount of Abundance is granted to the noble Prophet Muhammad only, which he got because of his attaining perfectness yet as a part of his perfectness, you also get a share of it proportional to your perfectness.

sections.heading: Man Created to Control Everything
paras: Man is the substance of everything, and all other things are only his accidents including the sky. All other things are only his parts, branches and shadows. Everything is from him, and he is the object and aim of everything. As the Quran says: he has created for you all things that are on earth: Khalaqa lakum maa fil ardhi jamii‘an: (Baqarah: 2: 29). Wisdom, actions and thoughts are your salves. Why do you lose heart and sell yourself at a low price? All existents are duty-bound to serve you, as you are the substance, and they are all your accidents. Substance cannot expect wages from the accidents who are his servants. You have to control all existents and not that you should be subordinate to them. But instead of seeking your knowledge and authority from within yourself, you seek the same from books. It is like enjoying sweets make out of husk. You are a drop in which is hidden the ocean of knowledge. The entire universe is wonderstruck at your body measuring three yards in length. What is the worth of wine, sex or music that you want to seek benefits and pleasure from? How can the sun be a borrower from a particle? Man is like the sun and everything in the universe is like a particle. How can the self-luminescent Venus seek light from a lump of fire? But what a tragedy? Soul deprived of its own sense of taste has imprisoned itself within the taste of other things; and the sun has entered into the constellation in which it has fallen into eclipse. Can there be a greater tragedy of man?

chapters.title: Further Arguments of the Lord
chapters.subtitle: The Lord’s reply to the intercessors

paras: The Lord countered: “No. No. I am not a lover of that wine what you are talking about. I am not contented with the taste of that wine. I am free of all kinds of fears and hopes. I swing around in all directions like the cane that swing with the blow of winds. I desire to swing like the jasmine plant at times in this way and at times in the other way. I swing like the cane on the right side as well as on the left, which has various styles of dances with the impacts of the wind.

Tell me my friends Lord can one be pleased with this wine when accustomed to drink the wine of the gnosis of God? Prophets of God who tasted this pleasure kept themselves away from all this, because they were amalgamated up with this pleasure of the gnosis of God. As their souls had seen that pleasure, these pleasures appeared funny to them. One for whom the real light appeared, cannot remain contented with darkness and smoke. One who eats the food: God the quench his hunger, cannot have a taste for bread and soup, as the prophet has said: Hunger is for the food of God which He provides to the truthful. One sleeping in a garden cannot be foolish to think of a furnace. One suffering from the sickness of chronic thirst cannot remain away from water. So also, a drunkard cannot remain away from wine. No man in love will remain satisfied without looking at the beloved, and no sick person can remain away from the physician. One in love with a living beloved cannot embrace a dead idol. Of course, he does take that idol in his bosom, which has no concern at all for the world.

chapters.title: Difference Between This and That World
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the Ayat: Verity the home in the hereafter — that is life indeed, it they but knew: Innsaddaaral aakhirata lahiyal haiwaan, laow kaanuu ya ‘lamuuna: (Ankaboot: 29: 64). Because, the doors, walls, and courtyards of that world, and its water, vessels, fruits and trees are all living, talking, and hearing as has been its seekers are dogs. Had there been no life in the other world, it would also have been called as a rotten dead body, as a dead body is called rotten for its foul smell and not for mere death

sections.heading: Needs: Different for the Different
paras: Every particle of that world has life and has the capacity to understand the depth of everything and speak about. It does not have peace in this dead world as it is just fodder worthy of none other than cattle. How can one be drinking in the company of friends in the one living in a gardens drink while sitting in a furnace? The place of the clean souls is highly elevated in paradise; and for every vicious soul it is a lowly dungeon. The place for the bulbul is the branch of flowers, and for the worms, it is dung. For, these appreciated by God are provided with clear and clear drinks and for the blind birds it is saltish water. One who has not seen the justice of H. ‘Umar, considering the murderer Hajjaj b. Yusuf as just. Lifeless dolls are given to young girls to play with as they are not aware of the games of the living persons. When children do not have strong arms of youths, it is better that they are provided with wooden swords. Infidels are contented with the pictures of prophets, which they keep well protected in the temples.
Greatness of the Prophet

That world is such a bright day for us that we are not in need of a shadows, images and pictures. One impression of the prophet is upon this world and another impression bright like moon is upon the heaven. His mouth speaks of many secrets in this world; and in that world he befriends God and engages in talks with Him.

His physical ear hears the narrations of the affairs of this world, but the ear of his soul absorbs the secrets of the command of “Be” (kun) of God. His visible eyes look and keep within themselves the shapes and profits of things but his inner eyes are capable of seeing the secrets and gets estranged at invisible sights which never turn away from the course as stated about the Prophet: His sight never swerved not did it go wrong: Ma zaaghal barsaru wa maataghaa: (Najm: 53: 17). His visible physical hand is engaged in receiving and giving, but the invisible is held at the door of the unique, everything. Never receiving God (Samad). His physical feet stand in prayer along with others in a rank, in the mosque but his spiritual, invisible feet circumambulate the heavens. You may consider every part of his body in similar way, that, it is one within the limits of time and space and the other beyond space and of time.

sections.heading: Leader of Two Directions of Prayers
paras: There are events and times of limited nature which come to end at death; and there is the time, which is a companion of the eternal, unbound everlasting God. Just as he has two parts, he has two names one is Protector of two kingdoms (Vulignd dawlatain) as leader of the two directions of prayers: (imamul Qiblatain): leader of two directions of prayer. That is: he led the prayers by facing toward Jerusalem the Jews and Christians did, and then toward Makka which his followers alone do. [while other communities prayed directly facing their idols and objects, Jews and Christians did so in the direction of Jerusalem, which also, the Prophet did earlier along with his followers. This was a special grand of God to these communities in comparison with others, that is, idol worshippers. But the Prophet was not satisfied with Jerusalem and looked upon God, and he was allowed to turn toward Makka, that is, Ka’aba, as a further grandeur gift to him and his followers. In the seeking and granting of this new direction these was a stress that these directions are for apparent worldly, unifying, specialization purposes. The following verses of the math(s)navi stress about the spiritual, esoteric matters — Translator]

sections.heading: Spiritual Meanings
paras: He reached such an elevated state, when seclusion and total lovely concentration were no more required for him. There was nothing that could overshadow his mental and spiritual state, as he was with God in every situation, which was a very special and unique state for him. The house of his loveliness was like the sun, which cannot be put behind any curtain of darkness. [the sun is ever shining. It never hides behind anything. It is always in appearance and brightness. There is no night and day for it. It gets hidden by the rotation of the earth resulting in dark night upon it so also upon other planets]. There was no sickness and deficiency for the Prophet then, and there was no need for any regimen. His earlier state of deviation from God, and earlier tribal infidelity in which he was born and brought up, got converted into faith and there was no scope for keeping those things with him. He became straight like the first alphabet (alif) of Arabic and Persian languages which is straight as against other alphabets which are in different curved shapes. This straightness took him into the count of God where he lost all his human, material qualities. He was completely rid of the formal apparels of social and community habits and customs and went toward the fresh, ever-increasing, spiritual grants. He discarded his tribal values and gods, ney, his own physical form, when he went before God without any apparent and external possessions, he was granted the dress of honor of absolute purity by the king. He put on this dress of the qualities of God and flew away from the lowly level of the bottom of the wells to the higher level of the palace. This is what happens when heavy solid particles settle down at the bottom of a vessel leaving the water above absolutely clean and clear.

sections.heading: Soul Released from Material Body
paras: In similar manner, the soul mixed up with the heavy solid particles of the body is in pain, with its admixture with the unfortunate contents of earth. It is living in an unsuitable company with its wings and feathers tied up with the companion, as otherwise its fundamental nature is very fast moving. When the command of ‘get down’: “Ihbitu” (Baqarah: 2: 36) was given to Adam as a punishment, he was hanged upside down in a well of the world as Haroot was hanged. This was because of H. Adam’s causing pollution to his soul by eating of the forbidden fruit.

It should be known that Haroot was certainly among the angels and was hanged upside down as a punishment in a well. He was left upside down as he went away from his high-level fundamental quality and went alone making himself alone leaving the company and quality of other angels. A basket though full of water floats on water, later separates itself from the river by going toward the riverbank. Therefore, with the impacts of waves it comes above the bank on the estuary and loses all the water it had. Then the sea takes pit, on it and floats it upon its head. In this manner, without efforts it enters into the merciful sea as though blessed by it. Similarly, when the soul gets rid of the connections of worldly attachments, it loses all its arrogance and pride, and then the mercy of God drags it towards itself. That is, mercy comes to it without efforts from the prosperous sea of God.

Therefore, return to the seashore of God, though those sitting on it are pale faced as searches of God due to their anxiety to meet Him. By remaining in their company, there are possibilities of yourself being graced with their anxiety, and your force later becoming red with the pleasures of meeting of the object.

sections.heading: Paleness of Face Due to Love
paras: Paleness is the best of the colors as it indicates the enthusiasm to meet the beloved object. This becomes red later after meeting the object, upon which it becomes completely contented and satisfied. Greed of seeing God makes the searchers pale and weak, but their paleness is not due to pain and sickness. When physicians, even of the level of Galen look at their pale faces, they get wonderstruck about the cause as they are not sick. Thus, when you establish your connection with the greed for the light of God, you become one who has disgraced and lowered the self, as the Prophet said: he has degraded his self: (Zallat nafsahu). That is a light that does not cause any shadow. It is very highly elevated and subtle, directly reaching him, and not the light that comes after passing through a sieve, which has light intermitted with darkness.

sections.heading: Spiritual Fasting for Whole Life
paras: Those in love deprive themselves of human weaknesses; that is, their real, potential manliness. They do not have anything bad with them to hide. But those without such manliness neither have such bodies nor are they in need of any covering. Their remaining covered or uncovered is the same. Bread and dishes are required for those who are fasting, to break their fast. A big fly has no concern for the stove and soup. Those in love with God clean themselves of the manly weaknesses and defects, as they have met their object. They are like the fasters who break their fast when the timing of fasting comes to end. They have a pleasure in breaking the fast. Lovers of God go on tasting till the time of breaking of fast which comes about only upon the sighting of God. Those engaged in the worldly affairs and in their search are like large flies which constantly lick everything that they get anywhere.

chapters.title: Continuing Change of Thoughts
chapters.subtitle: King’s asking Ayaz for the second time to explain the interpretations of his acts and eliminate the objections of the rejectors as it is not a manly act to leave to doubters in doubts.

paras: (Coming back to the narrative of Mahmood and Ayaz), the king said: “O Ayaz! The talks about the beloved, are much more than the limits and extents within which hone can normally talk, yet, you may proceed to say something about your affairs. You may speak about the affairs that come upon you, even though, I know, that it is impossible to say everything. Your affairs are like a new mine, from which very little had been taken out and much more is still in it. I also know that you cannot remain satisfied with what you have known about the affairs of the hidden world. yet, you may speak of some affairs which you may consider as worth revealing. Let those affairs be beyond the matters relating to five senses of man and the six dimensions of the apparent external world.”

sections.heading: Thoughts Always in Change
paras: Ayaz said: “though it is impossible to speak of the secrets of the hidden interior world, yet I shall speak a little of the odds and evens of that world in pure symbolic manner. It is required to be known initially that the hardship, defeats and bitterness’s come from the beloved in his search, yet they are better than sugar and sweets and more pleasurable for the soul. They are so sweet that if they fall into the ocean; its entire saltishness will become sweetness. Lakhs of such affairs come about and instantly pass off. They are not permanent and lasting. The come, put on impact and go back to the hidden world. the impacts of this day are not like those of yesterday. They are changing and different like the flowing water of the stream which continuingly shifts its place. It is not the same at the next moment. What exists at this moment does not remain in the same place at the next moment. Similar in the case of our thoughts. They are different on different passing days.

chapters.title: Body, a Guest House for Thoughts
chapters.subtitle: Man’s body is like a guest house and his thoughts are like the guests. And a patient gnostic in these thoughts is like a generous host like H. Ibrahim

paras: Know this young man! This body of ours is like a guesthouse in which, every morning a new gest comes. No! I am sorry! I said wrong! New thoughts come to man every moment. They are the guests of joys and sorrows! Therefore, you should also be like a new host to serve each of these guests like H. Ibrahim who was a very well-treating-host. You should be a pleasant host to welcome these guests with all pleasure. You should not shut the door. Keep it open and be attentive toward the way to welcome every new guest of thought. Whatever that comes into your heart from the hidden world is like your guest. So, keep it pleased! Yet you should not say that it has caught hold of you like a necklace that holds your neck around, as very soon it will fly back to the non-material world. where nothing exists.

chapters.title: Ill Treatment of Guest by Lapse
chapters.subtitle: Story of a guest and the wife of the host, who lamented when there was a heavy rain saying that the guest has held on to them

paras: A guest came to a person’s house at an inappropriate time. Yet the host embraced him and treated him well. He spread out his dining sheet and provided him with pleasing dishes. At that time there was a marriage function in their neighborhood. The husband told his wife in slow tone to spread to beds for the night. And spread his bed near the door and to spread a bed for the guest on the other side. The wife said: “I shall do as suggested with great pleasure. I heard your command, and I am obedient to it. O the brightener of my both eyes.” She spread both the beds and went out to attend to the marriage and spent much time there. Only the honorable guest and the host remained at home.

They kept dry fruits and sour snacks before them. They went on narrating about heir good and bad experiences up to midnight. Thereafter, the guest got tired of talks and stretched himself into the bed that was at the door and went into sleep. The husband hesitated out of regard for him to say that his bed was on the other side. What he had suggested to his wife to spread the bed for him near the door was upset and the guest slept on the bed meant for him. That night, there was such a heavy rain that they were frightened for the clouds.

The host’s wife came back and thinking that her husband was sleeping in the bed nearer to the door and the guest on the other side, undressed herself and entered into the blanket and kissed the guest mistaking him for her husband and told him: “what I was afraid of has happened. our guest will remain here for long because of the downpour and slush on the streets. He has become like a governmental taxation for you. How can he go back from our house in this rain and slush? He has become like a penalty upon your lead and life.”

Hearing this, the guest jumped up and said: “do not worry about this my lady! I have got boots and I am not worried about the slush. I am leaving you and say goodbye to you. May you be secure and safe! In any journey, there is no comfort and pleasure for the soul even for a moment. It is very good if a journeyman reaches his destination of achievements, as any joy becomes a dacoit in travelling.”

The women felt ashamed for her cold speech; but the guest felt unhappy and left. The woman told him very much: “I am sorry my Lord! I just said all that in fun. Please do not be displeased with what I said: “she entreated him and fell before him in humility, yet he did not respond and left leaving them in disappointment. The couple put on the blue clothes as was the habit of the people there to feel and express regret. They saw his face as a candle without candle holder.

But the guest left and was marching in the forest which became bright with his light like paradise totally away from any darkness of night. With these regrets, the host converted his house into a guest house to get rid of the pain and sorrow of this incident. The hearts of both the husband and wife were throughout engaged in the thought of the guest as though the guest telling them: “I was like a friend of deathless H. Khizr or Khizr (greenery) who had plenty of gifts for you. I spread them over for you. But you did not have any share in it.”

chapters.title: Service to the Guest of Thought
chapters.subtitle: Example of the thought that comes every day in the heart as of a new ill-tempered guest who enters first in the house and issues commands and misbehaves and the excellence of hospitality and rendering of service to the guest in humility Sultan Mahmood’s granting to Ayaz

sections.heading: New Thoughts Uproot of Thoughts
paras: Every moment a thought comes like an honorable guest into the heart and also on every day. Consider the thought as a living person, because only that man is capable of appreciating the worth of anything who takes it into account through his soul. If sorrowful thought spoils the paths of your pleasures, it also provides way for pleasures. It cleans the house of undesirable thoughts in a harsh manner and lays the foundation of fresh pleasures. It sheds the yellow decaying leaves from the tree so that fresh green leaves may sprout. It uproots the old cypress tree from its base so that a new tree may come about from the hidden world. sorrow drags out the old rotten roots so as to bring up afresh hidden root.

sections.heading: Sorrows Bring Pleasures
paras: Whatever, sorrow removes or puts into the heart, certainly brings about something better. This happens particularly in respect of those who have a faith that sorrow is a slave of those with firmness of mind. if you think that clouds and lightnings are harsh to bear, you should also think that without them, the grapevine facing the smiles of the sun would burn out. Prosperity and adversity are guests of your heart, which moe about from this place to that place like the planets that go from one constellation to another. Al the time when it is in your constellation, you should take it as the harbinger of your pleasures and smartness and be so like it, so that upon going close to the moon, it may speak of your thankfulness to God.

For seven years, H. Ayub (Jacob) with all his patience and willingness, was happy with pains taking them as guests to him sent by God, so that when this difficult-to-go-pains are taken back by Him, he might express hundreds of kinds of thanks. He was in love with the friend-killing-grains and did not turn his face from them even for a moment. With his sincerity and regard for the command of God who imposed these pains, he was like honey and milk in pains.

sections.heading: Welcome All Thoughts
paras: Thought comes into the heart fresh and new, and therefore, receive it laughingly and joyously; and pray to God saying: “O my creator, protect me from tis troubles. Do not keep me deprived of it but provide goodness from it. Put into my heart to be thankful to whatever I see, and not to grieve when it goes away.” And you should consider sour thoughts as sweet like sugar. Clouds appear to be sour, but they bring about gardens and eliminate saltishness. Consider sorrows as clouds and do not show a sour face to sourness. There are possibilities that there may be gems which may fall into your hands and try to see that they are in consonance with you. Even if they do not bring about gems and are not wealthy, you should try to increase the sweetness of your nature. This sweetness of your conduct may not be useful in that place, but there is a possibility of ti becoming useful to you in some other place, and one day surprisingly take you to meet your object.

The thought that prevents you form happiness is upon the order and wisdom of God. Do not consider it to be worthless. There are possibilities of it becoming a planet that falls into the constellation of Saturn and Jupiter. When they are together (about which it is believed that a conception and birth then provides great torture). Do not consider this thought as a branch ending at itself but consider it as a roof that brings about many branches, so that you may look at the final objective at all times without getting upset by temporary ups and downs. If you consider this thought as only a harmful branch, you will get disappointed, therefore, wait on to see the root.

You should know that a Sufi feels that there is great pleasure in the poison of waiting for good results. Whatever occurs to him is considered by him as on exponent of one or the other name of God. He will consider himself to be as inactive and unconcerned as a dead body leaving everything to God. He maintains this death like situation during his entire life time. Consider such altitude as a root for all good results and embrace it and hold on to it. In such a situation you will not think of death as something to come later which requires to be waited for.

The sultan said: “O Ayaz, the sincere, and follower of truth! Your truthfulness is greater than a mountain and ocean. You do not stumble at the excitement of sexual passions which would make a mountain like wisdom lowly like a scrap. Your patience, composure and self-control do not become dull and weak even in a situation of anger and hate. This is manliness and not the beard and genital, as otherwise the donkey’s genital is a leader of the leaders. God has spoken of men in the Quran as those not for the bodily development. There is no scope for body to play its role in this regard, as it is related to animal soul which all animals have. Manliness relates to human soul which is provided to man alone along with the animal soul. There is no value and worth of the animal soul, the loss of which results in bodily death. If you want to know about its worthlessness you may pass through the market of the butchers. Hundreds of heads of animals are placed upon their bellies whose worth is less than of a fat or thin tail. Therefore, as far as possible, do not be a slave of lust and of yourself pledged to it, as otherwise it will destroy the house of your body and throw you into the grave even before your death. An immodest woman gets excited at the vibration of the man’s organ upon which her wisdom becomes weak like a mouse and passions become strong like the lion.

chapters.title: Blindness of Excited Passions
chapters.subtitle: A father’s advice to his daughter to take care of herself, and not to conceive from her husband

paras: There was a gentleman with a daughter with Venus like cheeks, moon like face and silvery body. She attained puberty and he got her married to a husband who was lower in status than him. When watermelon ripens, it becomes full of juice; and if you do not cut it out, it rots and gets spoiled. As he was caught in a troublesome situation, he got his daughter married to one with lower status to avoid mischief. However, he told the daughter: “to protect herself from the son-in-law as far as possible and not be become pregnant with him. This was for the reason that getting married with that beggar was under difficulties. This mean fellow will not be sincere to you. He will abruptly run away from you leaving every one in lurch. The responsibility of taking care of the child would be entirely upon you. The daughter said: alright father! I shall do what you ordered me to do. Your advice is appealing to the heart and very worthy.” The father used to caution the girl every second and third day to protect herself. There have been such fellows also in the world who give such a kind of advice.

But the girl did become pregnant wit him, as both the husband and wife were youthful. She hid this fact from the father and the conception came over to five or six months and it became clear to the father. He asked her: “what is this? My instructions have flown away in the wind. My advice and convincing have been of no use.” She said: “Daddy! How could I prevent myself? Man and woman are like fire sparks and cotton. How could cotton protects itself from fire. Or where is care and caution in fire? Father said: “when had I told you not to go to him? I had told you only not be one to accept his semen. At the time of excitement, pleasure and ejaculation, it was required of you to pull up yourself.” The daughter said: “how could I know when the ejaculation would occur. This is totally hidden and very difficult to assess!” father said: “at that moment, eyes get stunned and become abnormal. You should have realized that it was the time of ejaculation.”
The daughter said: “by the time the situation of stunning and abnormality of eyes would come, my eyes would be blind because of the pleasure and excitement.”
Every lowly wisdom is not firm in greed and in the battlefield.

chapters.title: Minor Jihad and Major Jihad
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the quality of the weak-hearted, lazy Sufi who had lived in the shadow of comforts, not having undergone austerities, not tasted the pains and pangs of love, having received the kisses of the common people at his hand and honorable looks from them, their pointing fingers toward him to signified that he was the only Sufi of the time; and falling into treachery just as that teacher whom his student had falsely attributed sickness. (This narration has been explained in earlier pages). This speculation had made the Sufi think that he was a good fighter as the people thought. He went with other fighters to the apparent worldly fight, which is a lowly one, with apparent enemies thinking: “when I am already, a victor of the greater jihad against the self, well known and distinct in it, what worth does a small jihad have for me”. With the picture of himself as a lion with great might, he joined other fighters under the intoxication of bravery. He turned toward the forest before the lion and the lion told hm wit his body language: But Ney, you shall soon know (the reality). Again, you shall soon know: kallaa sawfa ta ‘lamuuna. Th(s)umma kallaa sawfa ta ‘lamuuna: (sura Takath(s)ur: 102: 3-4)

paras: A Sufi went with an army to the battlefield. Suddenly there was a battle cry and the battle started. The fighter ran their horses toward the battle formation and the Sufi was left with thin materials and other weak persons in the encampment. Those carrying the weight of the dust of the body remained stuck to their places and those foremost in faith were foremost: wal saabiquuna al saabiquun: (waaqi ‘a: 56: 10). After the battle they came back victorious becoming rich with the prize. They presented something out of it to the Sufi saying: “please take it”. He threw the gift out of tent and refused to take any. They asked him as to why he was angry. He said: I did not participate in fighting”. The Sufi was not happy with the generosity of the fighters as he was not in the battlefield using his dagger. They told him: “ we have brought some prisoners. You may take one of them to kill him. Cut off his head so that you may become one among the killers.” The Sufi felt a little pleasure initially but emboldened himself.

sections.heading: Coward Fear Even Looks
paras: Though there are many prosperities in the performance of wazu (ablution) with water; and when water is not available one can go for dry wash with clay. The Sufi took that hands-bound prisoner behind the tent to become one of the fighters by killing him. It took a long time for the Sufi to come after finishing the prisoner and the people wondered as toe what happened to him. The infidel prisoner with both hands is sure to be finished very easily. What is the reason for so much delay in killing him, one of them went forward to find out the reason and found the Sufi lying below infidel lying upon him, just as a male is upon the female? He was lying upon the Sufi like a lion. His hands are tied but he was chewing his throat with his teeth with utmost hate. The infidel was chewing the Sufi’s throat with his death and the Sufi lying down unconscious. The infidel with his hands tied was injuring his throat like the cat, without weapons. The Sufi was half dead, and his beard was full of blood flowing from his throat.

The situation face by the Sufi is like the situation that you have with your hand-tied-vicious-self. You are fallen down, and your vicious self is riding upon you. You are helpless before the sand dune of your vices and there are lakhs of mountains standing before you. When you died out of fear of a small mount, how can you pass through the narrow passages on the high mountains standing before you?

The fighters instantly killed the prisoner with the sword in anger. They sprinkled water and rose-water upon his face to bring him back to consciousness. Upon regaining consciousness, the Sufi saw his people and they asked him as to what had happened saying: May God protect you! What happened to you dear sir? What made you go unconscious in this manner? How your fell down unconscious in such a lowly manner before a half dead, hands-ted prisoner? He said: “when I attempted to cut off his head with all anger, that shameless fellow stared at me in a strange manner. His spread-out looks toward me, turning them around, were such that my body lost control of itself. The turning around of his eyes appeared to me like an army. I cannot explain to you how frightening they were. To say in a few words, his looks made me lose my consciousness and I instantly fell down. I would say in a few words that his ferocious eyes took away my consciousness felling me down.

chapters.title: A Coward Must Avoid Fighting
chapters.subtitle: Advice of the fighters to the sufi: with this heart and liver you have, you fell down unconscious with the stunning eyes of a hand-tied infidel, dropping, you dagger from your hand. Be warned a thousand times to sit in the khanqah’s kitchen and never go toward the battlefield to avoid being disgraced

sections.heading: Horrible Scenes of Battlefield
paras: The people said to the Sufi: the liver that you have do not even go to give battle and to fight. Be working within the kitchen of the khanqah so that you may not be put to shame before the soldiers. With the impact of the staring of a hand-tied prisoner, you sank down and your boat shattered to pieces. How can you swim in blood when you are not aware of the battles of the brave people, at a time when male lions are attacking, before whose swords, head are falling down like balls? Harsh shrieks of the cutting off of the necks are lowly like the splashing sounds of the washermen for the brave. Sharp swishing sounds of the life. Piercing-shot-down-arrows are such that clouds of the spring season feel ashamed upon comparison. How can you play in blood when you are not aware of the fights of the brave people? In the battle there are many torsos of the human body without heads quivering on the ground and many heads without bodies like bubbles in blood. Under the feet of the horses of the fighters in the battlefield are hundreds of murderous fellows. Suck into annihilation.

sections.heading: Strong Brave Hearts to Fight
paras: “How can your consciousness being one that flies away with the fear of a rat, hold the sword in the battlefield. This is fierce attacking with strong arms and not wine drinking, to drink which you fold your sleeves. This is not eating of wheat-broth. This is a place of playing of swords. A lion made of steel is needed in these ranks, and a brave man like H. Hamzah uncle of the Prophet. This is a field of swords and daggers and not of delicious dishes. It is not head alone that is to be staked here, but life itself: battling is not the job of every weak hearted, which vanishes like a doubtful thought upon finding reality. This is the job of the hardy Turks and not of their frail wives. The place of the frail wives is the home. You are like one like them. Better go back and sit at home like them. What more are we to tell you? You got out of control and fell down on the ground just upon the looks of the enemy.

chapters.title: Minor Jihad to Major Jihad
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of H. ‘Ayazi, may God’s mercy be upon him, who went into jihad for ninety times, who used to fight with bare chest with a desire to get martyred. When he lost hopes of martyrdom in this minor jihad, of fighting against enemies, he turned toward the major jihad of fighting against man’s dominating self and resorted to seclusion. Suddenly he heard the sound of the battle drums, when his self from inside started pressing him to join the fighters. He accused his self of pressing for battle for its own pleasure

sections.heading: Fight to Get Killed, Not to Kill
paras: “Ayazi said: I went into the battlefield bare-chested thinking that I might get an injury. I went before the arrow so that it might pierce thorough my chest. Getting hit by the arrow on the throat or any other part resulting in death is the share of the very fortunate or the martyr. There is no part of my body which has not been injured. My body has become like a sieve due to the piercing arrows. But they did not reach that part that would cause death. This can be the result of fortune only and not of bravery and smartness. When attaining martyrdom was not in my fate, I decided, and went fast into seclusion to perform austerities. It went from the minor jihaad of battlefield to the major jihaad against the vicious self. As a result of the austerities, I became very weak.

sections.heading: No Pleasures of Vicious
paras: In this situation, without expectation I heard the sound of battle drums, and an army of soldiers marched forward. My self-told me from inside, which I heard with my ears in the morning hours telling: “Get up! The time of Jihaad has arrived. Engage yourself in the fight and pledge yourself to it.” I told myself: “O vicious, dirty unfaithful fellow! Where are you from and from where is your inclination for Jihaad? Tell me the truth! What is the treacherous game you are playing! You are the source of all pleasures and pleasing situations. You are always away from worship and noble acts. Tell me the truth as to why you are advising me to go to fight, as otherwise, I shall make severe assault upon you and press you with greater austerities.” Then, my self-raised a voice from inside without a mouth, in a very clear and magical manner: “You drag me to this place (of austerities) every day and hit upon me like you hit upon the infidels. Nobody is aware of this pain of mine that you cause to me by depriving me of food and sleep. I can get out of the body and run away from you with one blow from the enemy in the battlefield resulting death and people will look at and appreciate my bravery and sacrifice.”

sections.heading: Temptations of the Self
paras: I told myself: “live life of a hypocrite and you want to die with that! What do you consider yourself to be? You are lowly, arrogant and ostentations. You are without sense in both the worlds. I have taken a firm decision that I shall never go out of seclusion, so long as there is life in my body. This is for the reason that whatever the body does in seclusion is not done to show to any man and woman. All his actions and rests in seclusion do not go beyond the intention to please none but God alone. This is a major jihaad and the other one is a minor Jihaad. Resorting to crush the enemy of the self without any exhibition to others, in seclusion has two jobs that can be done by very brave people, like H. Ali and Rustam. This is not the job of the fellow whose wisdom and consciousness fly away from the body merely upon the shaking of a rat’s tail. This madness and enthusiasm is not the job of one who loses his consciousness upon the movement of a rat and its tail. For such a person the proper place is to be away from the battlefield and spears, like women.

sections.heading: Pseudo Sufis: Pictures and Paintings
paras: “O sufi, you are one sufi who lost his conscious ness upon the looks of the idolators and that is that sufi like ‘Ayazi. There is a great regrettable difference. You are the one to bring disgrace to the sufis. You get killed with a needle and he considers the hitting of the sword as delicious food to live and thrive upon. You are only a picture of a sufi which has no life in it. Read sufi’s get a bad name because of pseudo-sufis like you. God has made hundreds of paintings of sufis upon two doors and walls of the bodies made of mud. So that with their magic, these paintings may move about, so long as the staff of H. Musa remains hidden. These paintings are swallowed by the truth of the staffs of the real sufis. And also, the eyes of Pharaoh which are full of dust and particles.

chapters.title: Death with More Wounds
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of another Mujahid and his bravery in the battlefield

paras: There is the narrative of another Sufi who came into the rank of fighters in the battlefield to fight for twenty times. He used to be with the Muslims at the time of attack and would not go with them in retreat. He would get injured and immediately dress the wound and be in the field and attack again. This was out of the fear that he should not die with one wound but with twenty wounds. He used to regret loss of his life with just one wound and in such an easy manner.

chapters.title: Both Inability and Fulfilment of Object Give Relief
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the Mujahid who from his purse used to throw one dirham into moat every day as a routine expenditure in order to fight against the greed and pleasure of his self; and the self’s asking him as to why you do not throw all dirhams on one occasion so that I might get relief from the pain of losing every thing once and for all, and possess nothing for later days, as it is said: both fulfillment of object and loss of hope provide relief from struggle. The Mujahid used to reply I shall not give you the relief of hopelessness

paras: A sufi had forty dirhams with him out of which he used to throw one dirham in the eater of the moat, so that his falsifying self may feel the pain everyday as slow and continuing pain is more troublesome like the pangs of slow death. His self-used to complain every night that it is getting weak in this continuing long drawn torture. It asked him: “why do you not throw all the dirhams at one go? You are continuingly killing me in torture and sorrow. For God’s sake, you may fulfil your object in one stroke and pay back your debts, as absence of hope provides as much relief as achievement of object provides.”

The Sufi world never hear this from the self and incline toward it, but would cause continuing suffering to it. In this manner the Sufi was in fight in the battle against the self and held it in his strong grip for the sake of God, just as the Sufi (earlier narrated) who used to be first in the rank while attacking and be the last while retreating. He used to get wounded, dress the wound and again attack. For twenty times spears and arrows struck and broke upon him. Thereafter he lost all strength and fell down, as a result of his sincerity and truthfulness of love in the abode of love: as referred to in the Quran: in an assembly of truth, in the presence of the sovereign omnipotent: “Fii maq ‘adi sidqin ‘inda maliikin muqtadirin (Qamar: 54: 55). O readers, proceed from this truthfulness toward forgiveness and garden of bliss and read in the Quran: Be foremost in seeking forgiveness from your Lord and a garden of bliss the width of which is as the width of heaven and earth: Saibiquu ilaa maghfiratin min rabbikum wa jannatin ‘ardhu haa ka ‘ardhi alsamaa ‘I wa al ‘ardh: (Hadid: 57: 21). And then be among the truthful as stated: among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant with God: minal muuminiina rijaalun sadaqu maa ‘aahadullaha ‘alaihi: (Ahzab: 33: 23).
To say in a nutshell, this death is the death of the sincere and truthful.

sections.heading: Bodily Death: No Martyrdom
paras: Buying in the path of God is not the death of the body, because his body is only a tool of the soul. There are many with only this body, who get their apparent bodies killed, but their living souls ran way in the opposite directions of object. This is like the loss of the weapons of the dacoit, leaving the dacoit alive or like a man in journey who killed his horse before reaching the destination. He remained imperfect and half done, totally unaware and far away from God. If everyone, who sheds his blood and dies is a shaheed (martyr), then the infidel who also dies in the battlefield is like the virtuous godly, (Abu sa’id). (Or like Abusa ‘iid abilkhair falling of the successful the great mysties: d: 1049 AD). Such of those who have crushed to death their own self are dead though moving about like living person in the world. [The noble Prophet said: if someone wants to see a dead man moving about in the world, he may look at Abur Bakr Siddiiq, who had completely crushed himself: Qazi Sajjad Husain].

sections.heading: Body Dies: Soul Lives with God
paras: Husain Self that was the dacoit of man died but the body is alive which is like the dacoit’s sword and is still enthusiastic to fight in the hands of the mujaahid. The sword is the same, but the holder of the sword is different. He has annihilated himself in God and now lives in God.

Such a man himself is a sword, and he is not a man. This statement and (situation) put you in amazement. It means that he is not as himself but as a sword, which is held by the hand of God and moves about in a manner as God moves, or that he becomes a tool of God. There is a man whose food is nothing but pain and yet there is another whose inside is totally empty like a ruined city with walls and houses but without humans.

chapters.title: Infatuation for a Beautiful Maid
chapters.subtitle: A reporter’s explanation of the beauty of a maid along with her painting on paper and present it to the calif of Egypt upon which he fell in love with her, and he dispatched commander of the army with soldiers toward Mosil to commit killings and plunder upon it to which the ruler the maid belonged

paras: A reporter told the calif of Egypt that the ruler of Mosil has a hoor-like maid. He keeps that beauty within his arms and there is none in the world a beautiful as her. It is not possible to explain her beauty in words. Her picture on this paper alone might be seen to realize it. That just king like the great kaiqabad, the Persian king, looked at the paper and lost control of himself and his cup fell down from his hand. He sent a brave general with a large army toward mosil to make a claim for that maid and say: “if you do not give that heavenly moon to me, to keep her by my side, I shall uproot your fort and the houses therein.” If he hands over that moon to you, give up all other things and bring that moon to me, so that I may hold that moon in my arms.”

The general went along with thousands of soldiers carrying flags and beating battle drums toward Mosil. They spread all over like locust around farms, around Mosil declaring their intention to kill all the people and plunder the city. All around the city, he erected large slingshots as large as the Caucasus Mountain to wage the battle and started shooting arrows and stones. Swords started shining in the dust like lightening’s. This, he kept up for a week resulting in the fort walls and bastions becoming soft like wax. When the king of Mosil saw those frightening attacks, he sent a messenger from the fort to the invading commander asking him: “what do you want to gain by shedding the blood of the faithful, who are dying in this battle. If you want to conquer the country and its capital, mosil, you can get it without any bloodshed. I shall get out of the city, and you may get inside so that blood of the suffering people may not catch you. If your aim is wealth, gold and gems, which are easier than this city to take. If you want gold and silver, I shall provide for you. What is this mischief and turmoil about?”

chapters.title: Invader’s Greed Satisfied
chapters.subtitle: Offer of the Maid by the ruler of Mosil to the Calif of Egypt to avoid further bloodshed of Muslims

paras: When the messenger came before the general, he gave the message of the king. The general said: “I am not after the country or wealth, but I am to get this beautiful person.” He showed the paper which contained her picture and markings and asked him to clearly show this to his king and to send her to me fast, so that your life and kingdom may be safe. Look well into this paper. I want her. Be warned, send her to me, as otherwise I shall dominate over you.”

The messenger returned to the king and explained all that was said and handed over to him the paper and showed the picture. Upon seeing this, the brave king said: “Accept the demand! What loss is there if a maid is no more with me. Take her to the general! I am not an idol worshipper in the days of faith. This idol of a women is better in the arms of that idol-worshipper.” He handed over many gifts and the maid to the messengers and he took her along with him and delivered to the general. Instantly upon seeing the maid, the general fell in love with her beauty.

sections.heading: Great Power of Love
paras: Love is an ocean and the sky above it is like its surf like Zulaikha who was a queen but fell in love with Yusuf who was her slave. Motions of the heavens may be considered as due to the waves of love. Had there been no love, the world would be cold and frigid. Minerals would not lodge themselves in plants, and plants and animals would not have developed in size by devoting their life to them. Soul would not have sacrificed itself to air, with a breeze of which, Maryam (Mary) became pregnant. Everything would have shrunk within itself as ice and would not have flowed and searched for food here and there like locusts. Every particle of everything in the universe is in the love of that beauty (of God) and moves fast to higher levels of success and achievements. Their fast swimming like motions are the praises of God which clean the matter (body) for the sake of energy (Life). Their praises are not by words but by fast, constant and continuous actions.

sections.heading: Love Makes One Mad
paras: When the general mistook the well as the way to pass through, unfertile, saltish land appeared to him very fertile, and he sowed his seed in it. This was like what a man sees unreal things and images in a dream during sleep. He sees a beautiful maiden in his dream and makes love with her resulting in the flow of this semen upon himself. When he wakes up from sleep, he does not see that doll anymore. He says to himself: “Alas! I flowed my liquid on a non-existing ant. How ridiculous, I got cheated by a cheat.” The general was a strong man but did not possess mannerism that he sowed the seeds of manliness in sand. The horse of his love broke up a hundred reins, and he declared: “I do not care for death, as there was a fear that the calif of Egypt might order for his death. What care can I have for the actions of the calif in comparison with my love. Both my existence and death are the same for me.”

sections.heading: All Fears Go Away in Love
paras: One should consult a wise man in a situation of such heat and burning. But where was the scope for consultation, when wisdom is overtaken by a flood of greed. He grew his own nails long enough to be able to cause his own death. There was a wall in front of him and also behind. Lover of the cheeks of the beloved does not look in front or back. Black flood of destruction has come over to take away his life just as the rabbit had felled the lion in the water and well. An image came out from the depth of the well and felled the lion in it. Do not allow any man to sit with a woman in seclusion as they are like sparks and cotton, just as the calif of Egypt did with his general. Fire should be kept cool with the water of the mercy of God just as H. Yusuf was kept under the protection of God from the tall, beautiful Zulaikha. He dragged himself from her like a strong lion. Passions of the self can be kept under control only with the support of those with perfect wisdom.
Now, let us go back to the narrative of that general as there is no end to this discussion.

chapters.title: Results of Togetherness
chapters.subtitle: Return journey of the general from Mosil to Egypt and his making love with the maid

paras: The general left Mosil for his place and camped in a plain patch of land in a forest. The fire of love was so ablaze in him that he could not find the difference between earth and heaven. He decided to go into the tent of that moon. He had lost his wisdom as well as the fear of the calif. When lust sets fire in the valley of heart, it sets fire to wisdom like setting fire to a heap of dry thorns destroying it. When lust beats its drum in this valley what is the worth of wisdom and dulled son of a dullard! Hundreds of kings turned into things of lesser worth than a housefly, before the fire spilling eyes of lust. He removed his trousers and that lustful worshipper of woman sat down between her legs. When he was about to pierce himself into her, there arose a doomsday like commotion from the camp. He got up and even without dressing himself, took the sword in his hand and ran toward the army lines. He saw a black lion having come from the forest and pouncing itself in the middle of the camp. Arabian horses panicked and started running helter-skelter in the camp after breaking their ropes from stables upsetting hundreds of tents in the camp. The lion was jumping high and low all around in the air to make itself free to move further feeling as though caught as a prison in a twenty yards width of a river.

The general was very brave and without any fear came before the lion, hit his sword upon its head and tore it off, and ran back toward the tent of that beauty. Inspite of the tension and struggle, his lust did not abate and when he exhibited himself before that houri, his maleness was as intact as before his engagement in the fight with lion. That sweet idol of the moon’s face fell into amazement at the sighting of this maleness. He jumped at her held her in his grip and joined himself with her and both became tow lives in one body.

sections.heading: Impacts of Togetherness
paras: At the time when two lives and bodies come together a new life comes into being from the hidden world, if there is no other force or sickness to prevent it. When man and woman come together, whether with love or hate, certainly a third one comes out. So also when two men or two women come together some new developments come about, which can be seen directly or indirectly after passage of time. Those with material shapes can be seen in this world itself, but those in the form of meaning and shapeless things appear I the other world. such of those result that originate from your company with others should be waited upon to see whether they are good or not. Conclusions should not be made immediately for their utility and goodness. You must wait till the promised time comes when you go to the next world, when all your actions are brought together and connected with you. All actions done by you and generated out of these actions as effects, get the tongue to speak out. They stand up with you to speak out or remain silent. Pleasing sounds will come from good actions and they will tell you: “come forward! Why do you hesitate! Souls of all men and women settled at the next world are waiting for you telling you why are you so slow. March fast and come to us!”
The general mistook false down with its dim light as true dawn and went forward but was lost on the way. He was like the housefly that fell down in a vessel containing buttermilk.

chapters.title: Seeing Mightier Than Hearing
chapters.subtitle: The general’s distress over his breach of trust and taking an oath from the maid, not to reveal of what happened to the Calif A narrative

paras: The general engaged himself in this manner for somedays and also felt ashamed of such a serious crime. He told the maid: “O bright moon! Make an oath and be careful to see that the calif does not become aware of all that happened. O bright faced one like the sun, give an oath not to give even a hint of what happened.”

To tell in few words, the general took the maid before that kind of the world. looking at her the calif lost his senses and fell down on the ground like something from the terrace along with his honor, authority, and self-respect. He found her a hundred times more beautiful that he and heard about. How can the actually seen be the same as heard about? Praising a thing is like making its picture for the eyes of consciousness. A face is the property of the eyes and is for them but not for the ears. To explain, I shall give an illustration and you may try to understand the meaning with all attention.

“O good explainer! A person asked a wiseman: please tell, what is true and what is untrue? The wise man kept his hand upon the ears and said: “this is untrue.” That is, what is heard is untrue. And he further said: “what is seen by the eyes is true and provides certainty.”

sections.heading: Impacts of Seeing, Hearing and Thinking
paras: What comes about as heard by ears is untrue and that seen by the eyes is true in a majority of cases in general parlance, but not always. If the bat keeps itself behind the curtain against the sun, the sun is behind the curtain for its eyes and not from the bat’s imagination. It remains always in its imagination which is also a kind of seeing. Its fear of light itself is a proof of the fact that its thought is well aware of the sun’s brightness. This thought and knowledge, drags it away from the sun. the thought of light is frightening to it making it attached to darkness. Your thoughts of the enemy provide a picture of the enemy making you to create friends for yourself and be with them. O Musa! You have seen the impact of the light falling on the mount. If did not have within it the capacity to realize the truth of light and to search beyond it just as you had. What the mount possessed can be considered as thought (impact) but not as reality.

sections.heading: Seeing, Hearing, Thinking Are Different
paras: This is to warn you that you should not be misled by thought alone. You should not remain attached to thought alone. Mere thought of anything does not lead you to the right path. Nobody goes panicky merely on the thought of a battle. There is no scope for bravery except in the battlefield. You should understand this well. In an imaginary battle, a coward thinks of many bold and grand acts of bravery like hundreds of Rustams, the great Persian fighter of yore. The picture of Rustam that is drawn of the walls of the public baths makes every incompetent fellow think of fighting with him. When imaginations made in the mind upon hearing of fights become similar to what is actually seen, what to talk of the coward, even a Rustam feels worried. Therefore, try to pass on what is heard about by the ears to the eyes to actually see that what is untrue becomes true by seeing. In such a case, your ears will get the higher quality of the eyes and become gems of greater value like the eyes. Rather, the entire body becomes a mirror, and your breast will become a combination of both the ears and the eyes and of the worth of a grant gem. Ear creates only a thought and becomes a go-between to take you toward beauty. Try to increase the thought so that it may lead you toward the reality just as it did in the case of Majnun that lead him toward Laila.

The calif also made a fool of himself and had fun with that maid for some days. You should consider the kingdom as the spatial territory between east and west. It does not last long and therefore consider it as short-lived like lightning in time. That kingship that does not last forever, should be considered as a dream which you see when in sleep. What can you do with this arrogance and self-pride which holds on to your throat like an executioner? Find out in this world itself that this is not a place of peace, and the next world only is the place of peace, which the hypocrite denies. Do not give ear to him.

chapters.title: Things Seen Other Than by Eyes
chapters.subtitle: Arguments of the rejecters of next life and explanation of the weakness of arguments
