paras: The hypocrite’s argument every time is that: “had there been such a thing I would have seen it.”

sections.heading: Different Persons See Differently
paras: Because a child cannot see the situations and possessions of wisdom, a wise man will not give up wisdom. Just because a wise man does not see the impacts of love on a lover. Beauty of H. Yusuf was not seen by the eyes of his brothers, but it did not go out of the heart of his father, H. Yaqub. H. Musa’s eyes saw his own staff as a stick of wood, but the eyes of the Copts saw it as a python and calamity. The inner eyes were in battle with the eyes located in the head. But the inner eyes dominated over the apparent, physical eyes and won, giving a proof of their existence. H. Musa’s eyes saw the palm of his hand only as a palm, but before the eyes of the hidden world, it was an apparent bright light.

There is no end to this talk. Every achievement of a successful man remains only as a thought for those deprived of it. When one takes the needy of the stomach and lust as the only truths, matters of secret nature should not be told to him. For men like us, whom needs of the stomach and sex are only secondary thoughts (not truths), our souls always demonstrate the inner beauty of things. One who considers the matters of sex and food only as the realities, guides and conduct in life, must be simply told as stated in the Quran: to you be your way and to me mine: Lakum diinukum w alia diini (Kafirun: 99: 6). This is what the Prophet was told by God to tell the rejectors.
Such being their rejection, better it is to lessen the talks. O Muhammad do not argue with the rejectors well committed to rejection since long.

chapters.title: When Petty Sounds Acts Like Thunder
chapters.subtitle: The Calif’s approach to the beautiful maid for sex

paras: The calif consolidated all his thoughts and thought of having sex with that maid and went to her. He thought and thought of her and erected his organ and decided to sleep and wake up with that love enhancing generosity. When he sat between her legs, fate also came in between and shut the door of his pleasure. Scratching sound of a rat entered into his ears, his organ went into sleep and his passions totally left him off. His ears imagined that lowly sound of the rat as the frightening hissing of the python, crawling fast underneath the bed.

chapters.title: Uncontrolled Laughter Reveals Secrets
chapters.subtitle: The maid’s laughing at the Calif’s weakness and the general’s strength; and the calif’s realization and suspicion of the cause of the maid’s laughter.

paras: The maid was astonished at the weakness of the calif and started laughing in a loud manner. She recalled to her mind the vigor of the general who killed a lion and yet his vigor stood at the same level. Her laughter overtook her senses and increased. She tried to shut her mouth but could not. She laughed uncontrollably like those under the impact of drugs. Her laughter took away her sense of good and bad results. The more she thought over, her laughter increased like the flow of water of the stream, upon sudden breach of the dam.

sections.heading: Cries and Laughs Controlled by God
paras: Crying’s and laughing’s, joys and sorrows of the heart may be considered as a lasting mine. Each of this is like a locked-up treasure the key of which is in the hand of God, as has been said: that is He who grants laughter and tears: wa anaahu huwa adh-haka wa abkaa: (Najm: 53: 43). Her laughter did not come to an end, and the calif got wild with wrath. He pulled out the sword from the scabbard and said: “O shameless one! Tell me about the secret behind your laughter. This laughter has created a suspicion in my heart. Tell me the truth. You cannot cheat me. If you cheat me by hiding the truth or bring forth before me slippery excuses, I shall yet know the truth as there is a light in my heart to show the truth. What is worth telling must be told to me. Consider the heart of the king possessor of a large moon in it, though at times with his carelessness it comes under the cloud. He is with a lamp in the heart even when he is walking and roaming about, which gets covered up by a trough at the time of anger and greed. At this moment that great quality of realization is in friendly terms with me and so you may tell the truth that is necessary to be told. If you do not, I shall fly off your head with the sword. Your pleading excuses and efforts to hide will not be of any use. I certainly going to kill”. So saying, he brought the sword close to her. Then he again proceeded: “if you tell me the truth, I swear upon God, that I shall set you free. I shall not commit breach of oath; and I shall please you with grants as well.” While taking this oath, he kept seven Qurans one upon the other and kept his hand upon them.

chapters.title: All Secrets Revealed by God
chapters.subtitle: The maid’s revealing of the secret before the calif out of the fear of the wounds of the sword, and upon the calif’s compulsion to tell the secret behind her laughter and due to fear of her death as warned by him

paras: When the woman felt herself humbled, she revealed the truth about the vigor, might and manliness of the general who had the vigour of hundred of Rustams. She explained to him in detail about all that happened in the tent on the way. She revealed to him of everything about his killing of the lion, entering into her tent with the erect posture of his organ like the horn of the rhinoceros, about there being no weakness in him due to the efforts against the lion and his vigour not getting reduced at this.

Then she continued: “As against this, you are so weak that you lost your sense upon the hearing of the scratching sound of a mouse. When I looked at you and thought of him, O king of the world, I could not control my laughter.”

sections.heading: Some Methods of God’s Revelation of Secrets
paras: God is the revealer of all secrets just as the revealing of the secrets of the seed. Therefore, be careful not to sow the seed of vices. Water, clouds, heat and the sun pull out the secrets of the soul. Spring season coming after the autumn making dead trees regain life, stands as evidence of the day of resurrection. Secrets of the soil of all that it has swallowed, are clearly exhibited in the spring season, through its lips and mouth, so much that all its plannings and capacities like hidden faith and conscience become fully revealed to one and all. Secrets of the roots of all plants and what all they ate, get exhibited upon their heads. All sorrows which sicken your heart are the intoxications of the different wines that you drank. But you cannot know as to from which wine you got a particular intoxication. The intoxication that has come from a particular wine becomes known to the wise, informed and smart.

sections.heading: Base and Product Do Not Resemble
paras: Branches of the trees and their shoots do not resemble the seed. So also, the sperm of man does not resemble man. Shape and form of anything, does not resemble the force and power that make it. Seed does not resemble the tree. Semen is a product of the bread, but it does not resemble bread. Man is made out of semen, but does he resemble it? Where does the jinn appear like fire even though it is born out of fire? Cloud comes out of vapor but does not resemble it. Jesus came into being wit a blow of the breath of Jibra ‘iil, but his shape is not that of the breath. Adam is made of clay, but he does not resemble it. So also, the grape does not resemble wine. Regular worship of God does not resemble paradise though paradise is its product. Theft does not have the shape of the place of punishment. Nothing appears as its product but be sure to know that every product is a result of something. So also, is the case of every headache and pain the cause of which is not known to you. These pains cannot come to you without there being a cause for them. Similarly, God does not cause trouble to anyone without any sin on his part. The essence and base of everything brings about the thing, even though these is no similarity between the essence and product.

sections.heading: All Reasons Cannot Be Known
paras: With all this explanation, you may conclude that any trouble for you is due to some wrong that you have committed; and the injury you got is due to some lust. If you can find out the reason for your pain you may repent for it and if you cannot find out, fall down before God, show your weakness and seek His pardon. Prostrate before Him a hundred times and say: “O the one beyond understanding and appreciation, this pain to me is for my own wrong. O Absolute, You are not the One to cause torture and pain to anyone. You do not give any pain and sorrow to the soul without commitment of some wrong! I cannot specifically identify the wrong that I have committed, but in order to seek your pardon, there has to be some wrong. But you have hidden the reason of my punishment as a mark of concern for me. Therefore, keep my wrong also in the hiding forever, as the punishment will appear to me as a recompense for my wrong and if my wrong is exposed it will add further to my pain, just as the punishment of the thief stands as a proof of this theft.”
Now, I shall revert to the repentance of the king so that, the secrets of his helplessness may become known.

chapters.title: Your Wrongs Fall upon You
chapters.subtitle: The King’s decision after coming to know of the misappropriation, to pardon and give over the maid to his general and his realization that the problem arose out of his own evil intention and cruelty shown toward the king of Mosir: as stated in the Quran: Whoever did wrong, it is upon him. Your Lord is ever watchful man assa’a fa ‘alaiha wa inna rabbaka labil mirsaad (Fajr: 89: 14). He feared that if he took revenge this revenge will recoil upon his own head just as this cruelty and greed fell upon him

paras: The Calif realized about his own fault and thought of his own crime, degradation and obstinacy. He said to himself: “whatever I have done for others became the punishment to my ownself. Because of my higher level. I though hill of the wives of others. This recoiled upon me and felled me into the well. I beat upon the door of another, and as a consequence he beat upon my door. Whoever thinks ill of the wife of another may be considered as one making others commit sins against his own wife. He is like a procurer for his own wife, as the recompense of his acts is the same as he does. The recompenses of wrong acts are wrong acts. The causes of your acts turn against you. Your thinking ill of another’s wife. Thus, you become a procurer for your own wife.

sections.heading: Repentance Before God
paras: I snatched away the maid of the king of Mosil and my general snatched away my maid. He was my a trustworthy servant and slave but he misappropriated my maid because of my misappropriation of the maid of the king of Mosil. This is as though I taught him to commit misappropriation. This is not a situation of ill-will and taking revenge. I have done the wrong with my own hand. If I take revenge of the general of my maid, that cruelty also will fall on my head. I have done the wrong once and got its reward. I have tasted once, and I shall not test again. The pain of the king of Mosil has broken my neck. I cannot break it again. God has warned us about the revenge of Bad with bad saying that if you repeat the wrong, we shall also repeat. Therefore, committing any excess in this matter is of no use. Nothing is better than patience and kindness. Now, the only solace left is to submit before God: O our God! We have wronged ourselves: Rabbanaa zhalamnaa anfusanaa: (A‘raaf: 7: 23). Do show mercy to us as your mercies are very many.

“I have pardoned them. You may also pardon me for my earlier sins and fresh wrongs.” Then, he said to the maid: “do not speak to others about your affair with the general which I have heard from you. Keep it with yourself and do not reveal to others of what you have told me. I shall get you married to the general. For God’s sake, so not speak of what happened between us, so that he may not feel ashamed before me, as he has done one wrong to me, but done thousands of good things for me. I have tested him on many occasions. I have kept in his charge many more beautiful ones than you, but I have found him perfectly honest. What has happened is a reward for my own misdeeds.”

chapters.title: A False Pretext
chapters.subtitle: The King’s grant of the maid to the general with a pretext

paras: Then, the calif called for the general before him and completely crushed within himself his anger and hate for hm. He made a very lovely pretext saying that he has developed a dislike for the maid for the reason that, out of jealousy and injury to her self-respect, the mother of my son is grumbling. Because of this annoyance, she is in constant distress. As the mother of my son, she has many rights upon me and she does not deserve to be put into such cruelty and harm. With the feelings of jealousy and loss of self-respect she is in too much of anxiety and feels extreme bitterness for this maid. Therefore, I have decided to give over the maid to someone else and I consider you to be the best person to be granted with, as you have shown great courage and bravery in taking her for me. Handing over her to anyone else other than you is not correct.”
So, saying the king got her married to the general and kept aside all hate and greed from himself. He said goodbye to her after marriage and shattered his wrath and greed into pieces.

chapters.title: Apportionment of Qualities
chapters.subtitle: To explain the meaning of: we have apportioned among them: Nahnu qasamnaa: (Zukhraf: 43: 32). That is one is given the strength and potentiality of the donkeys and another is given the wisdom and strength of the Prophets and angels. Turning aside of the head from sensual desires is leadership and giving them up is the vigour of Prophethood — Hakim Sanai. Fruits of seeds devoid of lust will not come other than on the doomsday —Hakim Sanai

paras: If the calif did not have the maleness of the donkey, there was in him the maleness of the prophets. Giving up greed, lust and wrath is possession of the nerve and maleness of prophethood. Though he did not have in him maleness of the donkey in his nerves. God called him as the lord of the lords. As such, if I am dead for myself, it is better that I am alive in God’s view and not rejected and kept away from Him. Consider this as the pulp of maleness which takes you into paradise, and the rest, as the rind which takes you into hell. This Hadith(s) has reached us which says that: paradise is kept surrounded with dislikable things and the hell with vicious desires of the self.

chapters.title: Tastes Are Different
chapters.subtitle: Address of Sultan Mahmud to Ayaz for the second time and conducting the test of other nobles of the court to exhibit Ayaz’s obedience to them

paras: The sultan said: “O Ayaz, you are a male lion and killer of the devil! You have less of donkey’s maleness and more of intelligence. What could not be understood by so many nobles was like a game of children for you. What a great maleness. You have seen the taste of obedience to my command to such an extent that you even sacrifice yourself in its obedience. O the one well aware of honoring by obedience to the king’s command, hear this narrative, so that you may become wiser. A narrative to explain the value and worth of the command and the taste of and pleasure of obedience, to understand their meaning.

chapters.title: Trial of Wisdom and Obedience
chapters.subtitle: The King’s placing in the hand of the minister a gem in the open court asking him to tell about its worth and the minister’s exaggerating its worth; and the king’s command to him to smash it. And the minister’s telling: how can I smash such a nice gem

paras: One day, Mahmud, the unconcerned about wealth, who was the great man and king of Ghagni, went to the office, and found all the officers and ministers there. He took a bright gem and kept it on the palm of a minister and asked him about it and its worth. The minister said: “it is more worthy than a hundred bags of gold carried by the donkeys.” He asked him to smash it, and the minister said: “How can I smash it. I am the well-wisher of your wealth and treasury! How can I feel it reasonable to destroy such a gem the worth of which cannot be fully assessed.” The Sultan said: ‘very Good” and offered him the dress of honour and further his mantle he had put on and took back the gem from him. Then, he kept him engaged in some other talks about old and fresh affairs. Thereafter, he gave it to his announcer to tell him for how much it could be purchased. He said: “this is worth the price of half your kingdom. May God protect it from destruction.” He asked him also to crush it, and he said: “O possessor of the sword of the sun! it is very regretful to smash it. Very regretful indeed! Do not look at its price; look at its brightness and brilliance that the light of the day has become subservient to it. How can my hand crush it. I am not an enemy of the king’s treasury”. The king passed order to increase his salary and gave a dress of honour and said words of appreciation for his wisdom.

After a little more time, he gave the gem into the hand of another noble to conduct the test. He also said the same which other nobles had said. He further did the same with other nobles and in the case of each next noble, he went on increasing the grants and dresses of honour and took all these lowly fellows from the normal path toward the well. In the same manner all the fifty-sixty nobles said following the words of the previous nobles. Though following the previous people is the pillar of the world in the normal course, but on the occasions of trial every follower gets disgraced.

Thus, the king tested all the nobles and gave them all plenty of dresses of honour and gifts. The gem thus rolled down from one hand to another and finally it came to the hand of the wise Ayaz. After keeping it on the palm of Ayaz, the king said: “O keenly observing friend! All of them have seen this gem. You may also see its brightness.”

chapters.title: Boon of Farsightedness
chapters.subtitle: Reaching of the gem from hand to hand and finally to hand of Ayaz, and his wisdom in not following the predecessors, and not falling into the trap of dresses of honour, other apparels, grants and appreciation of wisdom. It is not proper to take one as a muslim because of his blind followership. It is very rare that he would be well-settled in his faith. A blind follower is very rare to come out of the trials successfully as he would be far away from farsightedness and firmness of mind, possessing firmness of faith

paras: Then, the sultan said to Ayaz: “Tell me the value of this gem wit hits brightness and worth?” He said: “its worth is more than what all I can say.” The sultan told him to crush it to pieces. Ayaz had kept stones in his sleeve. He took them out and crushed the gem to pieces. This act was fully justified in his view.

sections.heading: Ultimate End Is Important
paras: It was the coming together of his good fortune and the occasion that a strange scheme had come to his hand, or it was that his bright heart had foreseen the occasion in the dream that he and kept too stones ready in his pocked to use for the purpose. This was like the case of Yusuf that, in the depth of the well he had seen the ultimate result of the event as revealed to him by God. For one whom, success and victory give their message, timely victory or defeat appear the same to him. Whoever is assured of the meeting of the beloved will not fear of any defeat in the battlefield. When he is confident that ultimately, he would defeat the enemy, he will consider the death of the horse and elephant as of no consequence. If the horse of one who is only after the horse is lost, he will consider the loss of horse as a forecast of defeat.

How can a man establish his relationship with the horse and consider it as everything? He loves his horse only to proceed forward to meet his object. Do not go with so much dependence on the images and means, and botheration about them, but go after the meanings.

sections.heading: Difference Between Pious and Gnostic
paras: A pious person bothers about the ultimate end as to what would happen to him on the doomsday. But the Gnostic is well aware of the end from the beginning itself and does not bother about the results and would-be-pains. He has this hope and fear in the beginning, but as he proceeds further. His foreknowledge and awareness chases away both these feelings of fear and hope. He knows what is to reap is the pulse which has been sowed. He knows about the crop as well as the place where the harvest is to be stored. He is a gnostic who is rid of fear and hope. The sword of God has cut them into two pieces. Earlier he had the hope and fear from God and later fear vanished and only hope remained intact. Fear rolled up itself and vanished and only hope remained as a solid body. It became so bright as to be totally covered by the sun.

Ayaz was well aware of the test that the king would conduct. He could not be misled by the king’s design behind the test. Dress of honour and further grants did not mislead him and so he crushed the gem upon the king’s order. Upon his crushing of the highly valuable gem, there was great uproar and commotion among the nobles saying: “what kind of dareness is this? This is a great rejection of a great grant of God that he smashed such a bright, brilliant gem.”

But this group did not think out of its ignorance and blindness, he smashed the gem at the command of the king. These people disobeyed the command of the king. They did not consider the worth of the gem of love and devotion. Such a question did not strike their mind that the king’s command is more valuable than the gem.

chapters.title: King’s Command More Valuable
chapters.subtitle: Condemnations of Ayaz by the nobles as to Why smashed the gem, and Ayaz’s reply to them

paras: Ayaz told them: “O great well-known leaders! Tell me whether the command of the king is more worthy or the gem? Please tell me for God’s sake, whether the command of the king is better before you or this precious gem! Your sight is on the gem but not on the king. The object of your worship is the ghoul (the forest dwelling devils who appear in the form of flowers of various colours) and not God of Ka’aba. Yours is not a straight path. I do not turn away my sight from the king. I do not turn my face toward the stone idol like an idolater. That lifeless gem that is like a coloured stone on the footpath, puts the king’s command on your back.

You should turn your back toward the colourful beautiful doll. Estrange your wisdom not in colour but in the provider of colour. Come into the stream and hit stone on the water pot. Set fire to colours and fragrances. If you are not like a dacoit in the path of faith. Do not worship apparent things like, women, who worship colour and fragrances. O senseless fellows: the king’s command is a gem and all of you openly smashed it.”

When Ayaz threw down these secrets in the open field, all the nobles fell into disgrace and bowed down their heads in shame and sought pardon with their hearts for the mistakes done by them. Form the heart of each one of them hundreds of sighs came out which reached up to the sky like smoke.

chapters.title: Forgieveance Is Better
chapters.subtitle: The King’s intention to till the nobles and Ayaz’s intercession and pleading for pardon before the throne — faineance is better

paras: The king ordered an experienced executioner to cleanse his court of these mean fellows saying: “these mean fellows are not worthy of remaining in my court who, for the sake of a stone, disobeyed my command. Our command was disgraced by these mischievous fellows and was ineffective for the sake of a colourful stone.”

At this the benevolent and love increasing Ayaz got up and ran before the throne of the great sultan. He fell down before him holding his own throat as a gesture of extreme sub-mission and said: O king, great like Qabaad, father of Anushervan the Just, before whom the sky smiles with wonder! You are the Huma, (bird whose shadow falling upon anyone makes him a king, as per popular belief), the cause of all prosperity and happiness, from whom all generous people learn the lessons of generosity! You are that beneficent one, around whose hidden signs, all benefactions move. You are that beautiful and nice looking that when the red lilac looked at you: it tore off its dress bloomed and beautified itself. All forgiveness gets pleased by looking at your forgiveness with which foxes dominate over the lions. Who can get any support of pardon other than from you which emboldens everyone to be fearless? The negligence and recklessness of these wrongful persons is because of the excessiveness of your forgiving greatness.

sections.heading: Forgetfulness Is Also Sin
paras: “Negligence always comes about due to recklessness. This is like pain in the eyes that puts an end to the regard to be shown appropriately. Negligence, forgetfulness and wrong lessons learnt, get burnt in the fire of respectfulness for the great Lord. His fear gives smartness and carefulness and chases out. Forgetfulness and dullness from the heart. At the time of a general loot by the enemy nobody gets any sleep fearing that his possessions and even his clothing’s of the destitute would be taken away. When sleep goes away with the fear of the poor-torn out clothing’s, how can there be sleep and forgetfulness when there is a fear of life? Making a supplication: “Our Lord! Do not condemn us if we forget: Rabbanaa laa tuwakhiznaa in nasiinaa: (Baqara: 2: 286) establishes the fact that forgetfulness is also a sin. This is because forgetfulness makes a forgetful fellow show deficiency in giving due respect to the one deserving respect. Had there been no forgetfulness, there would be no scope for troubles caused by it. Though forgetfulness appears on cursory considerations as something beyond one’s control but making efforts not to forget is in man’s authority and control. Failure to put efforts not to forget makes one liable for the wrong of forgetfulness.

sections.heading: Self-Imposed Intoxication Not Excusable
paras: It is upon one’s slackness in upholding the honour arises. It is the lack of attention of the mind that leads to the wrongful act of forgetfulness. This is like the commission of crime by an intoxicated person and his pleading that he was helpless because of his inability to differentiate between good and bad acts due to his lack of self-control. The judge will not accept his reasoning and say: “O vicious fellow, the loss of self-control was caused by your own wrong of drinking. Loss of self-control did not come to you, of its own, but you have invited it. Your control on yourself did not come to end, but you have chased it away.

sections.heading: Intoxication Caused by God’s Love
paras: Had you been intoxicated without your efforts, the Provider of the intoxication of the soul would have taken care of your decisions and actions. He would have been your physical protector as well as pardoner of your derelictions. I have great regard for such an intoxicated person, and I like be the slave of such a godly intoxicated pang of separation.”

Ayaz continued: “Pardoning’s by the entire world are just a particle before your pardoning. Every part of the pardoning isa reflection of your pardon. All pardoning’s praise your pardoning. Pardon their life and do not keep them away from yourself. These are the sweet means and objects of your successful life. Have pity on those who have seen your face. They cannot taste the bitterness of the distance and separation from you. You talk of keeping them away from you. You may do anything to them but do not separate them from you as there is nothing worse in the world than separation from the beloved. Keep this point about your lover intact in your mind. Lakhs of deaths are not as painful as one prick from you. So also, separation from you is not comparable to the strongest loop around the neck. Keep away the separation of the men from their wives and of wives from their men, which would be caused if they are killed. Keep the pains of the separations of them all and give relief to those wrongdoers. It is better to die in the hope of meeting with you as the bitterness of separation from you in more burning than fire. Even the infidel tells in the middle of hell: “if my beloved casts a look on me, I should not feel any sorrow in the hell.” This is because a good look sweetens sorrows just as the magicians of Pharaoh happily consented to get their hands cut off when they felt a generous look for H. Musa.”

chapters.title: How We Turn Toward God
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the statement of the Magicians of Pharaoh at the time of punishment: No matter! For us we shall but return to our Lord: Laa dhaira! Innaa ilaa rabbinaa munqalibuuna.: (Shu ‘raa: 26: 51)

paras: The declaration of ”laa dhaira” (no matter) was heard by the sky and it became like a ball for the bat of their declaration. They got involved with each other. They declared through this slogan: we are not affected by the cruelties of Pharaoh. God’s love in us has dominated upon the cruelties of others. O misguided fellow! If you blind-hearted had found out the hidden pleasure of our hearts, you would have freed us of this trouble. By your order to inflict pain upon us, you have actually done the opposite. Your freeing us would have been painful to us. Come close to us and hear the sweet tunes of the organ that is singing: “Ah me! Would that my people know.” Yaalaita qaqmii ya ‘lamuuna: (Yasiin: 36: 26). [when the people of Antioch killed Habib carpenter, a companion of Jesus (H. Isa), he had said: “Ah me, would that my people know that my lordless forgiven me and elevated me” — Qazi Sajjad Husain]. God’s grace has given us a kingdom like that of Pharaoh — but not that kingdom which is without God’s support. Raise your head and look at this everliving grand kingdom of ours. O proud of the country of Egypt and river Nile! If you also give up and throw away your torne royal apparel, you will also throw the river Nile in the Nile of your soul. O Pharaoh! Lift up your hands for mthe rule of Egypt and see that there are hundreds of Egypt and see that there are hundreds of Egypt’s in the Egypt of the soul

sections.heading: Difference Between Your ‘I’ and an ‘I’
paras: You say: “I am your Lord (Ana Rabb)” to the people, but you are not aware of the meanings of these two words — ‘I’ and ‘rabb’. How can a ‘lord (rabb)’ be frightened of those who are lorded upon? How can one aware of the meaning of ‘I’ be bounded by the body and soul? Look at us! Each one of us comprises of ‘I’, as we have all rid ourselves of our ‘I’, which ‘I’ was full of hardships and pains. Your ‘I’, you doggish fellow, is destructive and inauspicious but our ‘I’ is wealthy and prosperous for us. Had not your jealous and inimical ‘I’ been within you, we would not have been that fortunate as we are now. Your jealousy kills us which is our victory and prosperity. We are thankful that we are getting freed from this destructible world, and we are in a position to advice you from their cross. The cross to crucify is actually a vehicle for our journey; and your country is a country of arrogance and misguidance.

“This lasting life of ours is in the form of our death in this world. the life in this world is actually death hidden in a wrapping of life. It shows light as fire and fire as light, as otherwise, this world is nothing but a place of misrepresentation and misguidance, therefore, think over, be not fast; first of all, negate yourself. When you set yourself like sun in the west, you will show yourself as light in the east. There is a big difference between that ‘I’ and this ‘I’. that ‘I’ of yours is actually a narrowed down- heart from the beginning itself, whereas this ‘I’ is uncontrolled large life, in which the heart loses itself-control and gets wonderstruck. That ‘I’ is cold and narrow, but this ‘I’ is inebriated and turning pleasingly like the musical instrument.

sections.heading: Conflict Between Bodily ‘I’ and Spiritual ‘I’
paras: This ‘I’ of ours is ‘I’ is actually not ‘I’ at all. It is only to please ourselves that we have to call it so. This is rid of human qualities. It got enabled to jump out of that world. it became ‘I’ only upon getting rid of that ‘I’ of manly qualities. This ‘I’ has no tensions and worries of any kind. All praises are from this ‘I’. Man is running after destructible matters and his worldly ‘I’ is running along with him and trying to catch him. It is running as though it is not seeing the man at all and running on it own and for its own. It is his ‘I’ that is making him run here and there. You search for it, but it has no concern for you. And upon your death, your ‘I’ catches hold of you, and you become its object of choice. Take care! You are alive and you have to bathe yourself. It is only the dead who are given a bath by the bather. You are in search of your ‘I’ and what you are searching for, is not searching for you. The only means to end this searching is by merging your ‘I’ with God, the real object of search.
Not wisdom, but Taste clarifies

Wisdom cannot reach the proper conclusion in this search. Had wisdom been the proper guide in this matter, the great philosophers, Fakhruddin Razi would have been the knower of the secrets of faith. These are matters to be tasted to ascertain their truth; but as he did not taste them, his wisdom and thoughts became all the more estranged. This ‘I’ cannot become clear to anybody by thinking. This can become known only after its annihilation in God. Wisdoms have fallen down and lost in the pit of Hulul and I Itihad (translated generally as inherence and identification respectively). [getting annihilated in God has been understood by some as man getting inhered within himself the attributes of God in other words God has made man as his place and settled in him. This is Hulul. The other concept of Itihad (identification) means that there has occurred a unity of God and man or both are identified with each other. A detailed discussion on this is made earlier, with due references from H. Imam Ghazali’s al Maqsad al asna fii sharh asmaa’ Allah al husnaa” translated as “The Ninety-nine beautiful names of God” with notes by David B. Bursel and Nazih Daher Islamic text society, Cambridge 1995 — Translator]

sections.heading: Neither Hulul, nor Ittihad, but Annihilation
paras: This humble Ayaz has annihilated himself by nearness just as the star gets annihilated in the light of sun in which case both exist, but one is lost in another. The created man gets lost in the eternal Lord. This is a case of the change of the attributes or qualities. Then, there is also a case of the change of the essence in which, your semen gets converted into the body. In these cases, there is neither Hulul (inherence) nor Ittihad(identification), nor the confusions arising there from.
“Pardon them O generous king as pardoning is well kept in your box. Your kindness is ahead, and you are behind it.”

chapters.title: Intercession and Seeking Pardon Are Also Wrongs
chapters.subtitle: Ayaz’s considering himself as committer of the crime of intercession and seeking pardon for their mistake; and again committing a fresh crime by seeking pardon for himself; and further statement that even these wrongs occur because of the knowledge of the greatness of the king as stated by the Prophet about God: I know God better than you and I fear Him more than you (Hadith(s)) and god’s statement: Those truly fear God among His servants who have knowledge: Innamaa yakhshaltaa ha min ‘ibadihil ‘ulamaa’ u: (Fatir: 35: 28).

paras: Ayaz continued: “who am I to tell you to pardon them, O great king? You are the base of all commands! Who am I to present my own self before you, as you are the holder of the mantles of all existences. Who am I to seek mercy for those full of filth? I am only pointing toward the way for the knowledge of the penalty full of concern and softness. I am worthy of a lakh of slaps on my face, if you disgrace me with them. Who am I to stand before you and talk, or to remind you about your graceful attitude? What is it that is not in your knowledge? What is it that you do not remember as to from where it is in the world? you are totally clean of any lack of knowledge, and knowledge becomes cleansed because of you! How then can there be any forgetfulness? You have made a worthless fellow worthy of interceding for others. You have brightened him like the sun.

sections.heading: No Intercession but by You Alone
paras: “When you have made me something, further, to hear some flattery full of humility from me. In fact, you have taken me out of my own self and therefore, the intercession that I am making is actually your own. I do not have any possession of my own within myself, and everything is your own, so also this intercession. when my house has been emptied of everything, the dryness and wetness of this house is also not mine. When you alone have made this prayer flow from me like water, you alone may stop it from further flowing, and accept it. You alone are the one to make me pray and you alone are the one to accept the prayer. This has been done by the king of the world so that I may praise myself in this way so that he may pardon those wrong doers for the sake of this slave.

sections.heading: Grace Is Like Kauth(s)ar
paras: “I was a self-lover and pain in entirety, but the king made me a medicine for all pains. I was a hell full of turmoil and fire but the king with his grace made me into the stream of kauth(s)ar, which gives relief to the victims of burns. Whoever was burnt out in the hell as punishment, was provided with a new body by me as kauth(s)ar, what else is the job of kouth(s)ar? It is to make him develop once again and get re-organized. Every drop of kauth(s)ar makes a declaration of generosity saying, whatever has been burnt down by hell will be provided to you by me. Like ointment on a rotten wound, I bring about fresh flesh again. Hell is like the autumn and winter and kauth(s)ar is like spring and garden.

sections.heading: God Creator of Hell and Kauth(s)ar
paras: Hell is like death and destruction, and kauth(s)ar is like the sound of the trumpet of suur from God which raises the dead to life. Hell is like death and mud of the grave, and kauth(s)ar is upon the type of the blow of suur. Those whose bodies are burnt down by hellfire may come toward kauth(s)ar as God calls you toward it. Because, as a Qudsi Hadith(s) says: “I created the creatures so that they may get benefit from Me.” This is how the Ever living Self-existing-God has blessed us. This is not that He would get any benefit from the creatures. this is His grant to us, so that the deficient may become perfect.

sections.heading: Seeking God’s Pardon
paras: “Pardon these deficient fellows as pardon from the river of pardoning is of higher grade. Pardoning the people is like a river and its flow, and it runs its horse toward itself. Pardon’s the broken-hearted-people goes toward Your kingly Presence like pigeons flying toward You in the evenings. Then You make them fly off in the morning till the night, when you imprison their bodies so that they may rest. Again, in the evening, they fly upon your palace and terraces out of their love for You. This goes on for their whole life, when upon the breaking of the joints of their life, they finally come back to You, as everything has the finally return to You. Their beating of their wings is not turned against their faces like those of the sinners and infidels. It is a clear flight as per Your saying: To God we belong and to Him is our return: Inna lillahi wa inna ilaihi raaji ‘uuna: (Baqarah: 2: 156). From Your generosity comes the sound: ‘come on’ (Ta ‘aalaow). And after return, there is no more sorrow and pain.

This is like what God’s grace tells: “You have suffered a lot in many strange journeys in the world. by this you have understood My worth and value Now, you may spread your tired legs under the shadow of the tree of my graces and take rest. Spread your legs fully, comfortably as they are very much tired in traversing the paths of faith. You may spread them so that they may be in the hands and laps of the hears. These coquettish hears are very benevolent upon the sufis who have returned after a long journey. Such clean and clear sufis like the light of the sun who were mingled with mud and dirt of the world for a long time. They have now returned without any dirt attached to them like the light of the sun going higher up toward many other tablets of suns. Still higher in place than this sun comforts to the sufis at the hands of hoors is symbolic. Sufis who xx xxx their bodies through austerities in the world itself need no physical comforts in the next world. signifies the ideas of purity, beauty and truth and good will (Abdulla Yusuf page 1352 Holy Quran) further explanation on page 1407: casual sex has of course no place in heaven, but sex in our constitution here has a neutral psychological value, which we can picture in over transformed and perfect love alone. The word Hoors in some passages as 44: 54 and 52: 70 has been much misunderstood and misrepresented grammatically. It is not feminine in form, and the companionship of Hoors will be in heaven for men and women (as they were in this life) who will retain their personality, but not their carnal attributes — ibid pages (1467-68) — Translator]

sections.heading: Ranks of Worshipper
paras: O great one! “You may see the group of the sinners standing with their faces toward the wall out of shame. They became fully aware of their sins and wrongs now, even though they were defeated in the game of dice by you as a master player. With sighs cries they turn toward you saying: “O the one whose graces are the guides to show way to the wrong doers! Give the way to the polluted ones, so that they may wash their sins in the streams and the fountain in which H. Ayub had bathed after his long illness and regained full health. So that, they may bathe and cleanse themselves of the dirt of their long-drawn sins and enter into the ranks of those already engaged in prayers. These are the ranks in which there are more worshippers than imagined, who are sunk in the light in which the angels say: and we are verily ranged in ranks: wa inna lanahnu al saafiiunaa: (Saaffaat: 37: 165). When the pen reached this stage of explanation, it broke, and the paper tore off. Who has measured the ocean with a cup? Has a lamb even lifted a lion? If you can see the mysteries, come out of the curtains so that you may see the kingdom full of wonders.

sections.heading: Intoxication of Love
paras: Ayaz continued: “Even if these intoxicated people have broken up your cup, they required to be pardoned because they are intoxicated of your love. Are they not intoxicated with the prosperity and wealth given by you? Is not this the intoxication of your sweet contributions? O king, they are intoxicated of the special grants of yours. Therefore, O granter of mercy! Pardon the one’s intoxicated by you. The taste of the special treatment of your addressing them intoxicates them so much which even a hundred vessels of wine do not. When you have intoxicated me, do not impose the penalty of intoxication caused by wine, as law does not provide penalty to the intoxicated, so long as they are in it. You may impose punishment after I come back to my normal senses. But even this you cannot do because I shall never regain my senses, because this is not an intoxication of wine but of your love. O benefactor, whoever has drunk the wine of your love, remains away from senses and always escapes the imposition of penalty. He remains always in the annihilation of intoxication. One who is annihilated in your love is never capable of standing on his legs. Your grace tells our hearts to go away, even though we have pledged ourselves to buttermilk and not wine yet pretending to be intoxicated. Yet you accept our pretention as if you have intoxicated us with the buttermilk of your love. You tell us: Like the fly that has fallen in buttermilk, you are not intoxicated; yet a fly with your pretended intoxication can intoxicate the large bodies of the vultures, who you run your horse upon the ocean of honey. This is the impact even pretended love of yours. Mountains will become particles with your intoxication. Points, lines and circles, and resultant shapes are all in your hands. Mischiefs of the world before whom everyone shivers, shiver before you. All precious gems become worthless before you.”

Ayaz continued: “I can fully explain about you, that you are the soul of the worldly if God gives me five hundred months. But I have only one tongue and even that is incapable, and therefore I cannot explain about you. I feel ashamed for that. However, as the knower of all hidden things, you are aware of my disabilities. Yet with all my disabilities, I have to speak out as I am not a non-existent in the world of non-existent (‘dam) from where have come the mouths of all humans. [‘Adam is a world of non-existents. It is empty. Yet all existents come out of it]. There are lakhs of hidden symbols which are waiting to come out of ‘Adam with all their abilities, goodness and benevolence calling for your graces.

sections.heading: Water of Life, of Death, of Love
paras: It is with You grace only that my head moves, and I am dead before that generosity. It is only upon this, that I explain all this. Our desire to praise you is only your gift and upon your demand and persuasion. How can dust go up without being dragged by wind? How can a boat step in and sail without an ocean? One who has tasted the water of life never dies, and yet, the worth of this water of life is just a spill over water. Those who love to live have a love for the water of life. Gardens laugh and go green with water of life. as against this those who drink the water of annihilation in Him live with His love, and their hearts are disgusted with life and the eater of life. When the water of Your love reached our hand, water of life becomes use life for us. Every life gets refreshment with the water of life. Every moment you give death and new life to me which made me see your domination upon pleasures of life and death.

O God, death has become like sleep for me on the hope of getting up again. This has made me confident of resurrection after death. Even if the seven oceans become sand and mirage, every moment, you can pull them up and make them water again. Wisdom is afraid of death, but love laughs at it. This is like the rock which has no fear of rain as against a lump of mud has.

sections.heading: Verses of Math(s)navi Are Constellations and Stars
paras: From among the volumes of the Math(s)navi, this is the fifth one. This is a life, like the stars in the constellations of heavens. Every man cannot find the path by looking at the stars, but only the sailors who are well aware of their identifications and location. The fortune of others is only in looking at their beautiful sceneries. They are not fortunate to know of their prosperous effects in individual and combined forms. Be friendly with the days and nights and be watchful to look at the stars that set fire to the devils. Keep yourself in touch with this masnavi to get similar benefit. Every verse of it is like a star which is capable of chasing the devil of evil suspicions which throw burning naphtha from the forts of the heaven.

sections.heading: Stars and Constellations of Math(s)navi
paras: A star like a scorpion, is for an attack on devil; and there is Jupiter which is very friendly for those who go for buying Sagittarius as a blow shouts and pierces at the devil with arrows. Aquarians pours water from above and fills the farms and fruits with water. Pixes, as fish crushes the misguided ships, and Taurus is like the ox for the farmer to phough. Sun tears off the night like Leo (Lion) and provides and colourful and dresses to the ruby. Cancer, moves sideways, the shape of Libra is different. Though blood spilling and fighting is the profession of Mars, yet it is sub ordinated by the bright sun. Though Saturn is proved to be inauspicious, but it creates depthness in thinking while carrying on professions. When my moon claps with her palms, Venus the dancer of heaven dares not challenge her; and Mercury loses its own location and tears up and separates Gemini. Hands of Jupiter tremble and its hearts feels uneasy when my moon falls upon the surface of water like a basket. Vulture sheds down its feathers out of shame, and python, out of its greed, of turns soft like wax. Seven daughters of Atlas of the Pleiad become pregnant, get up and clap together.

Now you may stop further talk about this, as the galaxy is full with the stalks and ears of wheat. The explanations in the math(s)navi have become so many that even understanding of the plain narratives has become difficult. [stars and constellations are taken here as different good or bad as you take impacts that the Math(s)navi can have a people]

Take into account that the sun ahs come out from behind the mountain. Everything is quite clear and plain, but you find this to be quite bitter and difficult to grasp. You are inimical in feelings and therefore, even milk and honey straight away become poison in your body. This poisoning is not a result of this math(s)navi alone and this is the case with all other things. Every creation that came of the world of non-existence (‘dam) and raised its head has two versions: one dull of sugar and another full of poison. Become a clean hearted friend and give up vicious thoughts, so that you may eat sugar from a vessel of poison, as his sense and practice of justice were an antidote for poison. Therefore, o slavish victim of your own vices, search for the antidote of Faruq, so that you may become Faruq of the time. May God bless you.
Stars and constellations.
